items.title: CVE-2026-102950: The mount-time recovery scan of the Zephyr Memory Storage (ZMS) key-value store, zms_recover_last_ate() in subsys/kvss/zms/zms.c (subsys/fs/zms/zms.c in older releases), computes t
items.summary: The mount-time recovery scan of the Zephyr Memory Storage (ZMS) key-value store, zms_recover_last_ate() in subsys/kvss/zms/zms.c (subsys/fs/zms/zms.c in older releases), computes the end of the sector's data area incorrectly. Every valid allocation table entry (ATE) reset the data-end bound to the start of the sector, including entries whose value is stored inline (8 bytes or less) and delete entries. When the newest ATE in the active sector is one of these, the scan continues past the ATE area into the payload area and reads stored value bytes as struct zms_ate records. Any payload slot that passes the ATE check (a CRC8 plus the one-byte sector cycle count) is adopted as the newest entry. zms_init() then sets fs->ate_wra and fs->data_wra from it. The pointers are only this weak check away from data an application may have stored on behalf of a remote party: a BLE-writable device name, provisioned credentials, or configuration received over the network. An attacker who can get about 16 bytes of chosen content persisted in a ZMS value can plant a forged ATE. The forged entry takes effect after the next mount, provided the newest entry in that sector is small or a delete. Random data

items.title: CVE-2026-102951: The Intel SoC FPGA Agilex5 SoC's static MMU region table in soc/intel/intel_socfpga/agilex5/mmu_regions.c mapped the System Manager peripheral (sysmgr) with MT_P_RW_U_RW. That sets
items.summary: The Intel SoC FPGA Agilex5 SoC's static MMU region table in soc/intel/intel_socfpga/agilex5/mmu_regions.c mapped the System Manager peripheral (sysmgr) with MT_P_RW_U_RW. That sets the EL0 access-permission bit in the page-table descriptor, so user mode can read and write the block. The other peripheral windows in the same table, and the same block on the sibling Agilex SoC, are correctly mapped MT_P_RW_U_NA. On arm64, memory-domain page tables are cloned from the kernel page tables (arch_mem_domain_init()). When CONFIG_USERSPACE is enabled, every user mode thread therefore gets direct load/store access to the System Manager registers, with no partition grant or system call. Any untrusted code running as a user thread can exploit this. The System Manager controls system-wide state that only the kernel should own: NoC/FPGA-bridge idle requests, SDMMC and EMAC interface configuration, FPGA interface enables and boot scratch registers. A user thread can stall the interconnect or reconfigure peripherals out from under kernel drivers, causing denial of service and integrity loss for the platform, and can read that configuration. This breaks the userspace isolation boundary. Builds witho

items.title: CVE-2026-102952: The Zephyr TFTP client in subsys/net/lib/tftp/tftp_client.c does not check where the reply to its request comes from. After sending a read or write request to the configured server
items.summary: The Zephyr TFTP client in subsys/net/lib/tftp/tftp_client.c does not check where the reply to its request comes from. After sending a read or write request to the configured server, send_request() accepts the first UDP datagram that arrives on the client's socket from any address and port. It then calls zsock_connect() to that sender, so the sender becomes the peer for the rest of the transfer. RFC 1350 requires a client to discard datagrams whose source does not match the transfer ID it expects. A host that can send a UDP datagram to the client's ephemeral port before the real server replies can take over the transfer. It can reply from its own address and does not need to spoof the server. A host on the same network segment that sees the request can do this easily. An off-path attacker must guess the randomized ephemeral port and win the race, which is easier when the server is slow or unreachable. No authentication or user interaction is needed beyond the device starting a transfer through tftp_get() or tftp_put(), for example from an application or the net tftp shell command. items.title: CVE-2026-102953: usbh_req_setup() in subsys/usb/host/usbh_ch9.c returns -ETIMEDOUT as soon as a control request times out, even though the transfer is still in flight. usbh_xfer_dequeue() only requ
items.summary: usbh_req_setup() in subsys/usb/host/usbh_ch9.c returns -ETIMEDOUT as soon as a control request times out, even though the transfer is still in flight. usbh_xfer_dequeue() only requests cancellation, and the host controller driver keeps the transfer and its data buffer until it returns it through the completion callback. Callers such as usbh_req_desc_dev() and usbh_req_desc_cfg() free the buffer (net_buf_unref()) right after usbh_req_setup() returns. Separately, a single global semaphore (ch9_req_sync) with no mutual exclusion lets a late or foreign completion wake the wrong waiter. That waiter then returns early and its caller frees a buffer the controller is still filling. A malicious USB device attached to a Zephyr USB host port can trigger this during enumeration. It NAKs a GET_DESCRIPTOR request until the 5-second timeout expires, then answers with data around the cancellation, or delays its answer to the next request after leaving a stale semaphore signal. The controller driver (for example the MAX3421E max3421e_hrslt_success() path) then writes device-controlled bytes into the freed net_buf and updates its length. The result is a use-after-free write into the USB host buffer

items.title: CVE-2026-102954: The STM32 SMBus driver (drivers/smbus/smbus_stm32.c) implements smbus_block_read() and smbus_block_pcall() by issuing a single i2c_transfer() in which the byte-count byte returned
items.summary: The STM32 SMBus driver (drivers/smbus/smbus_stm32.c) implements smbus_block_read() and smbus_block_pcall() by issuing a single i2c_transfer() in which the byte-count byte returned by the peripheral is read directly into the len field of the following i2c_msg. That message then receives data straight into the caller-supplied buffer. Nothing bounds the count, so smbus_stm32_block_read() and smbus_stm32_block_pcall() read up to 255 bytes into a buffer that the SMBus API documents (and the syscall verifiers validate) as holding at most SMBUS_BLOCK_BYTES_MAX (32) bytes. The count is chosen by the addressed SMBus peripheral. A malicious, counterfeit or faulty device on the bus (for example a removable smart battery, PMBus supply or plug-in module), or anyone able to drive the bus lines, can report a block count above 32 and cause the driver to write up to 223 bytes past the end of the caller's buffer. Callers typically pass a 32-byte stack buffer, as the in-tree smbus block_read shell command does, so the overflow lands on the caller's stack before any caller-side count check can run. The result is attacker-controlled stack or memory corruption in the context of the calling thread, which

items.title: CVE-2026-102955: The OpenThread PSA crypto platform backend in modules/openthread/platform/crypto_psa.c only supported PSA key references. otPlatCryptoAesSetKey() copied aKey->mKeyRef into the AES
items.summary: The OpenThread PSA crypto platform backend in modules/openthread/platform/crypto_psa.c only supported PSA key references. otPlatCryptoAesSetKey() copied aKey->mKeyRef into the AES context unconditionally. On an OpenThread Radio Co-Processor (RCP) build, CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_CRYPTO_PSA does not select CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_PLATFORM_KEY_REF, so OpenThread passes the MAC key as literal bytes and mKeyRef is uninitialized. psa_cipher_encrypt() in otPlatCryptoAesEncrypt() then fails without writing its output, and the error is only caught by an OpenThread assertion that is compiled to a no-op when CONFIG_ASSERT is disabled. When the RCP handles transmit security in software, AES-CCM* is never keyed. That is the case with Thread 1.2 or later, where CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_MAC_SOFTWARE_TX_SECURITY_ENABLE defaults to y, on a radio driver without IEEE802154_HW_TX_SEC. Every MAC key-id-mode-1 frame goes out with its payload XORed against a single 16-byte pad of stale stack data, reused for every block, and with an unkeyed MIC. items.title: CVE-2026-102956: ethernet_send() in subsys/net/l2/ethernet/ethernet.c dropped the caller's reference on an IPv4 packet whenever net_arp_prepare() returned NET_ARP_PKT_REPLACED. That return value is
items.summary: ethernet_send() in subsys/net/l2/ethernet/ethernet.c dropped the caller's reference on an IPv4 packet whenever net_arp_prepare() returned NET_ARP_PKT_REPLACED. That return value is also used when ARP could not queue the packet because every ARP cache entry is already pending. In that case ARP holds no reference of its own, so the original packet was freed before the replacing ARP request was transmitted. If transmitting the ARP request then failed (a driver send error or an ethernet_fill_header() failure), the error path called net_pkt_ref() on the freed packet. net_if_tx() then called net_pkt_unref() on it again. If the freed net_pkt slab slot was reallocated in between, the stray unref releases a reference owned by an unrelated packet, which is freed while still in use. An attacker on the local link can drive the ARP cache into the all-pending state. CONFIG_NET_ARP_TABLE_SIZE defaults to 2, so it is enough to elicit replies to a few spoofed, non-responding on-subnet addresses. Reaching the memory corruption also needs a transmit failure the attacker does not directly control and a narrow slab-reuse race. items.summary: The system call verification handlers for smbus_block_read() and smbus_block_pcall() in drivers/smbus/smbus_handlers.c (z_vrfy_smbus_block_read() and z_vrfy_smbus_block_pcall()) validated the device object, the count pointers and (for process call) the send buffer, but never validated the receive buffer (buf / rcv_buf). The call then proceeds into the driver implementation, which runs in supervisor mode and writes the bytes received from the SMBus peripheral through that pointer. The driver then writes up to SMBUS_BLOCK_BYTES_MAX (32) bytes of peripheral-supplied data there (the STM32 driver writes as many bytes as the peripheral's length byte announces, up to 255). The address is fully attacker-chosen; the written content comes from the bus and is typically influenceable by the caller through the choice of peripheral and command, or by first writing data to a device that echoes it back. items.title: CVE-2026-102948: Several Bluetooth LE Audio services in subsys/bluetooth/audio register global connection and authentication callbacks but assume every connection is LE. When CONFIG_BT_CLASSIC is e
items.summary: Several Bluetooth LE Audio services in subsys/bluetooth/audio register global connection and authentication callbacks but assume every connection is LE. When CONFIG_BT_CLASSIC is enabled, the host also invokes these callbacks for BR/EDR connections. For such connections bt_conn_get_dst() returns NULL, and bt_conn_get_info() leaves info.le.dst unset (zero or uninitialized stack data). The CSIP Set Member (csip_disconnected(), handle_csip_disconnect(), handle_csip_auth_complete()), PACS (pacs_auth_pairing_complete(), pacs_security_changed()) and HAS (security_changed(), client_alloc(), client_free()) callbacks then compare or copy a Bluetooth address through that NULL or uninitialized pointer. A remote device within Bluetooth range can trigger this against a dual-mode device that exposes LE Audio server roles and accepts BR/EDR connections. Opening and closing a BR/EDR ACL link, with no pairing, reaches the CSIP Set Member disconnect path. Completing SSP pairing (for example Just Works) or encryption reaches the PACS and HAS paths. items.title: CVE-2026-102949: The Intel SEDI I2C controller driver (drivers/i2c/i2c_sedi.c, used on Intel ISH platforms) waits for each asynchronous transfer with k_sem_take() on a per-controller completion sem
items.summary: The Intel SEDI I2C controller driver (drivers/i2c/i2c_sedi.c, used on Intel ISH platforms) waits for each asynchronous transfer with k_sem_take() on a per-controller completion semaphore and a 1 s timeout. When the wait times out, i2c_sedi_api_full_io() aborts the transfer via SEDI_I2C_ABORT_TRANSFER, but if the controller's completion interrupt fires between the timeout expiring and the abort masking interrupts, the callback k_sem_give()s the semaphore and the token is never discarded. The next transfer on that bus then takes the stale token immediately and returns success (the stale context->err is usually 0) while the controller is still executing it. The HAL interrupt handler (or DMA) keeps copying received bytes into the caller's msgs[i].buf. Since I2C callers typically pass stack buffers, this writes into a stack frame that has already been returned from, and the caller also consumes incomplete data. The desynchronization can persist across later transfers. Triggering the race requires a transfer to complete just after the 1 s timeout. items.summary: MediaInfoLib before 26.10 contains a divide-by-zero vulnerability in TimeCode::FromString() that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying hour-unit timestamps with fewer than three fractional digits. items.summary: KindleEar 3.0.0 through 3.5.3 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows authenticated non-admin users to run Python code by uploading malicious recipes. items.summary: Tabbycat 2.9.0 through 2.12.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in TournamentViewSet that allows unauthenticated attackers to gain write access because PerTournamentPermissionRequired returns True for views lacking a tournament attribute. Attackers can send POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE requests to /api/v1/tournaments to create, modify or delete tournaments, cascading deletion to teams and speakers.

items.title: CVE-2026-135430: KindleEar 3.0.0 through 3.5.3 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in application/view/subscribe.py that allows authenticated users to access other users' rec
items.summary: KindleEar 3.0.0 through 3.5.3 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in application/view/subscribe.py that allows authenticated users to access other users' records by id without ownership checks. Attackers can enumerate sequential recipe ids to read recipe source containing credentials, delete recipes and custom RSS feeds, and overwrite saved site logins.

items.title: CVE-2026-135431: MyBibliotheca 3.0.0 before 3.0.4 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to modify or delete other users' books via /api/v1/books
items.summary: MyBibliotheca 3.0.0 before 3.0.4 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to modify or delete other users' books via /api/v1/books/ . Attackers can obtain book UUIDs from recently added books across all owners, then send PUT or DELETE requests to rename, alter, or permanently delete them.

items.title: CVE-2026-135432: sdcb Chats 1.10.0 before 1.17.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in GetAssignedUserDetails that allows assigned non-admin users to read other users' per-user MCP h
items.summary: sdcb Chats 1.10.0 before 1.17.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in GetAssignedUserDetails that allows assigned non-admin users to read other users' per-user MCP headers. items.title: CVE-2026-135433: FLTK through 1.4.5 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in Fl_BMP_Image::load_bmp_() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying crafted BMP or ICO files. At
items.summary: FLTK through 1.4.5 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in Fl_BMP_Image::load_bmp_() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying crafted BMP or ICO files. Attackers can specify very large image dimensions so the 32-bit row and alpha mask pointer offsets wrap, writing file-derived pixel bytes out of bounds to crash applications or possibly execute code.

items.summary: A vulnerability was found in vijaythapa333 django-student-management-system up to 0d96e62cc4e996e3e77bec1b8e3da3980edf8889. Affected by this issue is the function student_profile_update of the file StudentViews.py of the component Student Profile Update. The manipulation of the argument first_name results in cross site scripting. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been made public and could be used. This product utilizes a rolling release system for continuous delivery, and as such, version information for affected or updated releases is not disclosed. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

items.title: CVE-2026-127223: GFI HelpDesk before 4.99.13 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the staff group management feature that allows authenticated attackers with administrator privileges to execu
items.summary: GFI HelpDesk before 4.99.13 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the staff group management feature that allows authenticated attackers with administrator privileges to execute arbitrary SQL queries by supplying a crafted title parameter to /admin/index.php?/Base/StaffGroup/InsertSubmit. The Controller_StaffGroup.RunChecks() method concatenates the unsanitized title value directly into a duplicate name lookup query against the staffgroup table, allowing attackers to read or modify database contents.

items.title: CVE-2026-127224: GFI HelpDesk before 4.99.13 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the archiver export feature that allows authenticated attackers with administrator privileges to execute arbi
items.summary: GFI HelpDesk before 4.99.13 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the archiver export feature that allows authenticated attackers with administrator privileges to execute arbitrary SQL queries by supplying crafted itemid[] array values to /admin/index.php?/archiver/Manager/ExportAll. The Controller_Manager.ExportAll() method joins the itemid values with implode() and GetWhere() concatenates them into an IN() clause without sanitization or parameterization, and DumpTables() executes the resulting query against each ticket-related table, allowing attackers to read or modify database contents.

items.title: CVE-2026-134010: odf-kit is a TypeScript and JavaScript library for working with OpenDocument Format files. In versions 0.9.8 through 0.14.1, the odsToHtml() renderer inserts document-controlled ce
items.summary: odf-kit is a TypeScript and JavaScript library for working with OpenDocument Format files. In versions 0.9.8 through 0.14.1, the odsToHtml() renderer inserts document-controlled cell formatting and row height values into HTML style attributes without escaping them. An attacker can craft an ODS file that injects arbitrary HTML attributes or elements, allowing JavaScript execution in the host page's origin when an application inserts the converted output as HTML. This issue is fixed in version 0.14.2.

items.title: CVE-2026-134841: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, misreads some quoted text in its query parser. A `}` inside a literal ends a JDBC escape such as `{ts}`, and the rest of the literal is translat
items.summary: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, misreads some quoted text in its query parser. A `}` inside a literal ends a JDBC escape such as `{ts}`, and the rest of the literal is translated as SQL. A dollar quote whose tag has a non-ASCII symbol or space is not recognized. An `E''` string with a doubled quote is scanned as a standard string. `{fn right}` and `{fn timestampdiff}` with a negative argument produce a `--` comment. In each case text that the application quoted correctly can run as SQL with the privileges of the application's database role. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

items.title: CVE-2026-134842: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, can quote a string parameter for the wrong value of standard_conforming_strings when preferQueryMode=simple is set. A statement, trigger or conf
items.summary: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, can quote a string parameter for the wrong value of standard_conforming_strings when preferQueryMode=simple is set. A statement, trigger or configuration reload can turn the setting off during a session. A parameter value with a backslash and a quote then ends the literal, and the rest of the value runs as SQL. Before 42.7.6 any session with the setting off was affected. The statement cache can also reuse a parse made under the other setting. With allowEncodingChanges=true and the EUC_JP or SJIS client encoding, the yen sign acts as a backslash. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

items.title: CVE-2026-134843: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not close the connection when an unchecked exception interrupts a request. Part of a Bind message stays in the send buffer, and the server
items.summary: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not close the connection when an unchecked exception interrupts a request. Part of a Bind message stays in the send buffer, and the server reads the bytes that follow as the rest of it. The bytes of a value uploaded later on the same connection can then run as a SQL command. Since 42.6.0 a setBinaryStream() value without a length that is executed again throws such an exception, as does the driver's own retry after SQLState 0A000 or 26000. An application stream that throws an unchecked exception has the same effect in all versions. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

items.title: CVE-2026-134844: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, uses unqualified operators and functions in the catalog queries of DatabaseMetaData, ResultSetMetaData and TypeInfoCache. A role with CREATE on
items.summary: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, uses unqualified operators and functions in the catalog queries of DatabaseMetaData, ResultSetMetaData and TypeInfoCache. A role with CREATE on a schema of the application's search_path can add an operator with an exact type match, and the server runs it with the privileges of the application's role. TypeInfoCache also resolves an unqualified type name such as interval by its own ranking. A domain with that name in another schema, even the temporary schema of another session, can be used instead, and its CHECK runs in the application's session. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

items.title: CVE-2026-134845: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not enforce TLS for some settings that ask for it. When sslmode is not set, an ssl value such as 1, on, yes or verify-full gives sslmode=pr
items.summary: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not enforce TLS for some settings that ask for it. When sslmode is not set, an ssl value such as 1, on, yes or verify-full gives sslmode=prefer, or no TLS before 42.2.5. A service given in the Properties instead of the URL is ignored, so the sslmode of its pg_service.conf entry is lost. BaseDataSource.setUrl() keeps an sslmode, channelBinding or gssEncMode that was set before it. An attacker on the network path can then read and change the traffic. Versions 9.4.1208 through 42.7.14 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

items.title: CVE-2026-134846: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not check the token state that GSSContext.unwrap() reports on a GSS-encrypted connection. An attacker on the network path can replay an ear
items.summary: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not check the token state that GSSContext.unwrap() reports on a GSS-encrypted connection. An attacker on the network path can replay an earlier server packet from the same connection, and the driver accepts it as the answer to the current query. The driver also shares one MessageProp between reading and writing. One integrity-only packet from the server then makes the driver send later SQL and parameters without encryption. Only connections with gssEncMode=prefer or require that start GSS encryption are affected. Versions 42.2.15 through 42.7.14 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

items.title: CVE-2026-134847: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, cuts the weight and scale of a BigDecimal to 16 bits when it sends the value in binary, which is the default. The server then stores a different
items.summary: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, cuts the weight and scale of a BigDecimal to 16 bits when it sends the value in binary, which is the default. The server then stores a different number without an error. For example 999999.99e-262144 is stored as 999999.99, so a tiny value can pass a range check and be stored as a large one. The driver also computes 10 to the power of the scale first, so a short value such as 1e-200000000 keeps a thread busy for minutes. Versions 42.3.0 through 42.7.14 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

items.title: CVE-2026-134848: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not refuse a NUL character in a startup parameter. The StartupMessage is a list of NUL-terminated strings, so a NUL in the database name, u
items.summary: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not refuse a NUL character in a startup parameter. The StartupMessage is a list of NUL-terminated strings, so a NUL in the database name, user, currentSchema, options or ApplicationName adds further parameters. %00 in a URL decodes to a NUL. Someone who controls part of the URL or a property can choose another login role or add replication=database, although the connection still has to pass the authentication of that role. On a server that trusts the client, the attacker can log in as any role. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

items.title: CVE-2026-133469: XO (Xen Orchestra) is a solution to visualize, manage, backup and delegate your XCP-ng (or XenServer) infrastructure. Prior to 6.9.2 and 6.10.1, REST cookie parsing turns authentic
items.summary: XO (Xen Orchestra) is a solution to visualize, manage, backup and delegate your XCP-ng (or XenServer) infrastructure. Prior to 6.9.2 and 6.10.1, REST cookie parsing turns authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D into {}. REST authentication passes that object to the XO token provider without requiring a string. The token collection treats {} as an unfiltered lookup and returns its first token; the provider authenticates as that token's owner if it is unexpired. The authenticated /rest/v0/users/me/authentication_tokens route then returns reusable login token IDs. This vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild. This vulnerability is fixed in 6.9.2 and 6.10.1.

items.title: CVE-2026-96457: A flaw was found in the administrative interface of Keycloak, an identity and access management solution. The issue occurs when Fine-Grained Admin Permissions are used to restrict
items.summary: A flaw was found in the administrative interface of Keycloak, an identity and access management solution. The issue occurs when Fine-Grained Admin Permissions are used to restrict a group administrator from managing specific sub-groups. Due to an incomplete fix for a previous vulnerability, a restricted administrator can bypass these restrictions by moving a forbidden sub-group to the top level of the hierarchy. This allows the attacker to gain unauthorized control over the groups members, potentially leading to a full takeover of the security realm.

items.title: CVE-2026-135260: MISP contains multiple flaws in its login and one-time-password (OTP) brute-force lockout mechanism that collectively weaken authentication protection. - Lockout counter bypass: t
items.summary: MISP contains multiple flaws in its login and one-time-password (OTP) brute-force lockout mechanism that collectively weaken authentication protection. - Lockout counter bypass: the lockout stored and matched usernames using a single-byte case-fold function. An email address containing a non-ASCII capital letter (for example a Latin-1 or Cyrillic uppercase) was never counted toward the lockout threshold, allowing unlimited failed login attempts against that account. - Collation-folding authentication bypass: the database collation performs accent and width folding, so a Unicode variant of a valid address (e.g. a different diacritic or a full-width character) resolved to the same account during authentication while the lockout treated it as a distinct, untracked identity. An attacker could therefore authenticate as the target user using a folded alias without triggering the lockout. - Username enumeration via NUL byte: submitting a password containing a NUL byte caused the hashing routine to raise an exception, producing an HTTP 500 response for a known account but a different response for an unknown one, disclosing valid usernames. Preconditions: the target MISP instance is reachab

items.title: CVE-2026-135261: MISP's brute-force lockout mechanism for login and one-time-password (OTP) authentication is susceptible to bypass through Unicode case-folding inconsistencies and input handling f
items.summary: MISP's brute-force lockout mechanism for login and one-time-password (OTP) authentication is susceptible to bypass through Unicode case-folding inconsistencies and input handling flaws. - Email addresses containing non-ASCII capital letters are not counted toward the lockout threshold, permitting unlimited authentication attempts against a specific account. - Database collation folding (accent and width variants) allows an attacker to reach a valid account using a folded alias of the email address without the attempt being recorded in the lockout counter. - A password containing a NUL byte produces a distinct server error for known accounts while unknown accounts receive a different response, enabling username enumeration. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit these issues to perform unlimited password brute-force attacks against any account and to enumerate valid user accounts. Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52

items.title: CVE-2026-135262: MISP contains a DOM-based cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Pivot Explorer component. The bundled pivotick visualization library (version 1.2.0) rendered all string v
items.summary: MISP contains a DOM-based cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Pivot Explorer component. The bundled pivotick visualization library (version 1.2.0) rendered all string values it received as HTML markup rather than as plain text. As a result, user-controllable data fields, including attribute comments, attribute values, and reference relationship types, were interpreted and executed as HTML/JavaScript in the Pivot Explorer tooltip and sidebar panels. An authenticated user with the ability to create or modify MISP attributes could embed malicious HTML or script payloads in these fields. When another user (or the same user) opened the Pivot Explorer and viewed the affected event data, the injected markup would execute in the victim's browser context, potentially allowing session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions performed on behalf of the victim. Preconditions: - The attacker must have authenticated access to create or modify MISP attributes (comments, values, or reference relationship types). - The victim must open the Pivot Explorer and interact with or view the affected event data in the tooltip or sidebar. Security impact: Successful exploitation all

items.title: CVE-2026-135256: MISP contains a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) vulnerability in its Warninglist feature. Warninglist entries of type "regex" are evaluated against attribute values wi
items.summary: MISP contains a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) vulnerability in its Warninglist feature. Warninglist entries of type "regex" are evaluated against attribute values without any backtracking limit. An authenticated user with permission to add or import warninglist entries can supply a crafted regular expression pattern that triggers excessive backtracking in the PCRE engine, causing sustained CPU consumption and denial of service. Additionally, imported warninglists were not validated for syntactic correctness before replacing existing entries, allowing malformed or malicious patterns to be persisted and later evaluated without prior rejection. Preconditions: - An authenticated account with the ability to create, edit, or import warninglist entries (users below site-admin level can add entries). - The target MISP instance has at least one warninglist of type "regex" that will be evaluated against incoming attribute values. Impact: - Sustained CPU exhaustion leading to denial of service for all users of the MISP instance. - Potential for cascading performance degradation on shared infrastructure. Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135257: MISP contains an improper output sanitization vulnerability in the Zeek (Bro) intelligence export functionality. The export module constructs tab-separated lines for downstream Ze
items.summary: MISP contains an improper output sanitization vulnerability in the Zeek (Bro) intelligence export functionality. The export module constructs tab-separated lines for downstream Zeek/Bro intelligence feeds. The sanitization routine was intended to strip tab, newline, and carriage-return characters from user-controlled fields (organisation names and attribute values) before they were embedded into the export line format. However, the sanitization pipeline applied character replacement before HTML entity decoding, meaning that HTML entities such as (tab), (newline), and (carriage return) survived the initial pass and were subsequently decoded into actual separator characters. Additionally, organisation names were inserted into the export format string without any sanitization at all. An authenticated user with the ability to create or modify events, organisation names, or attribute values could embed HTML-encoded separator characters. When the Zeek/Bro export was generated, these characters would split a single export line into multiple lines or introduce extra tab-delimited fields, corrupting the structured intelligence feed consumed by downstream Zeek/Bro deployments. items.summary: MISP contains multiple related authorization and input-validation flaws in its object editing and attachment handling workflows. - A user with permission to edit their own object could inject a foreign attribute identifier into the object revision form. The revision data, stored in the server-side session, was merged into the stored object before the save diff was computed. The save then wrote to the foreign attribute row by its identifier without verifying that the row belonged to the caller's event or organisation, allowing an attacker to overwrite or soft-delete an attribute in another organisation's private event. - Attachment file paths were constructed directly from event and attribute identifiers supplied by the request. Because no type or format validation was applied, crafted values (for example directory-traversal sequences or file-name extensions) could cause the application to read from or write to file-system locations outside the intended attachment directory. - The audit-log behaviour recorded an edit under the event identifier carried in the save payload rather than the event identifier of the stored database row. items.title: CVE-2026-135259: MISP contains a type confusion vulnerability in the authentication key creation endpoint. When a user submits a floating-point value as the target user identifier, the authorizatio
items.summary: MISP contains a type confusion vulnerability in the authentication key creation endpoint. When a user submits a floating-point value as the target user identifier, the authorization check truncates the value to an integer (matching the attacker's own account), while the persistence layer rounds the same value to a different integer (the next account in the sequence). This discrepancy allows an authenticated user with key-creation permission to generate an API authentication key belonging to another user. Preconditions: - The attacker must be an authenticated user with the permission to create authentication keys. - The target user must have a consecutive numeric identifier immediately following the attacker's identifier. Impact: - Unauthorized creation of an API key for another user, granting the attacker access to that user's data and operations within the MISP instance. - The vulnerability is trivially exploitable by substituting a carefully crafted floating-point value for the integer user identifier in the request. Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135249: MISP accepted compressed HTTP request bodies (gzip, brotli, zstd) and decompressed them before authentication was performed, with no limit on the size of the resulting decompressed
items.summary: MISP accepted compressed HTTP request bodies (gzip, brotli, zstd) and decompressed them before authentication was performed, with no limit on the size of the resulting decompressed data. An unauthenticated attacker could send a small compressed payload that expands to a very large decompressed body, exhausting server memory and causing a denial of service. Brotli and zstd, with their high compression ratios, made the attack particularly effective. The vulnerability required no authentication and no special conditions beyond the ability to send an HTTP request with a Content-Encoding header. The impact is a complete loss of availability for the affected MISP instance. Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135250: MISP contains a denial-of-service vulnerability in its image processing pipeline. When generating attachment thumbnails or rendering event graph preview images, the application dec
items.summary: MISP contains a denial-of-service vulnerability in its image processing pipeline. When generating attachment thumbnails or rendering event graph preview images, the application decodes user-supplied image data using the GD library without first validating the declared pixel dimensions in the image header. Because GD allocates its pixel buffers outside the scope of PHP's memory_limit directive, a crafted image with an extremely large declared resolution (for example, 20000 x 20000 pixels) can trigger a multi-gigabyte memory allocation during the decode step, exhausting available system memory and causing the PHP worker process or the host to become unresponsive. Preconditions: - An authenticated MISP user with permission to upload attachments or to create/view event graphs. - The ability to supply a crafted image file (e.g., a PNG with a valid header declaring oversized dimensions). Impact: - Denial of service: memory exhaustion leading to process crash or host unavailability. - No confidentiality or integrity impact is indicated by the evidence. Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135252: MISP contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in its feed and sync HTTP request handling. When the application uses libcurl as the HTTP transport, the CURLOPT_FO
items.summary: MISP contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in its feed and sync HTTP request handling. When the application uses libcurl as the HTTP transport, the CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION option was enabled by default, causing the library to automatically follow HTTP redirects without the application's own per-hop validation logic being invoked. - Feed requests: MISP implements its own redirect validation for feed sources, but libcurl was following redirects before that validation could execute, allowing a malicious or compromised feed source to redirect the request to arbitrary internal URLs. - Sync requests: Sync peers are server-configured, and the application does not perform per-hop redirect validation for sync traffic. libcurl's automatic redirect following allowed a malicious sync peer to redirect the request to internal network resources. An attacker who is a configured sync peer, controls a feed source URL, or can influence DNS resolution for a configured endpoint can exploit this to cause the MISP server to issue requests to arbitrary internal services, potentially reading sensitive data or interacting with internal APIs that are not otherwise exposed. Affected: MISP

items.title: CVE-2026-135253: MISP's NIDS rule export functionality for Snort and Suricata formats does not properly escape user-controlled data before embedding it into generated rule text. Attribute values, t
items.summary: MISP's NIDS rule export functionality for Snort and Suricata formats does not properly escape user-controlled data before embedding it into generated rule text. Attribute values, tag names, and URL paths are inserted directly into rule options (msg, metadata, content matches) without neutralizing characters that are syntactically significant in the NIDS rule grammar, such as double quotes, semicolons, backslashes, commas, and control characters. An authenticated user with the ability to create or modify attributes in a MISP instance can craft attribute values or tag names containing these special characters. When the NIDS rules are exported, the unescaped data breaks out of the intended option or content field, allowing injection of arbitrary rule options, corruption of rule structure, or generation of syntactically invalid rules that may cause the downstream NIDS engine to reject the entire ruleset. The affected export paths include: - Snort and Suricata msg: option (quotes, semicolons, backslashes, control characters) - Suricata metadata: option (commas, semicolons, quotes, whitespace, control characters) - Suricata http.uri content: match for URL path (quotes, semicolons, pipe c

items.title: CVE-2026-135254: MISP is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in its correlation management functionality. The top-correlation cache regeneration and occurrence count regeneration actio
items.summary: MISP is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in its correlation management functionality. The top-correlation cache regeneration and occurrence count regeneration actions were accessible via bodyless GET requests and were triggered from the admin interface using plain hyperlinks rather than POST forms. Because these state-changing operations did not require a POST method and were reachable through simple URL navigation, an attacker who can induce an authenticated administrator to visit a malicious page or click a crafted link can trigger these operations without the administrator's explicit consent. Impact: - Unintended triggering of resource-intensive correlation regeneration processes - Potential disruption of correlation data processing and increased server load - No direct data disclosure or corruption is evidenced Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52

items.title: CVE-2026-135243: MISP contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the handling of sightings during server synchronization and bulk operations. The vulnerability allows a remote attacker with
items.summary: MISP contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the handling of sightings during server synchronization and bulk operations. The vulnerability allows a remote attacker with access to a synchronized MISP instance to pull sightings for events that are not shared with their organization or community. The sighting pull mechanism previously executed with elevated privileges and accepted event identifiers without verifying that the local event was authorized for sharing with the remote server. Additionally, the bulk save functionality for sightings did not strictly enforce that the attributes referenced in the request belonged to the specific event specified in the URL, allowing an attacker to associate sightings with unauthorized events by referencing attributes from other events. This can lead to unauthorized disclosure of threat intelligence data and integrity issues where sightings are incorrectly attributed to events the attacker should not access. The issue was reported by ENISA and fixed in version 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135244: MISP trusted client-supplied forwarded IP headers (such as X-Forwarded-For) without verifying that the request originated from a known proxy or that the value was a valid IP addres
items.summary: MISP trusted client-supplied forwarded IP headers (such as X-Forwarded-For) without verifying that the request originated from a known proxy or that the value was a valid IP address. The configured header value was accepted as the authoritative client IP for all security-relevant functions. An unauthenticated remote attacker could forge the forwarded header to: - Bypass IP-based restrictions on API authentication keys - Evade brute-force / rate-limiting protection - Inject arbitrary values into application and ECS logs, corrupting audit trails The vulnerability required the MISP.log_client_ip_header setting to be configured to a forwarded header (e.g. HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR), which is a common deployment when MISP sits behind a reverse proxy. Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52

items.title: CVE-2026-135245: MISP's LDAP authentication components (LdapAuth plugin and Apache LDAP authentication) unconditionally re-enabled user accounts that had been disabled by an administrator. During t
items.summary: MISP's LDAP authentication components (LdapAuth plugin and Apache LDAP authentication) unconditionally re-enabled user accounts that had been disabled by an administrator. During the user provisioning or update step of an LDAP login, the disabled flag was reset to enabled regardless of the account's current state. This allowed any user with valid LDAP credentials to bypass an administrative disable action simply by authenticating, effectively nullifying the ability to revoke access through account deactivation. - Affects the LdapAuth plugin and the ApacheSecureAuth component - The insecure behavior was the default; no special configuration was required to trigger it - An administrator's decision to disable a user (e.g., after a security incident or employee departure) could be reversed by the user's next successful LDAP login Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52

items.title: CVE-2026-135247: MISP's LinOTPAuth plugin, used for one-time-password authentication against a LinOTP server, did not enforce TLS server certificate verification when the LinOTPAuth.verifyssl confi
items.summary: MISP's LinOTPAuth plugin, used for one-time-password authentication against a LinOTP server, did not enforce TLS server certificate verification when the LinOTPAuth.verifyssl configuration option was not explicitly set. In a default or minimally configured deployment, the authentication request to the LinOTP server was sent without peer or peer-name certificate validation, effectively allowing self-signed or spoofed certificates. An attacker with a network position between the MISP instance and the LinOTP server could perform a man-in-the-middle attack to intercept or tamper with the authentication exchange, potentially capturing one-time passwords or user credentials. Preconditions: - The LinOTPAuth plugin is enabled and configured to communicate with a LinOTP server - The LinOTPAuth.verifyssl setting is absent or null (not explicitly set to true or false) - The attacker can position themselves on the network path between MISP and the LinOTP server Security impact: - Confidentiality of OTP tokens and authentication credentials in transit - Potential for credential interception or replay Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52

items.title: CVE-2026-135248: MISP contains a vulnerability in its password reset (forgot password) functionality where the base URL used to construct the reset link sent by email could be derived from the HTTP
items.summary: MISP contains a vulnerability in its password reset (forgot password) functionality where the base URL used to construct the reset link sent by email could be derived from the HTTP request's Host header rather than from an explicitly configured value. An unauthenticated attacker can send a crafted request with a malicious Host header. If the application's base URL was not explicitly configured (MISP.baseurl or MISP.external_baseurl), the bootstrap would derive it from the request, and the resulting password reset email would contain a link pointing to the attacker-controlled domain. When the victim clicks the link, they are directed to the attacker's site, enabling credential phishing or token theft. Preconditions: - The password reset feature (allow_password_forgotten) is enabled - MISP.baseurl and MISP.external_baseurl are not explicitly set to trusted values - The victim initiates or is targeted for a password reset Impact: - Phishing: victim is redirected to an attacker-controlled URL instead of the legitimate MISP instance - Potential credential compromise if the victim enters credentials on the attacker's site - No direct compromise of the MISP server itself Affected: MISP ve

items.title: CVE-2026-135239: MISP contains an authorization flaw in the data capture and import paths for events, galaxies, galaxy clusters, analyst data, and sightings. A user who is neither a sync user nor a
items.summary: MISP contains an authorization flaw in the data capture and import paths for events, galaxies, galaxy clusters, analyst data, and sightings. A user who is neither a sync user nor a site admin could create or import records attributed to an organisation other than their own, or cause the creation of a new organisation from a payload-supplied identifier. The root cause is an inconsistent authorization check: the code validated one representation of the creator organisation (for example a numeric ID or a UUID field) while storing a different representation taken directly from the user-supplied payload. In the event import path, a MISP export naming another organisation or a fabricated one was accepted and stored under that organisation. In the galaxy, cluster, analyst data, and sighting capture paths, the nested organisation object from the payload was used to create or reference an organisation without verifying the caller's membership. Impact: - Data (events, galaxies, clusters, analyst notes, sightings) can be created under an organisation the attacker does not belong to, polluting that organisation's data and potentially exposing it to that organisation's members. - New organisati

items.title: CVE-2026-135240: MISP contains an authorization bypass in its tag attachment functionality. The endpoints responsible for editing event tags, editing attribute tags, and adding tags to event report
items.summary: MISP contains an authorization bypass in its tag attachment functionality. The endpoints responsible for editing event tags, editing attribute tags, and adding tags to event reports accepted arbitrary tag IDs without verifying whether the authenticated user was permitted to attach the referenced tag. The events/addTag endpoint already resolved tag IDs through a restricted lookup that enforced per-user and per-organisation tag visibility rules. However, the three tag-editor endpoints (editEventTags, editAttributeTags, and eventReports/addTag) passed the supplied tag IDs directly to the attachment logic without any such check. Preconditions: - An authenticated user with tagger and add permissions on the target event/attribute/report. - Knowledge or discovery of a tag ID that is restricted (local_only) to another organisation. Impact: - A user can attach a tag that is restricted to a different organisation, effectively bypassing the tag visibility and scoping model. - A local_only tag can be attached as a global tag, violating the intended distribution restriction and potentially exposing the existence or semantics of another organisation's restricted tag to a broader audience. - Data

items.title: CVE-2026-135241: MISP contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the handling of Galaxy and Galaxy Cluster publish/unpublish operations. The application failed to enforce consistent permissi
items.summary: MISP contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the handling of Galaxy and Galaxy Cluster publish/unpublish operations. The application failed to enforce consistent permission checks when users attempted to unpublish a Galaxy or Galaxy Cluster. Specifically, the unpublish action only required the 'perm_galaxy_editor' permission, whereas the publish action required both 'perm_galaxy_editor' and 'perm_publish'. This inconsistency allowed a user from a different organization who possessed the 'perm_galaxy_editor' permission but lacked the 'perm_publish' permission to unpublish a Galaxy or Galaxy Cluster created by another organization. This action could disrupt the availability of shared threat intelligence data for other users and organizations relying on that cluster. The vulnerability affects MISP versions prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135242: MISP contains an authorization flaw in the Sharing Group Blueprint execution path. When a blueprint is executed, it rewrites the organisation roster of the associated sharing group
items.summary: MISP contains an authorization flaw in the Sharing Group Blueprint execution path. When a blueprint is executed, it rewrites the organisation roster of the associated sharing group. The check verifying that the blueprint's owning organisation still holds the right to extend (modify) that group was performed only once, at the time the blueprint was created. It was not re-evaluated at execution time. As a result, an organisation that subsequently lost its extend permission or was entirely removed from the sharing group could still execute its existing blueprint and overwrite the group's organisation roster, adding or removing member organisations at will. Preconditions: - An authenticated user belonging to an organisation that previously had extend rights on a sharing group - A blueprint already exists in that group owned by the attacker's organisation - The attacker's extend rights have been revoked or the organisation has been removed from the group after the blueprint was created Security impact: - Unauthorised modification of a sharing group's organisation roster - Potential unauthorised addition of organisations to a sharing group, exposing shared indicators and events - Bypass

items.title: CVE-2026-135237: MISP contains a DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the event report element rendering pipeline. The client-side sanitization function used to prepare values for
items.summary: MISP contains a DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the event report element rendering pipeline. The client-side sanitization function used to prepare values for doT templates only escaped ampersand, less-than, and greater-than characters. However, the templates place these values inside double-quoted HTML attributes. Because double-quote and single-quote characters were not escaped, a user with the ability to author or modify report element values could inject a quote character to break out of the attribute context and inject arbitrary HTML or JavaScript that executes in the viewing user's browser. Preconditions: - The attacker must be an authenticated user with permission to create or edit event report elements (e.g., a report author). - A victim must open or view the crafted report in a browser. Security impact: - Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the victim's MISP session. - Potential theft of session tokens, sensitive data, or unauthorized actions performed on behalf of the victim. Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135238: MISP contains a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Overmind server preview's analyst data badge component. When rendering the analyst data link for a remote attribute,
items.summary: MISP contains a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Overmind server preview's analyst data badge component. When rendering the analyst data link for a remote attribute, the remote server's UUID value was inserted into an inline JavaScript event handler using only HTML entity encoding, which is insufficient to prevent breakout from the JavaScript string context within the HTML attribute. An attacker who can control or influence the UUID value of a remote attribute (for example, through a malicious or compromised upstream MISP server sharing data via Overmind) could inject arbitrary JavaScript that executes in the context of the victim's MISP session when the analyst data badge is clicked. Preconditions: - The victim must be authenticated to a MISP instance with Overmind enabled. - The victim must view a remote event preview containing the crafted UUID. - The victim must interact with (click) the analyst data badge element. Security impact: - Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser session. - Potential theft of session credentials, manipulation of page content, or initiation of unauthorized actions on behalf of the authenticated user. Affected versions:

items.title: CVE-2026-135234: MISP contains a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the feed and server event preview pages. When a remote MISP instance (configured as a feed source or connected server) s
items.summary: MISP contains a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the feed and server event preview pages. When a remote MISP instance (configured as a feed source or connected server) supplies object or reference UUIDs and IDs containing special characters, these values are rendered in the preview HTML without proper escaping. The vulnerable behavior occurs in two contexts: - HTML element identifiers and text content: Remote UUIDs and IDs are inserted into DOM element IDs and visible text without HTML encoding, allowing injection of arbitrary HTML markup. - Inline JavaScript event handlers: Remote UUIDs and IDs are embedded into onClick handler strings using only HTML escaping, which does not protect against JavaScript string-literal breakout. A crafted value containing a single quote can terminate the string and inject arbitrary JavaScript. An attacker who controls a remote MISP instance (feed or server peer) can craft UUID or ID fields with a malicious payload. When an authenticated user on the victim instance views the corresponding event preview, the injected script executes in the user's browser within the MISP application origin, potentially allowing session hijacking, data exfilt

items.title: CVE-2026-135235: MISP contains a stored cross-site script (XSS) vulnerability in the event review page used for merge, import, and enrichment workflows. Object references displayed on this page in
items.summary: MISP contains a stored cross-site script (XSS) vulnerability in the event review page used for merge, import, and enrichment workflows. Object references displayed on this page include the UUID, name, and meta-category of the referenced object. These values originate from imported data (another event, a module result, or an import file) and were rendered into the HTML output without any encoding or sanitization. An attacker who can supply or influence imported MISP-format data can embed arbitrary HTML or JavaScript in the referenced object's UUID, name, or meta-category fields. When a user views the review page, the malicious script executes in the user's browser context. Preconditions: - The attacker must be able to introduce data into a MISP instance (e.g., via import, module enrichment, or event merge). - A victim user must open the affected review page in a browser. Security impact: - Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the MISP web application. - Potential theft of session tokens, manipulation of user actions, or exfiltration of sensitive threat-intelligence data visible on the page. Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135236: MISP contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in its map attachment rendering. When a GPX or GeoJSON file is uploaded as an attachment to a MISP event, the waypoi
items.summary: MISP contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in its map attachment rendering. When a GPX or GeoJSON file is uploaded as an attachment to a MISP event, the waypoint names (GPX) and property names and values (GeoJSON) are inserted into Leaflet map popups without HTML escaping. Because Leaflet renders popup content as raw HTML, any markup or script embedded in those fields is executed in the browser of every user who views the map and interacts with the affected marker or icon. Preconditions: - An authenticated user with permission to upload attachments to a MISP event crafts a GPX or GeoJSON file containing malicious HTML/JavaScript in waypoint names or GeoJSON property keys/values. - A victim user views the event map and clicks the affected marker or GeoJSON icon, triggering the popup. Impact: - Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the MISP web application, potentially leading to session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions performed on behalf of the victim. Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135213: Worklenz before 3.4.3 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in GET /api/v1/activity-logs/:id that allows authenticated users to read other teams' task activity
items.summary: Worklenz before 3.4.3 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in GET /api/v1/activity-logs/:id that allows authenticated users to read other teams' task activity logs because it lacks the verifyTaskAccess middleware. Attackers who know another team's task UUID can retrieve reporter and assignee names and avatars plus the full timeline of status, priority, label and estimation changes.

items.title: CVE-2026-135231: MISP contains an authorization bypass in the galaxy cluster detachment functionality. Users holding the sync role permission were incorrectly exempted from the tagger and organisat
items.summary: MISP contains an authorization bypass in the galaxy cluster detachment functionality. Users holding the sync role permission were incorrectly exempted from the tagger and organisation ownership checks when detaching galaxy clusters from events or attributes. This allowed a sync user belonging to one organisation to remove galaxy cluster associations (threat intelligence tags) from events and attributes owned by a different organisation. The sync permission was intended for replication workflows, which never invoke the cluster detachment code path, but was erroneously used as a blanket authorization bypass. Impact: - Cross-organisation data integrity: a sync user can strip threat intelligence cluster associations from other organisations' events and attributes. - Disruption of shared threat intelligence: removal of cluster tags can alter the analytical context of events visible to other users. Preconditions: - An authenticated user with the sync role permission (perm_sync) and tagger permission (perm_tagger). - The target event or attribute must belong to a different organisation than the attacker. Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135232: MISP Collections retained a sharing group reference (sharing_group_id) even when the collection's distribution level was below 4 (i.e., not restricted to a sharing group). As a res
items.summary: MISP Collections retained a sharing group reference (sharing_group_id) even when the collection's distribution level was below 4 (i.e., not restricted to a sharing group). As a result, the sharing group name and UUID were displayed in the collection index and view endpoints to any user who could see the collection, regardless of whether that user was a member of the sharing group. Additionally, when collections were pushed to remote MISP servers, the sharing group data was included in the push payload even for collections not distributed to a sharing group, potentially leaking the group identity to remote systems. Preconditions: - An authenticated user with sufficient access to view the affected collection (e.g., a collection with distribution 0-3 that is publicly or broadly visible). - The collection must have a stale sharing_group_id stored from a prior save. Impact: - Unauthorized disclosure of the sharing group name and UUID to users outside the group. - Potential leakage of sharing group structure to remote MISP servers via the push mechanism. - An attacker could enumerate sharing group names to identify targeting opportunities. Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135233: MISP's interactive CLI shell, when used to edit or disable a user account, did not update the user record's modification timestamp. The application's session validation mechanism r
items.summary: MISP's interactive CLI shell, when used to edit or disable a user account, did not update the user record's modification timestamp. The application's session validation mechanism relies on this timestamp to detect that a user's record has changed and to reload the user's state in all active sessions. As a result, a user who was disabled or had their role or permissions modified through the CLI would retain their existing authenticated session and continue to operate with their previous privileges until the session naturally expired. The administrative intent to revoke or reduce access was not enforced on already-active sessions. Preconditions: - An administrator performs a user edit or disable action via the MISP interactive CLI shell rather than the web interface. - The target user has one or more active web sessions at the time of the change. Impact: - A disabled user retains full access to the MISP instance for the duration of their existing session. - A user whose role or permissions were reduced via the CLI continues to operate with their prior, higher privileges in open sessions. Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135207: Healthchecks before 4.4 contains a verification bypass vulnerability that allows project users to mark arbitrary email addresses as verified because Channel.make_token() omits the
items.summary: Healthchecks before 4.4 contains a verification bypass vulnerability that allows project users to mark arbitrary email addresses as verified because Channel.make_token() omits the email address. Attackers can verify an address they control, change the integration to a victim address, then reuse the original link to send unsolicited alert emails.

items.title: CVE-2026-135208: Kerberos Agent before 3.14.4 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge administrator tokens because JWTMiddleWare() falls back
items.summary: Kerberos Agent before 3.14.4 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge administrator tokens because JWTMiddleWare() falls back to the hard-coded key TOBECHANGED. Attackers can sign HS256 tokens with arbitrary username and role claims to access /api and /config routes, exposing RTSP, ONVIF, Hub and encryption keys, rewriting configuration, and stopping the camera.

items.title: CVE-2026-135209: ServerOS Panel before 1.10.1 contains a decompression bomb vulnerability in DeploySourcePacker::extract() that allows authenticated users with manage-machines permission to bypass
items.summary: ServerOS Panel before 1.10.1 contains a decompression bomb vulnerability in DeploySourcePacker::extract() that allows authenticated users with manage-machines permission to bypass the 4 GB unpacked-size limit by under-declaring zip entry sizes. Attackers can upload a crafted archive via POST /machines/{machine}/sources whose entries inflate far beyond declared sizes, filling the host disk and denying service to all workspaces.

items.title: CVE-2026-135210: Plane before 1.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in WorkspaceDraftIssueViewSet that allows authenticated workspace members to create drafts in unauthorized project
items.summary: Plane before 1.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in WorkspaceDraftIssueViewSet that allows authenticated workspace members to create drafts in unauthorized projects by supplying an arbitrary project_id. Attackers can convert drafts into work items in private or removed-from projects with chosen title, state, assignees, cycle_id and module_ids, triggering notifications and disclosing project membership.

items.title: CVE-2026-135211: BISHENG before 3.0.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the /api/v2/workflow/invoke and /api/v2/workflow/stop routes that allows unauthenticated attackers to run wo
items.summary: BISHENG before 3.0.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the /api/v2/workflow/invoke and /api/v2/workflow/stop routes that allows unauthenticated attackers to run workflows as the administrator. Attackers knowing a workflow UUID can supply an override replacing a Code node's code parameter with Python passed to exec(), achieving remote code execution, or stop other users' workflow sessions.

items.title: CVE-2026-135212: AiSOC before 23.6.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the agents service that allows authenticated users to read other tenants' investigation runs by supplying thei
items.summary: AiSOC before 23.6.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the agents service that allows authenticated users to read other tenants' investigation runs by supplying their run_id. items.summary: ToDesktop Builder before 0.36.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the todesktop-fs custom protocol handler that allows attackers to escape the bundled files directory using ../ sequences. items.title: CVE-2026-135078: A vulnerability has been found in KeudellCoding User Location Map up to 1.2.5. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file resources/humhub.usermap.js of
items.summary: A vulnerability has been found in KeudellCoding User Location Map up to 1.2.5. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file resources/humhub.usermap.js of the component MapView Widget. The manipulation of the argument displayname leads to cross site scripting. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. Upgrading to version 1.3.0 addresses this issue. items.title: CVE-2026-134492: In mcp-server-fetch from 2026.10.10 and before 2026.11.11, the check that blocks requests to non-public addresses treats IPv6 site-local addresses (fec0::/10) as public. A fetch to
items.summary: In mcp-server-fetch from 2026.10.10 and before 2026.11.11, the check that blocks requests to non-public addresses treats IPv6 site-local addresses (fec0::/10) as public. A fetch to such an address passes the server-side request forgery guard. Practical impact is limited because many hosts have no route to this range.

items.title: CVE-2026-134465: In mcp-server-git before 2026.10.28, the --repository restriction can be bypassed through a nested directory that contains a .git file with a gitdir pointer to a repository outside
items.summary: In mcp-server-git before 2026.10.28, the --repository restriction can be bypassed through a nested directory that contains a .git file with a gitdir pointer to a repository outside the allowed path. A caller who can invoke the server's tools, place such a file in the allowed tree, and knows the outside repository's path can read committed content from that repository and create branches in it.

items.title: CVE-2026-133632: In astro-airflow-mcp 0.5.0 through 0.9.1, the af CLI and the MCP server send telemetry from a Python subprocess that can import modules from the current working directory. If a use
items.summary: In astro-airflow-mcp 0.5.0 through 0.9.1, the af CLI and the MCP server send telemetry from a Python subprocess that can import modules from the current working directory. If a user runs an af command or an MCP tool call from inside a project that contains an attacker-supplied json.py, that file runs with the user's privileges. Users who only run the tool in projects they trust are not affected. Fixed in 0.9.2; in earlier versions, setting AF_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 prevents it.

items.title: CVE-2026-132779: When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use TLS 1.3 early data using the ssl_early_data on directive, an attacker can use a specially crafted TLS 1.3 connection to dr
items.summary: When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use TLS 1.3 early data using the ssl_early_data on directive, an attacker can use a specially crafted TLS 1.3 connection to drive an NGINX worker into a tight loop in which it repeatedly retries the same send without ever making progress. The worker continues accepting new connections and handling existing ones, but one CPU core is pinned at 100%. Impact: System performance can degrade until the NGINX worker process is either forced to restart or is manually restarted. This vulnerability may allow an unauthenticated attacker to cause a degradation of service that can lead to a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

items.title: CVE-2026-129975: A flaw was found in gpgme. When processing crafted input, an early return following memory reallocation can leave internal buffer pointers referencing previously freed memory, resu
items.summary: A flaw was found in gpgme. When processing crafted input, an early return following memory reallocation can leave internal buffer pointers referencing previously freed memory, resulting in a double-free condition during cleanup. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to corrupt process memory, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or a Denial of Service (DoS) crash.

items.title: CVE-2026-107784: On Windows, the tarfile "tar" and "data" extraction filters did not reject member names or link targets that have a drive but no root, such as "C:foo". When extracting to a relativ
items.summary: On Windows, the tarfile "tar" and "data" extraction filters did not reject member names or link targets that have a drive but no root, such as "C:foo". When extracting to a relative destination, such a member was written to the current working directory of that drive instead of the destination, and a symbolic link with such a target pointed outside the destination. The filters now refuse these member names and link targets with AbsolutePathError and AbsoluteLinkError.

items.title: Cisco Expressway Series Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.summary: A vulnerability in the database service feature of Cisco Expressway Series could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker with network access to a Cisco Expressway device to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root . This vulnerability is due to the use of persistent cookies. Additionally, there is insufficient validation of client certificates when the TLS Verify Mode is set to Enabled for clustering, which means that client certificates are not validated. An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device. Note: Cisco Expressway Series refers to Cisco Expressway Core (Expressway-C) devices and Cisco Expressway Edge (Expressway-E) devices. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-vcs-static-

items.summary: Wing FTP Server before 8.2.8 contains a predictable session identifier vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to hijack administrator sessions by deriving identifiers from process, time, ServerID, and client IP state. items.title: CVE-2026-93585: An improper authorization vulnerability in the EasyVistas EV Reach Client Agent allows authenticated users with low privileges to execute arbitrary commands on a remote Windows end
items.summary: An improper authorization vulnerability in the EasyVistas EV Reach Client Agent allows authenticated users with low privileges to execute arbitrary commands on a remote Windows endpoint with LocalSystem privileges. The affected agent service does not sufficiently enforce authorization restrictions for certain privileged remote management operations. Under specific conditions, the agent fails to apply the intended user impersonation mechanism and executes user-supplied commands within the security context of the agent service, which runs as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM. As a result, an authenticated attacker may bypass the intended privilege restrictions and execute arbitrary commands with the highest user-mode privileges on an affected Windows system. Successful exploitation may lead to complete compromise of the affected endpoint, including unauthorized access to sensitive information, modification of system configurations, installation of malicious software, or disruption of system availability. The vulnerability does not require administrative credentials or user interaction after successful authentication.

items.title: CVE-2026-134927: A weakness has been identified in phpBB up to 3.3.19. Affected by this vulnerability is the function phpbb_get_user_rank of the file includes/acp/acp_ranks.php of the component Ran
items.summary: A weakness has been identified in phpBB up to 3.3.19. Affected by this vulnerability is the function phpbb_get_user_rank of the file includes/acp/acp_ranks.php of the component Ranks Handler. This manipulation of the argument rank_image causes cross site scripting. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The vendor confirms: "We have reviewed the report and intend to address the issue as part of our ongoing security hardening efforts. Given that exploitation requires authenticated administrative access, we consider this a low-priority issue. We will aim to include a fix in our next release and will notify you once it is available."
