items.title: CVE-2026-132662: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the SQL Profiler save and load functions in the PEM web application do not keep the client-supplied file name inside the user's storage direct
items.summary: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the SQL Profiler save and load functions in the PEM web application do not keep the client-supplied file name inside the user's storage directory. A user with the SQL Profiler role (pem_comp_sqlprofiler) can read JSON files, and overwrite files that the PEM web server account can write, outside their own storage directory. Overwriting the PEM web application's configuration database stops the web console for all users. From PEM 10.6.1, the SQL Profiler only reads and writes files inside the user's storage directory.

items.title: CVE-2026-132663: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), webhook URLs are not validated, and the PEM agent does not restrict the URL schemes it uses to deliver webhooks. A user with the alert configu
items.summary: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), webhook URLs are not validated, and the PEM agent does not restrict the URL schemes it uses to deliver webhooks. A user with the alert configuration role (pem_config_alert) can set up a webhook with a file:// URL. When the webhook is sent, the agent on the PEM server, which runs as root by default, reads the local file and stores its contents in the webhook error record in the PEM database, where any PEM user can read it. From PEM 10.6.1, PEM accepts and sends only http and https webhook URLs.

items.title: CVE-2026-132664: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), any PEM user can read the encrypted passwords that PEM agents use to connect to monitored servers, including the PEM backend superuser passwor
items.summary: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), any PEM user can read the encrypted passwords that PEM agents use to connect to monitored servers, including the PEM backend superuser password stored when the PEM server is configured. Unless a custom encryption key is configured, these passwords are encrypted with a key that is the same in every PEM installation, so they can be decrypted. From PEM 10.6.1, PEM users can no longer read these passwords.

items.title: CVE-2026-132665: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the pem.deploy_job_template() function does not check that the caller can access the servers, groups and agents it deploys a job template to.
items.summary: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the pem.deploy_job_template() function does not check that the caller can access the servers, groups and agents it deploys a job template to. When PEM teams are used to separate access, a user with the scheduled tasks role (pem_manage_schedule_task) can deploy and schedule SQL or shell job steps on agents that belong to other teams. From PEM 10.6.1, PEM checks team access for every server, group and agent a template is deployed to.

items.title: CVE-2026-132668: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), any PEM user can run the pem.send_webhook() function, which runs with elevated privileges and queues a payload for any configured webhook. The
items.summary: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), any PEM user can run the pem.send_webhook() function, which runs with elevated privileges and queues a payload for any configured webhook. The PEM agent then delivers it with that webhook's stored headers, OAuth token or client certificate, so a user can send forged notifications to endpoints they could not otherwise authenticate to. From PEM 10.6.1, no PEM login role can call this function directly. PEM still sends webhook notifications through its own internal paths.

items.title: CVE-2026-132658: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the pem_agent role, which every PEM agent login inherits, is a member of the PostgreSQL pg_read_server_files and pg_write_server_files roles o
items.summary: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the pem_agent role, which every PEM agent login inherits, is a member of the PostgreSQL pg_read_server_files and pg_write_server_files roles on the PEM backend database. An attacker who controls any monitored host, and so its PEM agent certificate, can read and write files on the PEM server host as the postgres operating system user. This includes the PEM certificate authority key, which lets the attacker issue certificates for other agents and act as them. From PEM 10.6.1, PEM agents no longer hold these roles.

items.title: CVE-2026-132659: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the row-level security policies on pem.job and pem.jobstep that apply to PEM agents do not limit an agent to its own jobs. An attacker who con
items.summary: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the row-level security policies on pem.job and pem.jobstep that apply to PEM agents do not limit an agent to its own jobs. An attacker who controls one monitored host, and so its PEM agent certificate, can create, change or delete jobs for every other agent, including the agent on the PEM server. Agents run SQL job steps with the database credentials of the server they monitor, and shell job steps where batch jobs are enabled, so compromising one monitored host can give superuser SQL access to every monitored database and to the PEM backend. From PEM 10.6.1, PEM agents can no longer create jobs or change job definitions or job steps.

items.title: CVE-2026-132660: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), several SECURITY DEFINER functions in the pem schema of the PEM backend database are owned by a superuser but do not set a safe search_path. A
items.summary: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), several SECURITY DEFINER functions in the pem schema of the PEM backend database are owned by a superuser but do not set a safe search_path. Any PEM user who can connect to the PEM backend database can create objects that these functions use in place of the intended ones, and so run arbitrary SQL with superuser privileges. Temporary objects can be used for this on every supported PostgreSQL version, and objects in the public schema on PostgreSQL 14 backends and backends upgraded from PostgreSQL 14. From PEM 10.6.1, these functions run with a fixed search_path.

items.title: CVE-2026-132661: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), multi-factor authentication (MFA) is not enforced on the PEM web application's own routes. An attacker who knows the password of a user who ha
items.summary: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), multi-factor authentication (MFA) is not enforced on the PEM web application's own routes. An attacker who knows the password of a user who has enrolled a second factor can skip the second factor and call PEM's pages and APIs directly, with that user's permissions. A similar issue in pgAdmin 4 was assigned CVE-2024-4215. From PEM 10.6.1, every authenticated PEM route requires a completed MFA check.

items.title: CVE-2026-126334: Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in phoenixframework phoenix_live_view allows an authenticated user to mount a router-mounted LiveView without the on_mount hooks of its live_s
items.summary: Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in phoenixframework phoenix_live_view allows an authenticated user to mount a router-mounted LiveView without the on_mount hooks of its live_session via a phx_join message that carries neither a "url" nor a "redirect" key. The catch-all clause of the private Phoenix.LiveView.Channel.authorize_session/3 in lib/phoenix_live_view/channel.ex accepts a join without a URL for any session, including a root LiveView mounted at the router. The channel then mounts the LiveView with no route, and only a route adds the live_session hooks to the mount lifecycle. Checks that those hooks perform on the connected mount do not run, and event checks that they attach through attach_hook/4 are never attached. The attacker needs a valid session token for the LiveView, which only the HTTP render issues, after the hooks pass there. on_mount hooks declared in the LiveView module still run. This issue affects phoenix_live_view: from 0.16.0 before 1.0.20, from 1.1.0-rc.0 before 1.1.34, and from 1.2.0-rc.0 before 1.2.14.

items.title: CVE-2026-127027: Poste.io is vulnerable to remote code execution in DMARC report processing. Email sent to dmarc-reports@ is saved without sender verification. Script that runs as root unpa
items.summary: Poste.io is vulnerable to remote code execution in DMARC report processing. Email sent to dmarc-reports@ is saved without sender verification. Script that runs as root unpacks the attachments using unsafe shell commands, allowing command injection through crafted attachments (e.g. file names or archive contents). A remote unauthenticated attacker who can send an email to the server's port 25 can execute arbitrary commands as root within the Poste.io container. This issue was fixed in version 2.5.22.

items.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
items.summary: Between October 17 and October 20, 2026, a critical security compromise involving Certificate Authorities that are managed by eMudhra was uncovered. A security researcher demonstrated that the private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were fundamentally broken due to an unprecedented error in their Key Generation Ceremony (KGC) in April 2025. This allows anyone to brute-force acquire these private keys within seconds. For more information, see eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise and the Cisco Talos blog post Compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates . For information about Splunk products and offerings, see Compromised eMudhra Intermediate Certificate Authorities on Splunk Products - October 2026 . Important: If a product is not listed within this advisory, Cisco's review indicates that the product is not affected by this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-emudhra-info-ScS22A1r Security Impact Rating: Informational

items.title: CVE-2026-80188: The BuddyBoss Addons plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in versions up to, and including, 1.2.1. This is due to the Social Logi
items.summary: The BuddyBoss Addons plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in versions up to, and including, 1.2.1. This is due to the Social Login REST endpoint trusting unverified Apple and Facebook identity-token claims and linking an attacker-controlled provider identifier to an existing WordPress user selected by the token’s email claim. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers who know a user’s email address to associate their provider identity with that account, including administrator accounts, and subsequently authenticate as the victim. Successful exploitation requires the BuddyBoss Platform plugin to be installed and active, with the Social Login module and selected provider enabled and configured. On sites with the separate BuddyBoss App JWT component, the vulnerable REST request can return an application token immediately.

items.title: CVE-2026-106024: Mongoose Embedded Web Server / Networking Library before 7.24 contains a WebSocket fragmentation validation vulnerability that allows remote attackers to spoof message metadata by
items.summary: Mongoose Embedded Web Server / Networking Library before 7.24 contains a WebSocket fragmentation validation vulnerability that allows remote attackers to spoof message metadata by sending a single CONTINUATION frame with FIN=1 as the first data frame instead of a required TEXT/BINARY start frame, violating RFC 6455 sequencing rules. Attackers can craft this malformed frame to make mg_ws_cb() in src/ws.c misinterpret the first byte of payload as saved FIN/opcode flags, causing the application to receive a dispatched MG_EV_WS_MSG event with attacker-controlled flags and data truncated by one byte without closing the connection.

items.summary: diffpy.structure before 3.5.1 contains a code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run Python code by supplying crafted CIF symmetry operations passed to eval() in get_symop(). items.title: CVE-2026-101340: Net::DNS uses a 16-bit query ID to match responses to the corresponding requests. In versions up to and including 1.57, the ID is obtained from Perl's built-in rand() function. A
items.summary: Net::DNS uses a 16-bit query ID to match responses to the corresponding requests. In versions up to and including 1.57, the ID is obtained from Perl's built-in rand() function. An attacker that can observe the sequence of query IDs is able to expose the internal state of the PNRG and hence predict query IDs before they are transmitted. The victim Net::DNS instance is then exposed to forged responses injected by the attacker. Note that the deduplication cache in 1.57 has no impact on the feasibility of this attack.

items.title: CVE-2026-131167: pretix offloads certain processes to background tasks that are run by a different server to avoid HTTP workers being clogged with processes that take longer than a usual web reques
items.summary: pretix offloads certain processes to background tasks that are run by a different server to avoid HTTP workers being clogged with processes that take longer than a usual web request. The browser periodically polls the server to see if the task is already finished using a UUID-shaped task ID. Once the task is completed, pretix resumes to the next step of the operation based on the result of the task. The system does however not check if the result stems from the correct type of task. Therefore, an attacker can supply the UUID of a task of a different type and pretix will continue with the result from the wrong task. In most cases, this will just result in an error because the return types do not match up, but in some cases this can be abused to extract objects the attacker usually should not see. Specifically, a vector was discovered that allowed to abuse this for unauthorized access to other people's ticket purchases. The attacker can, however, not control which purchases they get access to.

items.title: CVE-2026-131170: Our payment integration with Stripe did not properly validate payment status responses. An attacker could use a successful payment status response from one payment and supply it to
items.summary: Our payment integration with Stripe did not properly validate payment status responses. An attacker could use a successful payment status response from one payment and supply it to the system for a different payment, gaining access to multiple valid tickets with only one payment. However, the attack requires knowledge of a valid charge ID from the same event which we believe is usually not exposed to users. To simplify attack surface, the fix removes support for incoming webhooks regarding payments created through Stripe's old "source" API. pretix stopped creating payments using this API in 2024.1 for most payment methods and in 2024.9 for all payment methods.

items.title: CISA Adds Four Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.summary: CISA has added four new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action

A browser receiving such a response will parse and render the body as HTML, so any HTML or script embedded in the stored value is executed in the victim's context. items.title: CVE-2026-133660: FlowIntel contains an authorization bypass in its user directory and assignment endpoints that allows authenticated users to access data belonging to other organisations. When the
items.summary: FlowIntel contains an authorization bypass in its user directory and assignment endpoints that allows authenticated users to access data belonging to other organisations. When the LIMIT_USER_VIEW_TO_ORG setting is enabled to restrict directory visibility to the caller's organisation, several API endpoints (user lookup by ID, last name, Matrix ID, and role-based listings) did not consistently enforce the organisation boundary. An authenticated non-admin user could retrieve profiles of users in other organisations by supplying their identifiers. Additionally, OrgAdmin users could retrieve the task assignments of any user in the system, including tasks and case titles from private cases to which they had no access. The assignment endpoints did not verify that the requested user belonged to the caller's organisation or that the underlying cases were visible to the caller. Security impact: - Exposure of user identities (names, Matrix IDs, roles) across organisation boundaries - Disclosure of task assignments, case titles, and workflow details from private cases - Potential enumeration of other organisations' membership and case activity Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0

items.summary: Flowintel , contained a session management vulnerability in its browser authentication mechanism. An attacker who obtained a valid session or remember-me cookie (e.g., through XSS, network interception, or cookie theft) could maintain unauthorized access even after the legitimate user changed their password. items.title: CVE-2026-133658: Flowintel contains a privilege escalation vulnerability in its Matrix relay (bot) integration. When the relay forwarded API requests on behalf of a represented user, the authorizat
items.summary: Flowintel contains a privilege escalation vulnerability in its Matrix relay (bot) integration. When the relay forwarded API requests on behalf of a represented user, the authorization and permission checks evaluated the relay bot's elevated role while the request handlers acted as the lower-privileged represented user. This mismatch allowed users with restricted roles (e.g., Read Only) to perform write operations, directory lookups, calendar modifications, assignment changes, template creation, and import actions they were not authorized to perform. Additionally, relay authority was determined by matching editable user profile fields (name and email) rather than a protected, non-spoofable identifier. An ordinary user who modified their profile to match the expected bot name could be recognized as the trusted relay, enabling impersonation of the bot and potential access to its elevated privileges. Preconditions: - A valid Flowintel user account with a restricted role (e.g., Read Only) - Access to the Matrix relay integration or the ability to send API requests with the relay's API key and a MATRIX-ID header - For the impersonation vector: ability to edit one's own profile name field

This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the site to have granted mc_add_events to Subscriber-level users (a configurable plugin permission), and relies on a privileged user — such as an Administrator — following the event preview link surfaced on the My Calendar Events management screen.

items.title: CVE-2026-119611: The NextGEN Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 4.5.5 via the 'ajax_pagination_referrer' request parameter u
items.summary: The NextGEN Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 4.5.5 via the 'ajax_pagination_referrer' request parameter used on the /ngg_tag/ / taxonomy page. This is due to the plugin reading the pagination base URL from $_REQUEST, preserving the attacker-supplied host on the tag route (where ngg_wprouting_add_post_permalink is forced to false so the plugin does not re-base the links to the site's own permalink), and caching the fully rendered page in a transient keyed only on the request URI (not the request body) for 1800 seconds via NGG_RENDERING_CACHE / PHOTOCRATI_CACHE. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to poison the cached /ngg_tag/ / page so that its pagination links point to an attacker-controlled host; the plugin's own ajax_pagination.

items.summary: The My Calendar – Accessible Event Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'event_street' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.13 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that an administrator has granted the mc_add_events capability to Subscriber-level users via the plugin's Permissions settings; once granted, the Subscriber can store the payload without the mc_edit_locations capability because mc_admin_save() does not enforce it before calling mc_insert_location().

items.title: CVE-2026-120681: The Mang Board plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.7. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user
items.summary: The Mang Board plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.7. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete any board post — including administrator-owned content — along with its associated comments and file links. A nonce sufficient to pass the initial nonce check is publicly exposed on any board listing page, meaning no prior authentication or privileged access is required to initiate the exploit.

items.summary: The Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes – NextGEN Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.5.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. items.summary: The My Calendar – Accessible Event Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'event_title' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.13 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. items.title: CVE-2026-133626: FlowIntel contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in its file-to-note conversion feature. When a user converts an attached CSV or JSON file into a case note, the application r
items.summary: FlowIntel contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in its file-to-note conversion feature. When a user converts an attached CSV or JSON file into a case note, the application renders the data as a Markdown table by padding every row to the maximum column count. A crafted file with a small number of filled cells but a very large number of columns (or keys) causes the application to allocate a quadratic number of padded table cells, potentially exhausting a worker process in memory or CPU. The same issue affects nested JSON values rendered inside table cells, where pretty-printed indentation further inflates the output size. Preconditions: - An authenticated user with access to a case in FlowIntel - Ability to attach and convert a CSV or JSON file to a note Impact: - Denial of service: exhaustion of a worker process, potentially disrupting service for other users - No confidentiality or integrity impact Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0

items.title: CVE-2026-133627: flowintel contains a log injection vulnerability in its case history (audit log) subsystem. The case history is stored as a line-delimited file where each line represents a single
items.summary: flowintel contains a log injection vulnerability in its case history (audit log) subsystem. The case history is stored as a line-delimited file where each line represents a single event attributed to a specific user. User-controlled fields, including user names, event messages, and case titles used during case merging, were written to the history file without sanitizing embedded line separator characters (such as carriage return, line feed, vertical tab, form feed, and Unicode line/paragraph separators). An authenticated user with the ability to create or modify case history entries could embed line separators in these fields. Upon writing, the injected separators would split a single intended entry into multiple lines, each of which the history format interprets as a distinct event. This allows an attacker to forge additional history entries attributed to arbitrary users, corrupting the audit trail and undermining the integrity of case records. The vulnerability affects the case history append and merge operations. No authentication bypass or privilege escalation is required beyond normal case-management access. Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

items.title: CVE-2026-133620: Flowintel's template repository subsystem did not adequately constrain file access to the configured repository base directory. Two related weaknesses existed: - Repository regist
items.summary: Flowintel's template repository subsystem did not adequately constrain file access to the configured repository base directory. Two related weaknesses existed: - Repository registration and editing accepted arbitrary local paths without verifying they resolved inside the configured REPOSITORY_BASE_PATH, allowing an authenticated user to point a repository at any readable directory on the host. - Manifest and template file lookups used normalized (non-canonical) path joins and a startswith-based guard that could be bypassed by symbolic links, permitting reads of files outside the intended repository. An authenticated user with the ability to add or edit a template repository could therefore cause the application to read and return the contents of arbitrary files readable by the service account, including configuration files, credentials, or other sensitive data. Affected: Flowintel versions prior to 4.1.0.

items.title: CVE-2026-133622: A flaw was found in certmonger. This vulnerability allows a malicious certificate authority or an attacker positioned on an unencrypted network to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) b
items.summary: A flaw was found in certmonger. This vulnerability allows a malicious certificate authority or an attacker positioned on an unencrypted network to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending oversized or deliberately slow responses. Certmonger fails to enforce size limits or transfer timeouts when downloading and buffering Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol (SCEP) replies over HTTP. Consequently, an attacker can exhaust host memory, drive CPU usage to capacity, or cause certificate requests to hang indefinitely.

items.title: CVE-2026-133531: A flaw was found in cluster-network-operator. The OVN IPsec certificate signer does not verify that the requested certificate Subject and DNS names belong to the requesting node. A
items.summary: A flaw was found in cluster-network-operator. The OVN IPsec certificate signer does not verify that the requested certificate Subject and DNS names belong to the requesting node. An attacker with an accepted OVN node credential and permission to submit certificate signing requests could obtain a signed certificate identifying another node. In certificate authenticated OVN IPsec deployments, this could enable peer impersonation when the attacker can also satisfy the configured peer address check, potentially compromising protected traffic.

items.title: CVE-2026-129840: In the nrfconnect/ncs-zigbee repository, the GitHub Actions workflow .github/workflows/build_documentation.yml used the pull_request_target trigger while checking out and executing
items.summary: In the nrfconnect/ncs-zigbee repository, the GitHub Actions workflow .github/workflows/build_documentation.yml used the pull_request_target trigger while checking out and executing untrusted pull request code. This allowed a pull request from a fork to run attacker-controlled code in the base repository context with a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN (contents: write, pages: write, pull-requests: write), enabling remote code execution in CI, token exfiltration, and unauthorized modification of repository content and GitHub Pages. The workflow was disabled and then rewritten to remove the issue.

items.title: CVE-2026-130010: The Chatterbug Forms – Fast, Flexible WordPress Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the cbforms_d
items.summary: The Chatterbug Forms – Fast, Flexible WordPress Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the cbforms_delete_uploaded_files function in all versions up to, and including, 1.1 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). Exploitation requires an administrator to delete the attacker-planted form entry, and the attacker must know or be able to guess the absolute path of a file writable by the PHP process. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The fv_player_db_save AJAX endpoint's INSERT path is gated only by a per-user preview nonce and never calls current_user_can(), allowing any authenticated subscriber-level user who possesses their own nonce to store the malicious payload. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with contributor-level access and above.

items.title: CVE-2026-99804: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/io-wq: save worker type before dropping its reference io_wq_cancel_tw_create() inspects cb->func afte
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/io-wq: save worker type before dropping its reference io_wq_cancel_tw_create() inspects cb->func after calling io_worker_cancel_cb(). For an existing worker, that call can drop the last worker reference and wake io_worker_exit(). If the canceling task is preempted, the worker can be unlinked and freed by kfree_rcu() before the callback function is inspected. KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free read in this path. Save whether the callback belongs to an unpublished continuation worker while its reference is still held, then use the saved result for the conditional free. This preserves the existing accounting and frees only the worker allocated for the canceled continuation.

items.title: CVE-2026-99796: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/poll: cancel all matching requests in one pass With IORING_ASYNC_CANCEL_ALL, __io_async_cancel() call
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/poll: cancel all matching requests in one pass With IORING_ASYNC_CANCEL_ALL, __io_async_cancel() calls io_try_cancel() until nothing is found, and io_poll_cancel() cancels one request per call, starting each lookup at the beginning of the hash. A cancelled request stays hashed until its task work runs, so every lookup walks past the ones already cancelled. Cancelling K of N pending polls visits about K*N/2 requests in one io_uring_enter(), with uring_lock held. A single CANCEL_FD|ALL on 80000 polls on one eventfd takes 17.06s, 0.02s with this change. With voluntary preemption the soft lockup watchdog fires: watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#1 stuck for 26s! [repro:100] RIP: 0010:io_cancel_req_match+0x19/0xa0 io_poll_cancel+0x73/0x170 io_try_cancel+0x7b/0xf0 __io_async_cancel+0x41/0x110 Walk the hash once and cancel every match, as io_cancel_remove() does for futex and waitid. Cancel by user_data only needs its own bucket. __io_async_cancel() still loops until nothing is found, so a request that io-wq parks in the poll hash meanwhile is still cancelled. A cancel that matches one request now walks the whole h

items.title: CVE-2026-99797: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/cancel: drop sqd->lock while SQPOLL waits An exiting SQPOLL thread calls io_uring_cancel_generic() wi
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/cancel: drop sqd->lock while SQPOLL waits An exiting SQPOLL thread calls io_uring_cancel_generic() with sqd->lock held, and keeps it across cond_resched() and the sleep until nothing is in flight anymore. A zero-copy send notification can't be canceled and stays pending as long as the peer doesn't read, so the lock is held for as long as a user cares to. io_ring_exit_work() needs it to park the thread, and so do IORING_REGISTER_IOWQ_AFF and IOWQ_MAX_WORKERS. With 64 such rings sharing the thread, every iou_exit slot sleeps on the lock and no ring gets freed for anyone. Drop the lock around cond_resched() and the sleep, like the main loop of the thread does. Each walk of ctx_list is still under one hold, and nothing is kept across the unlock. The thread drops its io-wq, frees its tctx and clears sqd->thread under one hold after the loop, so whoever holds the lock and finds sqd->thread set can still use them. [axboe: adapted to the schedule_timeout() based loop]

items.title: CVE-2026-99798: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring: defer foreign io-wq enqueues to task_work An IOPOLL ring without DEFER_TASKRUN can be reaped by a ta
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring: defer foreign io-wq enqueues to task_work An IOPOLL ring without DEFER_TASKRUN can be reaped by a task other than the one that submitted the I/O. If a polled request is marked REQ_F_REISSUE, io_free_batch_list() calls io_queue_iowq() with the original tctx. Ordinary task exit can tear down tctx->io_wq after draining only the tracked requests. The live request pins the task, but not its io-wq, so the foreign task can race io_wq_put_and_exit() and enqueue through a freed or NULL queue. Forward foreign userspace enqueues to the owning task before accessing tctx->io_wq. Use a dedicated task_work callback so reissues still go straight to io-wq, and fail them if task_work is running in cancellation mode. Preserve the existing PF_KTHREAD cancellation path. This also covers the other callers of io_queue_iowq() without changing the worker-owned enqueue path.

items.title: CVE-2026-99799: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/sqpoll: don't wait for the thread to exit io_sq_thread_stop() wakes the SQPOLL thread and waits for i
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/sqpoll: don't wait for the thread to exit io_sq_thread_stop() wakes the SQPOLL thread and waits for it to exit. The thread belongs to the thread group that created the ring, so a SIGSTOP or the cgroup freezer holds it in get_signal(), and the wake up doesn't change that. io_ring_exit_work() then sleeps in that wait until someone continues or kills the process. iou_exit has 64 slots, so 64 closed SQPOLL rings of a stopped process keep every other ring from being freed, for everyone. Don't wait. Set the stop bit, wake the thread, and let it exit when it gets to run again. The sqd can now outlive its last ring, so give it a second refcount with one reference for the rings and one for the thread, and free it with the last one. The thread can't reach a freed ring, rings leave ctx_list before dropping their reference, and the io-wq hash is refcounted.

items.title: CVE-2026-99800: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring: free the task context after a grace period A task other than the owner can free a request, io_ring_e
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring: free the task context after a grace period A task other than the owner can free a request, io_ring_exit_work() running the local task_work of a DEFER_TASKRUN ring for example, or io_do_iopoll() reaping completions. io_put_task() then takes the else branch: percpu_counter_sub(&tctx->inflight, 1); if (unlikely(atomic_read(&tctx->in_cancel))) wake_up(&tctx->wait); put_task_struct(tctx->task); The first line is what lets the owner leave io_uring_cancel_generic(), and on exec it frees the tctx right after. Nothing holds that off for the remaining three lines, the task reference only covers a tctx freed along with the task_struct. It used to work out because io_uring_del_tctx_node() took the uring_lock that the freeing side holds across io_put_task(), until that moved to tctx_lock. Free the tctx with kfree_rcu(), and enter an RCU read section in io_put_task() before the count is dropped.

items.title: CVE-2026-99801: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/bpf-ops: clear bpf_ctx while submitting SQEs bpf_io_uring_submit_sqes() calls io_submit_sqes() from i
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/bpf-ops: clear bpf_ctx while submitting SQEs bpf_io_uring_submit_sqes() calls io_submit_sqes() from inside the loop program, with current->bpf_ctx set, and requests issued inline run with it set too. The socket code uses has_current_bpf_ctx() to recognize calls from bpf_setsockopt() and friends, where the caller holds the socket lock and has already been vetted, and skips both. So a SOCKET_URING_OP_SETSOCKOPT from the SQ passes sockopt_capable() without the capability, and runs without lock_sock(). A task with no capability can set SO_MARK, IP_TRANSPARENT or TCP_REPAIR, and two threads changing IP_OPTIONS on one socket, one through the ring, double free in no time. SOCK_DESTROY via IORING_OP_SENDMSG ends up in tcp_abort() without the lock the same way. Clear the run context around io_submit_sqes(). The SQEs come from userspace and must be issued like those of any other ring. They still run inside the program's RCU tasks trace read section, so a request that sleeps there holds up that grace period, but other request types do that already.

items.title: CVE-2026-99802: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/register: enforce per-task restrictions in io_uring_register_blind() When io_uring_register(2) is inv
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/register: enforce per-task restrictions in io_uring_register_blind() When io_uring_register(2) is invoked with fd == -1, it dispatches directly to io_uring_register_blind() without checking current->io_uring_restrict. As a result, a task with per-task register restrictions installed via IORING_REGISTER_RESTRICTIONS can still invoke blind registration opcodes such as IORING_REGISTER_SEND_MSG_RING even when those opcodes are not in the task's allowed register_op bitmap. Check current->io_uring_restrict->register_op in io_uring_register_blind() before dispatching blind registration opcodes.

items.title: CVE-2026-99803: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/net: mask socket type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK in io_socket_bpf_populate() When an IORING_OP_SOCKET reques
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/net: mask socket type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK in io_socket_bpf_populate() When an IORING_OP_SOCKET request is prepared in io_socket_prep(), sock->type retains creation flags such as SOCK_CLOEXEC and SOCK_NONBLOCK until __sys_socket_file() masks them off with SOCK_TYPE_MASK during execution. However, io_socket_bpf_populate() copies sock->type into bctx->socket.type without masking off ~SOCK_TYPE_MASK. As a result, a cBPF filter inspecting bctx->socket.type against socket types such as SOCK_DGRAM or SOCK_STREAM can be bypassed by ORing SOCK_CLOEXEC or SOCK_NONBLOCK into the socket type. Mask sock->type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK when populating bctx->socket.type.

items.title: CVE-2026-89095: The Shortcodes and extra features for Phlox theme plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 2.17.22 via the 'extra_template_p
items.summary: The Shortcodes and extra features for Phlox theme plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 2.17.22 via the 'extra_template_path' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. This can be used to bypass access controls, obtain sensitive data, or achieve code execution in cases where .php file types can be uploaded and included. The slug-based allowlist introduced as the fix for CVE-2023-37888 constrains only the template_part_file filename suffix and does not validate the extra_template_path directory component, meaning path traversal sequences are fully functional against this parameter.

items.title: CVE-2026-133613: Flowintel's community data launcher script passes the admin API key as a command-line argument to a child Python helper process. On Unix-like systems, process arguments are readabl
items.summary: Flowintel's community data launcher script passes the admin API key as a command-line argument to a child Python helper process. On Unix-like systems, process arguments are readable by all local users via standard tools such as ps or by reading /proc/ /cmdline, allowing any local user to observe the key while the helper process is running. An attacker with local access to the host can capture the admin API key during the brief window in which the helper process is active. Possession of the key grants full administrative access to the Flowintel REST API, enabling unauthorized creation, modification, or deletion of threat intelligence data, users, roles, and organisations. Preconditions: - The victim must invoke the community data import or deletion command (launch.sh -tdc or -dtdc) with the API key supplied as a positional argument. - The attacker must have a local user account on the same host and be able to observe process listings during the helper execution window. Impact: - Disclosure of the Flowintel admin API key to any local user. - Subsequent full administrative control over the Flowintel instance via its REST API. Affected: <4.1.0

items.summary: A vulnerability was found in Vahe1994 AQLM up to e79a896ed6656fe4ed06193d42d004e7d0bbdbb2. The affected element is an unknown function of the file inference_kernels/triton_kernel.py of the component Triton Kernel. items.title: CVE-2026-133505: When message history is serialized and loaded again, a tool result that contains a JSON object in the serialized shape of one of Pydantic AI's file types is rebuilt as that file. A
items.summary: When message history is serialized and loaded again, a tool result that contains a JSON object in the serialized shape of one of Pydantic AI's file types is rebuilt as that file. A third party who controls data a tool returns, such as a record that an MCP server or a function tool returns from an external system, can use this to make the application download a URL on its local network, or make the model provider read an s3:// object or uploaded file with the application's credentials. Applications are affected when tool results can contain third-party data, message history containing those results is serialized and loaded again (stored history, history a UI adapter holds on the server, or Temporal, DBOS or Prefect durable execution), and the model is one Pydantic AI downloads files for, one that honors force_download, or one whose provider resolves non-HTTP file URLs or uploaded files. History that a client submits through the Vercel AI or AG-UI adapter in the default mode is not affected. The issue is fixed in pydantic-ai and pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.10 and 2.66.0.

items.title: CVE-2026-133611: vulnerability-lookup prior to version 7.1.0 contains two security issues in its web interface. First, the /user/toggle_2fa endpoint accepted HTTP GET requests and disabled the auth
items.summary: vulnerability-lookup prior to version 7.1.0 contains two security issues in its web interface. First, the /user/toggle_2fa endpoint accepted HTTP GET requests and disabled the authenticated user's two-factor authentication without requiring password confirmation. Because the state-changing operation was reachable via GET, an attacker with a basic account could embed an image element (or any other GET-triggering markup) in a comment pointing to that endpoint. When a victim with 2FA enabled viewed the comment, their browser silently issued the GET request, disabling the victim's second factor of authentication. No CSRF token was enforced on the GET path, and no password was required to confirm the action. Second, the comment detail page (/comment/ ) rendered unpublished comments to any visitor who possessed the URL, bypassing the moderation workflow that was intended to keep such content hidden until approved. The API correctly restricted access, but the web view did not enforce the same authorization check. The combined effect allows an attacker to degrade a victim's account security (removal of 2FA) through a single page view and to read content that was not yet approved for public

items.title: CVE-2026-133421: Validating an untrusted ISO 8601 duration string into a timedelta field with Pydantic V1 takes quadratic time: an input of a few dozen kilobytes takes seconds to validate. The iso
items.summary: Validating an untrusted ISO 8601 duration string into a timedelta field with Pydantic V1 takes quadratic time: an input of a few dozen kilobytes takes seconds to validate. The iso8601_duration_re regular expression used to parse ISO 8601 durations (in pydantic/datetime_parse.py) contains an unescaped ".", which also matches digits. On a string of digits, the repeated groups overlap and the regex engine backtracks in quadratic time. The issue was fixed in commit 62791e66a9f8f118e465ed760c9e2ede9ae3055e. Users relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2 should upgrade to 2.14.2 or later. Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted strings into timedelta fields.

items.title: CVE-2026-133422: Validating an untrusted list into a field constrained with unique_items=True with Pydantic V1 takes quadratic time: an input of a few hundred kilobytes takes seconds to validate.
items.summary: Validating an untrusted list into a field constrained with unique_items=True with Pydantic V1 takes quadratic time: an input of a few hundred kilobytes takes seconds to validate. The ConstrainedList.unique_items_validator validator (in pydantic/types.py) checks each item against all the following ones. For a list with no duplicates (the common, valid case), this results in a quadratic number of comparisons. The issue was fixed in commit 6ec75e57f277a820ec583e601167f25fe8dc7c87. Users relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2 should upgrade to 2.14.2 or later. Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted lists into fields constrained with unique_items=True (using conlist() or Field()). The fix only applies to lists of builtin scalar types (int, float, str, bytes, bool and None), for which duplicates can be detected in linear time. Lists of other types (e.g. models or dictionaries) are still checked in quadratic time, as their items aren't guaranteed to be hashable: bound their size using the max_items constraint. Pydantic V2 models are not affected.

items.title: CVE-2026-133424: When extra data is allowed, providing both the alias and the name of an aliased TypedDict or dataclass field makes the unvalidated value (provided under the name) overwrite the val
items.summary: When extra data is allowed, providing both the alias and the name of an aliased TypedDict or dataclass field makes the unvalidated value (provided under the name) overwrite the validated one (provided under the alias), resulting in validated data not matching the declared type. Extra items are stored in the same dictionary as the fields (the returned dictionary for TypedDict, the instance __dict__ for dataclasses). As only the alias is marked as used, the field name is treated as an extra item, and its unvalidated value overrides the validated one. The TypedDict validator (pydantic-core/src/validators/typed_dict.rs) and the dataclass validator (pydantic-core/src/validators/dataclass.rs) share this logic. The issue was fixed in commit 34491f5328f168f14e3769cd5f0f83c0af0f4778. Impact: validation bypass, as data returned by validation doesn't match the declared type. Affected are applications validating untrusted data into TypedDict or dataclass types with aliased fields and extra data allowed (with extra='allow', or with the extra_items argument for TypedDict), using Pydantic V2 (up to and including 2.14.1). Pydantic models (BaseModel) are not affected, as extra data is stored separa

items.title: CVE-2026-133426: Validating an untrusted string in exponent notation into a Fraction field computes the full power of ten without any bound: an input of a few bytes takes seconds to validate. Stri
items.summary: Validating an untrusted string in exponent notation into a Fraction field computes the full power of ten without any bound: an input of a few bytes takes seconds to validate. String inputs are passed to the Fraction constructor. For strings in exponent notation (e.g. '1e8000000'), CPython computes the corresponding power of ten as an integer (in Lib/fractions.py). The issue was fixed in commit 69ed168e9ad465eef4c8d81efb152a93b604daf5. For strings in exponent notation, the exponent is now parsed before calling the Fraction constructor, and exponents larger than 4300 (in absolute value) are rejected. Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted strings into Fraction fields (in both JSON and Python mode, including in strict mode), using Pydantic from 2.10.0 up to (but excluding) 2.14.0. From 2.14.0, exponents larger than 4300 (in absolute value) are rejected, matching the maximum number of digits accepted for integers.

items.title: CVE-2026-133428: Validating an untrusted URL with a long scheme and many hosts into a multi-host URL field (e.g. PostgresDsn) takes quadratic time and memory: an input of about a hundred kilobytes
items.summary: Validating an untrusted URL with a long scheme and many hosts into a multi-host URL field (e.g. PostgresDsn) takes quadratic time and memory: an input of about a hundred kilobytes takes around a gigabyte of memory to validate. The parse_multihost_url() function (in pydantic-core/src/validators/url.rs) parses each host separately, prepending the whole URL prefix (including the scheme) to every one of them. As the scheme can be arbitrarily long, and is parsed and stored once per host, both time and memory grow quadratically with the input size. Allowed schemes (e.g. postgres for PostgresDsn) are only checked after parsing, so they don't prevent the issue. The issue was fixed in commit b4028f9d87e34750e53be0ba011d70f3c0fcc94e. Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted strings into multi-host URL fields (PostgresDsn, MongoDsn, NatsDsn, or custom types built on MultiHostUrl).

items.title: CVE-2026-133429: When validating JSON data into a model allowing extra data, the keys of extra data aren't validated against the key type annotated on __pydantic_extra__, resulting in extra data no
items.summary: When validating JSON data into a model allowing extra data, the keys of extra data aren't validated against the key type annotated on __pydantic_extra__, resulting in extra data not matching the declared type. This is the case if you define __pydantic_extra__ as e.g. dict[Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r'^x_')], int]. The validate_json_by_iteration() method (in pydantic-core/src/validators/model_fields.rs), used to validate JSON data into models, only validates the values of extra data, and stores the keys as is. The issue was fixed in commit 4c65dbda9970a488e2ff21c8693fc6f6d70a3358. Impact: validation bypass, as extra data returned by validation doesn't match the declared type. Affected are applications validating untrusted JSON data into models allowing extra data (with extra='allow'), with a key type annotated on __pydantic_extra__ (e.g. dict[Annotated[str, Field(pattern=...)], int]), using Pydantic from 2.13.0 up to (but excluding) 2.14.2. Python mode validation isn't affected.

items.summary: A flaw was found in the Kuadrant WebAssembly (WASM) shim shipped in Red Hat Connectivity Link 1.5. items.title: CVE-2026-99795: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: cxl/features: Ensure that count is set before access to ent[] __counted_by() get_supported_features() assigns
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: cxl/features: Ensure that count is set before access to ent[] __counted_by() get_supported_features() assigns entries->num_features only after the memcpy() loop that fills entries->ent[] has already run. Since ent[] is __counted_by(num_features), the compiler's bounds instrumentation sees a 0-length array during that loop and FORTIFY_SOURCE trips on the memcpy. Set @num_features right after allocation, before any write into ent[], so the bound is correct for the whole lifetime of the array. This was found via a fortify panic: memcpy: detected buffer overflow: 384 byte write of buffer size 0 WARNING: lib/string_helpers.c:1035 at __fortify_report+0x54/0xa0 kernel BUG at lib/string_helpers.c:1043! Call trace: __fortify_panic+0x10/0x18 get_supported_features.isra.0+0x4a0/0x4d0 [cxl_core] devm_cxl_setup_features+0x84/0x120 [cxl_core] cxl_pci_probe+0x254/0x5e0 [cxl_pci] Same class of bug, same fix shape as commit 6c9d2e87df40 ("cxl/fwctl: Fix __fortify_panic"), which fixed the analogous issue in cxlctl_get_supported_features() but missed this one. items.title: CVE-2026-99788: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ACPI: CPPC: Validate FFH register fields before hardware access The x86 CPPC FFH accessors construct masks and

A zero-width field or a field extending beyond bit 63 can therefore cause an invalid shift. The safe MSR accessors only handle an access fault, not invalid field arithmetic after a successful read. Also, the 64-bit GAS address is implicitly narrowed to the 32-bit MSR number. A descriptor with nonzero upper address bits can access a different MSR from the one described by firmware. The arm64 AMU counter readers have the same unchecked field arithmetic. Validate the field bounds before reading a counter, including both descriptors in the paired counter path. Dispatch FFH accesses before decoding the GAS Access Size in the common read and write paths. Otherwise, a large access_width can trigger an invalid shift in GET_BIT_WIDTH() before the architecture validates its register. That field has architecture-specific FFH semantics and is not needed by the generic memory/port accessor on this path. Validate x

items.title: CVE-2026-99789: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: block: restore the iterator when rejecting a misaligned bio bio_iov_iter_get_pages() can extract some iovecs b
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: block: restore the iterator when rejecting a misaligned bio bio_iov_iter_get_pages() can extract some iovecs before encountering a misaligned one. It releases the pages and rejects the entire bio, but leaves the supplied iterator advanced. An iomap direct-I/O caller may subsequently reexpand the iterator's byte count and fall back to buffered I/O. The reexpanded count then includes bytes before the iterator's current segment, potentially causing iterate_iovec() to read beyond the imported iovec array. In a reproducer using an initial empty iovec followed by 10-byte and 1015-byte segments, writev() returned 1015 instead of 1025 and KASAN reported an 8-byte read beyond the nine-element iovec allocation. Saving and restoring the iterator on the rejected-bio path makes writev() return 1025 and eliminates the KASAN report. Restore the entire iterator rather than reverting a byte count: advancing past an empty segment changes its position without consuming any bytes. Leave successful and partially accepted bio paths unchanged.

items.title: CVE-2026-99790: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: stop registering with rpcbind after a failure in listener_set nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() calls svc_xprt
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: stop registering with rpcbind after a failure in listener_set nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() calls svc_xprt_create_from_sa() once for each requested listener and passes flags of 0, so every listener registers with rpcbind on its own. A rpcbind that accepts the connection and never replies therefore costs one timeout for each entry. With the cap of 1024 entries the request can hold nfsd_mutex for about 34 minutes, which is roughly 17 times the hung-task threshold. One failure is enough to know that the next call will not fare better. Read svc_rpcb_failure_count() before the create loop, and pass SVC_SOCK_ANONYMOUS for the rest of the request once the count moves.

items.title: CVE-2026-99792: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb/server: prevent file publication after tree disconnect TREE_DISCONNECT closes the tree's published file ha
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb/server: prevent file publication after tree disconnect TREE_DISCONNECT closes the tree's published file handles before marking and removing the tree connection. A concurrent CREATE that already holds a tree reference can therefore publish its file after the close pass. When CREATE drops its reference, the tree can be freed while the published file still points to it. Mark and remove the tree connection before closing its files, and serialize both new-open and durable-reconnect volatile ID publication with that state transition. An opener is then either published in time for the close pass or rejected after disconnect with STATUS_NETWORK_NAME_DELETED. Keep a tree reference while a file carries its tree pointer. This protects asynchronous users that can defer the file's final destruction past tree disconnect. The close pass can race the successful FP_NEW to FP_INITED transition. Take the opening request's file reference atomically with that transition. This keeps the file alive until request completion even if teardown removes the ID immediately. items.title: CVE-2026-99793: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Only accept connection responses to outstanding requests An outgoing channel waits in BT_CON
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Only accept connection responses to outstanding requests An outgoing channel waits in BT_CONNECT until security and the feature mask exchange complete, and only then sends its connection request. A peer can answer it before that with a connection response matching our source CID. The channel then moves to BT_CONFIG, completes configuration and becomes connected before security has completed. If security then fails, l2cap_security_cfm() leaves the connected channel alone, so it stays up on a link that did not reach the required security level. A connection response with a zero source CID is matched by identifier. Another channel can hold the same identifier for a response it still has to send, so the lookup can pick the wrong channel. Only accept a connection response while our request is outstanding, and only look at such channels when matching by identifier.

items.title: CVE-2026-99794: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject signalling responses in invalid states A peer can send configuration messages while a
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject signalling responses in invalid states A peer can send configuration messages while an incoming channel is in BT_CONNECT2, before the security or deferred accept gate has completed. A configuration response can then promote the channel to BT_CONNECTED. Configuration responses can also act on channels that are closing, and a late connection response can move a disconnecting channel back to BT_CONFIG. Accept connection responses only while waiting in BT_CONNECT. Answer configuration requests in BT_CONNECT2, but defer our own request until BT_CONFIG so configuration cannot complete before the gate. Ignore configuration responses outside BT_CONFIG and BT_CONNECTED, and only complete configuration in BT_CONFIG.

items.title: CVE-2026-99783: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/9p/usbg: Fix use-after-free in disable_usb9pfs() disable_usb9pfs() frees the IN and OUT usb_request object
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/9p/usbg: Fix use-after-free in disable_usb9pfs() disable_usb9pfs() frees the IN and OUT usb_request objects before it disables the corresponding endpoints. If either request is still queued, the later usb_ep_disable() call cancels the endpoint queue and the UDC driver can still access the already freed request. With dummy_hcd and KASAN, this is reproducible by queueing the OUT request and then disconnecting the configfs gadget: BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in dummy_disable+0x2b4/0x300 Read of size 8 at addr ffff888009702400 by task sh/1 usb_ep_disable+0x8e/0x1f0 usb9pfs_func_unbind+0x193/0x350 gadget_dev_desc_UDC_store+0x135/0x280 dummy_free_request() also warns because the request is freed while its queue entry is still linked. Disable both endpoints before freeing the request objects. This lets usb_ep_disable() cancel any queued transfers and invoke the completion callback while the request storage is still valid. The request objects are then freed only after they have been removed from the endpoint queues.

items.title: CVE-2026-99784: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: 9p/xen: fix refcount leak in p9_xen_response() on wrong tag p9_xen_response() looks up the request for an inco
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: 9p/xen: fix refcount leak in p9_xen_response() on wrong tag p9_xen_response() looks up the request for an incoming reply with p9_tag_lookup(), which takes a reference on the returned p9_req_t. When the tag does not resolve to a request in REQ_STATUS_SENT, the function warns and continues the loop without dropping that reference, permanently leaking the p9_req_t and its msize buffers. The reply header, including the tag, is supplied by the backend, so a malicious or buggy 9P backend can leak kernel memory on every crafted response. Drop the reference before continuing.

items.title: CVE-2026-99785: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: 9p/trans_virtio: reject mount tags longer than NAME_MAX at probe p9_virtio_probe() reads a 16-bit mount tag le
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: 9p/trans_virtio: reject mount tags longer than NAME_MAX at probe p9_virtio_probe() reads a 16-bit mount tag length (tag_len) from the device config and kzalloc()s tag_len + 1 bytes for chan->tag with no upper bound. A malicious or compromised host can present a tag of up to 65535 bytes; that tag is later copied into the single-page sysfs buffer by p9_mount_tag_show() (memcpy(buf, chan->tag, tag_len + 1)), a host-controlled out-of-bounds write of up to ~64 KiB past the PAGE_SIZE attribute buffer. Reject an overlong tag at probe time. A 9p mount tag is a name-like identifier, so bound it by NAME_MAX (255): that limit is independent of the sysfs/seq_file page size and is far above any legitimate mount tag, which keeps p9_mount_tag_show() safe at the root without hard-coding a seq_file implementation detail.

items.title: CVE-2026-99786: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfrm: retry inexact policy lookup after node reinsertion An inexact policy lookup first records pointers to ca
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfrm: retry inexact policy lookup after node reinsertion An inexact policy lookup first records pointers to candidate hlist heads and then traverses the lists. A concurrent policy insertion can merge inexact tree nodes between those operations: lookup policy insertion ------ ---------------- find inexact candidates save obsolete hlist head write_seqcount_begin(&bin->count) merge inexact tree nodes hlist_del_rcu(&policy->bydst) reinsert policy->bydst in survivor write_seqcount_end(&bin->count) evaluate saved candidate list miss the moved policy The merge immediately reinserts the same hlist node into the surviving tree node. RCU keeps the policy alive, but it does not provide a consistent view while its list node is moved. A lookup that selected the obsolete list can observe it empty. A lookup already traversing a moved policy can instead follow the next pointer rewritten by the reinsertion. Either case can return an incorrect IPsec policy result. The per-bin sequence counter already brackets calls to xfrm_policy_inexact_insert_node(), including node merges. The read side, however, currently validates the counter on

items.title: CVE-2026-99787: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: cpufreq: CPPC: Select the frequency-invariance callback per CPU cppc_cpufreq_cpu_fie_init() initializes deferr
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: cpufreq: CPPC: Select the frequency-invariance callback per CPU cppc_cpufreq_cpu_fie_init() initializes deferred work only for CPUs whose feedback counters use PCC. However, if any CPU in a shared policy uses PCC, it installs the PCC tick callback for the entire policy. With FIE enabled, a non-PCC CPU then queues an uninitialized irq_work and can call a NULL function pointer when that work runs. Choose the frequency-invariance callback separately for each CPU using the recorded work-initialization state. Processor removal can unpublish the CPC descriptor before callback registration, so querying its counter transport again can incorrectly select direct reads for a PCC CPU. Register the callbacks after all counter initialization has completed, so a failed initial read for an online CPU cannot leave a partially registered policy. PCC CPUs use their initialized deferred work, while non-PCC CPUs read their own counters directly from the tick.

items.title: CVE-2026-99773: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/drm_crtc: ensure dma_fence_ops remain valid during device unbind In [1], sashiko reported the following is
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/drm_crtc: ensure dma_fence_ops remain valid during device unbind In [1], sashiko reported the following issue: === snip === Looking at how these fences are managed, drm_crtc_create_fence() creates a dma_fence without taking a reference to the drm_device or drm_crtc. Because the sync_file framework exposes this fence to userspace, the fence can outlive the CRTC. The dma_fence contract requires that data accessed by dma_fence_ops (like get_driver_name) must remain valid for an RCU grace period after the fence is signaled. However, drm_crtc_cleanup() and the subsequent freeing of the device do not wait for an RCU grace period via synchronize_rcu(). items.title: CVE-2026-99774: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfrm: espintcp: reorder operations within espintcp_init_sk When enabled on a socket, espintcp sets the socket
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfrm: espintcp: reorder operations within espintcp_init_sk When enabled on a socket, espintcp sets the socket callbacks to its own before it has finished setting up its context and published it as icsk_ulp_data. Any one of those callbacks that gets called before will dereference a NULL icsk_ulp_data. Fix this by reording the operations, and add memory barriers to ensure callers will have a struct espintcp_ctx available. Add a few WRITE_ONCE/READ_ONCE too while we're there.

items.title: CVE-2026-99775: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfrm: interface: validate the IP header on xmit Packets injected into an xfrm interface (e.g. AF_PACKET on an
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfrm: interface: validate the IP header on xmit Packets injected into an xfrm interface (e.g. AF_PACKET on an xfrmi device) reach the xfrm output path without IP header validation, but xfrm4_transport_output() uses iph->ihl for __skb_pull() and memmove() and expects the header to be valid. vti_tunnel_xmit() already calls pskb_inet_may_pull() before handing packets to the xfrm output path. Do the same in xfrmi_xmit() and perform the header checks ip_rcv_core()/ip6_rcv_core() do on entry to the IP stack: reject wrong IP versions and malformed IPv4 header lengths.

items.title: CVE-2026-99776: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/9p/usbg: clear stale client pointer on close p9_usbg_close() tears down the client transport, but usb9pfs
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/9p/usbg: clear stale client pointer on close p9_usbg_close() tears down the client transport, but usb9pfs keeps using usb9pfs->client from asynchronous TX and RX completion handlers. A late completion can therefore dereference a client that has already been freed during mount teardown. Clear usb9pfs->client under usb9pfs->lock when closing the transport, detach any pending TX request from in_req->context, and make the TX/RX completion handlers bail out once the transport has been detached. This keeps late completions from touching a freed or rebound p9_client.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/9p/usbg: remove bogus context initialization in alloc_requests alloc_requests() initializes usb9pfs->in_req->context to point at the struct f_usb9pfs instance itself. usb9pfs_queue_tx() later overwrites this with the real struct p9_req_t pointer before every transmit, and usb9pfs_tx_complete() clears it back to NULL after each completion, so in_req->context only ever holds a valid p9_req_t once a request has actually been queued. usb9pfs_clear_tx(), however, can run at any time (mount close, gadget disable) independent of whether a request was ever queued. This reliably corrupts memory or panics whenever the transport is torn down before any 9p request has been transmitted, e.g. mounting and immediately unmounting, or a cable disconnect racing the very first request. usb9pfs->out_req->context is set t

items.title: CVE-2026-99778: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/9p/usbg: fix out_req buffer leak in disable_usb9pfs usb9pfs->out_req is allocated with alloc_ep_req(), whi
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/9p/usbg: fix out_req buffer leak in disable_usb9pfs usb9pfs->out_req is allocated with alloc_ep_req(), which also allocates the request's data buffer (req->buf). disable_usb9pfs() frees it with plain usb_ep_free_request(), which only frees the usb_request structure itself and leaks req->buf on every close. Use free_ep_req() instead, matching the allocator, as documented by its own comment ("Requests allocated via alloc_ep_req() *must* be freed by free_ep_req()").

items.title: CVE-2026-99779: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/9p/usbg: call disable_usb9pfs() from usb9pfs_disable() usb9pfs_disable() is the usb_function ->disable cal
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/9p/usbg: call disable_usb9pfs() from usb9pfs_disable() usb9pfs_disable() is the usb_function ->disable callback, invoked by the composite gadget core whenever the host resets or unconfigures the gadget. The gadget function API requires this callback to disable its endpoints; every other in-tree function driver does so from its ->disable hook. usb9pfs_disable() never called disable_usb9pfs(), so the IN/OUT endpoints and their usb_request objects were left active and allocated across a host-driven disable. When the host later reconfigures the device, enable_usb9pfs() calls alloc_requests() again and unconditionally overwrites usb9pfs->in_req/out_req, permanently leaking the previous allocations, while the endpoints themselves are left enabled underneath the function's own idea of being disabled. Call disable_usb9pfs() before reinit_completion(&usb9pfs->send), mirroring the same sequence already used in p9_usbg_close(). items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: scsi: target: Fix demo-mode dynamic ACL dev-entry UAF vs LUN teardown A demo-mode (generate_node_acls=1) login that allocates a dynamic NodeACL populates that ACL's per-LUN dev entries in core_tpg_add_node_to_devs() *before* the ACL is linked onto tpg->acl_node_list by target_add_node_acl(): core_tpg_check_initiator_node_acl(): ... core_tpg_add_node_to_devs(acl, tpg, NULL); /* builds deves */ target_add_node_acl(acl); /* only now listed */ The LUN teardown sweep, core_clear_lun_from_tpg(), enumerates only tpg->acl_node_list, so a dev entry whose ACL is still in the window above is invisible to the sweep and is never disabled.
