items.title: CVE-2026-99682: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: virtio_blk: use synchronous quiesce in virtblk_freeze_priv() blk_mq_run_work_fn() can call blk_mq_sched_dispat
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: virtio_blk: use synchronous quiesce in virtblk_freeze_priv() blk_mq_run_work_fn() can call blk_mq_sched_dispatch_requests() through blk_mq_run_dispatch_ops(). The dispatcher checks QUEUE_FLAG_QUIESCED while the flag is clear. It can then be preempted before it gets a request. At that time, it has no queue usage reference, so blk_mq_freeze_queue() does not wait for it. virtblk_freeze_priv() then calls blk_mq_quiesce_queue_nowait() and blk_mq_unfreeze_queue(). A new request can enter the queue. The old dispatcher can run again, use its old flag check, get the new request, and call virtio_queue_rq(). At the same time, virtblk_freeze_priv() can reset the device, delete the virtqueues, and free vblk->vqs. The old dispatcher can then use a deleted virtqueue or a NULL vblk->vqs, and the kernel can crash. Fix this by using blk_mq_quiesce_queue(), which waits for dispatch code that was already running. Keep the existing freeze and unfreeze order. The queue remains quiesced until virtblk_restore_priv() calls blk_mq_unquiesce_queue().

items.title: CVE-2026-99683: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vduse: fix VA/PA confusion in the coherent page fault path vduse_domain_get_coherent_page() assumes that iotlb
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vduse: fix VA/PA confusion in the coherent page fault path vduse_domain_get_coherent_page() assumes that iotlb entries above bounce_size were installed by vduse_domain_alloc_coherent(), so it treats map->addr as a physical address. But vduse registers with use_va = true, and when the device is bound to vhost_vdpa, vhost_vdpa_va_map() stores a userspace virtual address in map->addr, which vduse_domain_set_map() then copies into the same iotlb. A process holding the domain file descriptor across a rebind can therefore fault in an arbitrary physical page with read/write access, ignoring the entry permissions. Additionally, since the domain file mmap lacks VM_IO, the domain file itself can be mapped and passed to vhost_vdpa_va_map(), producing self-referential entries that bypass the coherent path check. To fix, only translate entries whose backing file is the domain file itself in vduse_domain_get_coherent_page(), reject such entries in vduse_domain_set_map() since only external mappings should be imported, and set VM_IO on the domain file mmap so vhost_vdpa_va_map() refuses to map it in the first place.

items.title: CVE-2026-99684: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: hwrng: virtio - prevent use-after-free after a failed restore remove_common() frees the driver data during fre
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: hwrng: virtio - prevent use-after-free after a failed restore remove_common() frees the driver data during freeze, but does not clear vdev->priv, which points to freed memory. If probe_common() then fails during restore, a later remove or freeze can dereference the dangling pointer. Clear vdev->priv on the probe_common() error cleanup path and before freeing the driver data in remove_common(). Also reset the device and return early from remove_common() if vdev->priv is already NULL for a safe teardown after a failed restore.

items.title: CVE-2026-99685: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: iommu/virtio: Reset device before deleting virtqueues on probe failure viommu_probe() marks the device DRIVER_
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: iommu/virtio: Reset device before deleting virtqueues on probe failure viommu_probe() marks the device DRIVER_OK before populating the event virtqueue and registering the IOMMU device in sysfs. viommu_fill_evtq() hands the device a set of device-writable buffers through virtqueue_add_inbuf(), so from that point on the device may write into them and into the rings. If either step fails, the error path deletes the virtqueues without resetting the device first. The event buffers are allocated with devm_kmalloc_array() and are released as probe unwinds, so the device can go on writing to memory that has been freed. Reset the device before deleting the virtqueues, the way viommu_remove() already does.

items.title: CVE-2026-99686: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vhost: fix used ring index wrap in vhost_add_used_n_in_order vhost_add_used_n_in_order() advances start by nhe
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vhost: fix used ring index wrap in vhost_add_used_n_in_order vhost_add_used_n_in_order() advances start by nheads[i] but wraps it with a single subtraction. If start + nheads[i] >= 2 * vq->num, start can remain outside the ring. With used-ring logging enabled, start > vq->num makes (vq->num - start) underflow. log_write() then sets bits beyond the dirty-log bitmap, potentially corrupting adjacent userspace memory. This is reachable on the vhost-net TX path with VIRTIO_F_IN_ORDER: done_idx can reach VHOST_NET_BATCH (64), triggering the issue with a 32-entry ring. Wrap start with a mask to keep it within the ring. VHOST_SET_VRING_NUM enforces a nonzero power-of-two ring size, allowing start to be wrapped using & (vq->num - 1).

items.title: CVE-2026-99687: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vhost-scsi: zero misaligned I/O bounce pages The misaligned I/O fallback copies the full bounce scatterlist to
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vhost-scsi: zero misaligned I/O bounce pages The misaligned I/O fallback copies the full bounce scatterlist to the request buffer during completion. If a data-in command transfers less than requested, part of a newly allocated bounce page can remain unwritten. Allocate bounce pages with __GFP_ZERO so all bytes copied during completion have a defined value. This path is already the slow fallback for misaligned I/O, so the added initialization cost is acceptable. Found during an LLM-assisted source audit and validated with a QEMU/KVM vhost-scsi target using misaligned data-in commands.

items.title: CVE-2026-99688: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/sched: sch_qfq: prevent aggregate self-replacement qfq_change_class() snapshots the current aggregate sett
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/sched: sch_qfq: prevent aggregate self-replacement qfq_change_class() snapshots the current aggregate settings while holding the qdisc tree lock, but drops the lock before selecting the destination aggregate. During that gap, qfq_enqueue() can move the class to an aggregate matching the requested settings. When qfq_change_class() resumes, qfq_find_agg() then returns cl->agg. If it is a singleton, qfq_deact_rm_from_agg() frees the aggregate before qfq_add_to_agg() immediately accesses the same pointer, causing a use-after-free. While holding the tree lock, skip the replacement when the destination is already the current aggregate. Any estimator replacement has already completed, so the class change can finish normally.

items.title: CVE-2026-99689: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: fix temporary cursor leak in btree shift corruption paths In xfs_btree_lshift and xfs_btree_rshift, when
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: fix temporary cursor leak in btree shift corruption paths In xfs_btree_lshift and xfs_btree_rshift, when XFS_IS_CORRUPT detects an invalid firstrec/lastrec result after xfs_btree_dup_cursor has successfully allocated a temporary cursor, the error path jumps to error0 which returns without freeing tcur. This leaks the cursor memory, the xfs_group reference, and the per-level buffer references held by the duplicated cursor. Jump to error1 instead, which calls xfs_btree_del_cursor(tcur, XFS_BTREE_ERROR) to properly release all resources.

items.title: CVE-2026-99674: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: dev: can_dropped_invalid_skb: drop CAN XL frames on non-CAN XL devices Sending a PF_PACKET bypasses the C
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: dev: can_dropped_invalid_skb: drop CAN XL frames on non-CAN XL devices Sending a PF_PACKET bypasses the CAN framework logic and can directly reach a CAN driver's xmit() function. The PF_PACKET framework only checks that skb->len does not exceed the net_device MTU. For a CAN device that is not CAN XL capable, anything above CANFD_MTU (72 bytes) is therefore dropped before it reaches the driver. However, CAN XL frames are variable length. can_is_canxl_skb() accepts lengths in the range CANXL_HDR_SIZE + CANXL_MIN_DLEN up to CANXL_MTU, i.e. 13 to 2060 bytes. As a result, an ETH_P_CANXL skb with a length between 13 and 72 bytes can pass both the MTU and the can_dropped_invalid_skb() checks. A driver that does not support CAN XL will interpret canxl_frame->flags as a length because of the overlap with can_frame->len. And because CANXL_XLF is set, the resulting length is between 128 and 255. For drivers that do not check can_frame->len before copying can_frame->data, as most drivers do, this results in a buffer overflow of up to 247 bytes. Drop ETH_P_CANXL skbs if the device does not have the CAN_CAP_XL capability. K

items.title: CVE-2026-99675: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nvmet: reject keep-alive timeouts that would overflow nvmet_set_feat_kato() and nvmet_alloc_ctrl() convert the
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nvmet: reject keep-alive timeouts that would overflow nvmet_set_feat_kato() and nvmet_alloc_ctrl() convert the 32-bit millisecond KATO from the host to seconds with DIV_ROUND_UP(kato, 1000). The addition in DIV_ROUND_UP() is done in 32 bits, so any KATO above 4294966296 ms wraps around and rounds to 0 seconds. A Set Features command with KATO 0xffffffff then succeeds but disables the keep-alive timer: Get Features returns 0 and Keep Alive fails with Keep Alive Timeout Invalid. A Connect command with such a KATO creates a controller without a keep-alive timer. The converted value has more consumers that can overflow. Get Features multiplies it by 1000, and the timer paths multiply it by HZ in 32 bits and arm a delay that must not exceed MAX_JIFFY_OFFSET. Reject a KATO whose rounded value does not fit all of these. Return Keep Alive Timeout Invalid from both Set Features and Connect. Validate Set Features before stopping the current timer so a failed update leaves its timeout unchanged. Round in 64 bits. A KATO of 0 keeps its current meaning.

items.title: CVE-2026-99676: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: restore refcount ordering for lockless socket access Before commit fb041bb7c0a9 ("locking/refcount: Conso
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: restore refcount ordering for lockless socket access Before commit fb041bb7c0a9 ("locking/refcount: Consolidate implementations of refcount_t"), default builds implemented refcount_inc_not_zero() using atomic_add_unless(), which provided full memory ordering on success. The commit removed that ordering on weakly ordered architectures, allowing accesses after a successful reference acquisition to be reordered before it. Use refcount_inc_not_zero_acquire() in the IPv4 and IPv6 established lookups and in inet_twsk_purge(), where the socket is validated again after taking a reference. bpf_sk_assign() can receive a socket pointer obtained through BTF without a reference. Use acquire ordering when it takes its own reference for a refcounted socket. Use refcount_set_release() when setting refcounts in the SYN cookie, TCP Fast Open, request migration, and TIME_WAIT paths. Keep the existing TIME_WAIT smp_wmb(), which separately orders the refcount store before ehash publication.

items.title: CVE-2026-99677: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: clamp the pNFS layout range to the maximum file size xfs_fs_map_blocks() lets two bad layout ranges throu
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: clamp the pNFS layout range to the maximum file size xfs_fs_map_blocks() lets two bad layout ranges through. An offset of 2^63 or more is negative and passes "offset > limit". A length above the limit, such as NFS4_UINT64_MAX, wraps "offset > limit - length" and stays unclamped. With NFS4_UINT64_MAX, a read layout is built from an uninitialized mapping. Reject a negative offset and one at the limit, and clamp the length. This needs "xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one extent".

items.title: CVE-2026-99678: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one extent xfs_iomap_write_direct() reserves blocks fo
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one extent xfs_iomap_write_direct() reserves blocks for the whole count in an unsigned int. For a pNFS layout the client chooses that count, and an RW LAYOUTGET for 16 TiB wraps the reservation and shuts XFS down. xfs_bmapi_write() maps at most XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN blocks here, so cap the count at that. nfsd asks again for the rest. The other callers get the same mapping as before.

items.title: CVE-2026-99679: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: refuse a pNFS LAYOUTCOMMIT of a range without blocks A client can commit a hole in a LAYOUTCOMMIT, becaus
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: refuse a pNFS LAYOUTCOMMIT of a range without blocks A client can commit a hole in a LAYOUTCOMMIT, because nfsd does not check the extents against its layouts. xfs_iomap_write_unwritten() then allocates written blocks there. A large hole overruns the block reservation and shuts XFS down. A small one exposes stale data. Refuse such a range with -EIO, using XFS_BMAPI_CONVERT_ONLY.

items.title: CVE-2026-99680: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: mark the inode preallocated for pNFS write layouts past EOF xfs_fs_map_blocks() marks the inode XFS_DIFLA
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: mark the inode preallocated for pNFS write layouts past EOF xfs_fs_map_blocks() marks the inode XFS_DIFLAG_PREALLOC only when it allocates blocks for a write layout. A write layout past EOF can also hand out allocated blocks, such as speculative preallocation. blockgc then frees them under the layout, and another file may get them. Mark the inode whenever a write mapping ends past EOF.

items.title: CVE-2026-99681: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: blk-mq: fix out-of-bounds read in blk_mq_free_rqs A KASAN slab-out-of-bounds read can occur in blk_mq_free_rqs
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: blk-mq: fix out-of-bounds read in blk_mq_free_rqs A KASAN slab-out-of-bounds read can occur in blk_mq_free_rqs() when there is a mismatch between the number of hardware queues allocated for the IO scheduler (et->nr_hw_queues) and the number of hardware queues in the block tag set (set->nr_hw_queues). This mismatch can happen if blk_mq_update_nr_hw_queues() fails halfway through (e.g., due to memory pressure during blk_mq_prealloc_tag_set_tags()). In this error path, the elevator is restored with a larger number of hardware queues than the block tag set actually has. When the elevator is later freed, blk_mq_free_sched_tags() iterates up to the new et->nr_hw_queues and calls blk_mq_free_rqs(). In blk_mq_free_rqs(), it attempts to access set->tags[hctx_idx] to get the driver tags. Because set->nr_hw_queues was not updated due to the earlier failure, set->tags still has the old (smaller) size, leading to an out-of-bounds read. items.title: CVE-2026-99667: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/khugepaged: always recheck the pmd in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() drops the
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/khugepaged: always recheck the pmd in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() drops the PTE lock after it has cleared the page table, and takes the PMD lock and the PTE lock to remove it. In between, MADV_DONTNEED with CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM can reclaim the page table. The pmd_same() check is supposed to handle this, but it is only done with CONFIG_SPLIT_PTE_PTLOCKS. Fix it by performing the check unconditionally. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private. [ david: adjust description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99668: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: fix zapping migration entries for device-private THPs A PMD migration entry can refer to a dev
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: fix zapping migration entries for device-private THPs A PMD migration entry can refer to a device-private folio. zap_huge_pmd_folio() checks the folio type instead of the entry type, so it treats such a migration entry as a device-private entry. Installing the migration entry already removed the reverse mapping and dropped the mapping reference. Zapping it must not repeat those operations. Concurrent MADV_DONTNEED during migration back to system memory can trigger this. Check the PMD entry type using pmd_is_device_private_entry(). Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99669: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: fix truncate racing with PMD zapping zap_huge_pmd_folio() removes the rmap before calling foli
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: fix truncate racing with PMD zapping zap_huge_pmd_folio() removes the rmap before calling folio_mark_dirty(). If this was the last mapping, truncation can skip unmapping the folio and proceed without waiting for the PMD lock, racing with dirtying. ifs_set_range_dirty() can oops if MADV_DONTNEED races with ftruncate() on XFS, when we get the folio set dirty after it was found to not be mapped anymore. Move folio_mark_dirty() and folio_mark_accessed() before rmap removal, matching the PTE zap path. This keeps the folio mapped while updating its state, so truncation must wait for the page table lock. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify comment and description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99670: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: dev: can_fill_info(): don't wake up controller if interface is down If the interface is down, the CAN con
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: dev: can_fill_info(): don't wake up controller if interface is down If the interface is down, the CAN controller might be powered down and its clocks gated. Don't call do_get_berr_counter() to read the bus error counters if the interface is down, and adjust can_get_size() to match. This removes one trigger for a synchronous external abort seen on i.MX8QXP when "ip link show" is run on a flexcan interface that was never brought up. The underlying cause is platform-specific: on i.MX8QXP the CAN clocks are gated through the SCU LPCG and the subsystem shares the IMX_SC_R_CAN_0 power domain, and there is a window after pm_runtime_resume_and_get() returns where the clock has not reached the module yet. This patch avoids the netlink query path while the interface is down, but does not root-cause the LPCG window itself. As a result, IFLA_CAN_BERR_COUNTER is no longer reported for down interfaces. Userspace must treat the attribute as optional. The issue was triggered on an i.MX8QXP board by running "ip link show" without ever bringing the interface up: Internal error: synchronous external abort: 0000000096000210 pc :

items.title: CVE-2026-99671: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: raw, isotp: copy socket options outside of lock_sock() The CAN_RAW and CAN_ISOTP specific socket options
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: raw, isotp: copy socket options outside of lock_sock() The CAN_RAW and CAN_ISOTP specific socket options are copied from and to user space while holding lock_sock(). A copy that faults or stalls, e.g. on a userfaultfd or FUSE backed mapping, holds lock_sock() for its whole duration. raw_notify() and isotp_notify() take lock_sock() of a socket that is bound to the vanishing device while holding RTNL. As the CAN_RAW options can also be changed on a bound socket, a stalled copy can block RTNL on an unregistration or namespace change of the bound device. Before "can: protect the receive lists with a per-device lock", raw_setsockopt() even held RTNL itself during the copy. CAN_ISOTP only copies its options for unbound sockets, which isotp_notify() skips without taking lock_sock(). Keep the user space copies out of the locked sections: Check the option name and length and copy the option values, including the CAN_RAW_FILTER filters, to kernel memory before lock_sock(). raw_setsockopt_locked() and isotp_setsockopt_locked() get the copied values directly and drop their now redundant length checks and copies. As a side

items.title: CVE-2026-99672: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: protect the receive lists with a per-device lock The receive lists of a CAN device are located in the dev
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: protect the receive lists with a per-device lock The receive lists of a CAN device are located in the device's can_ml_priv and travel with the device when it is moved to another network namespace. But they are protected by the per-netns rcvlists_lock. So can_rx_unregister() needs dev_net(dev) to pick the right lock and silently returns when the passed namespace does not match dev_net(dev) anymore. isotp_release() and bcm_release() leave their notifier list before they take any lock that serializes against the netdev notifier, which runs under RTNL. When the bound device is moved to another namespace in this window, the notifier skips the socket and the release path has to remove the filters itself. isotp_release() passes the socket's namespace, which does not match dev_net(dev) anymore. bcm_rx_unreg() passes dev_net(dev), which can_rx_unregister() reads again for its check, so a namespace change between both reads makes the check fail as well. In both cases can_rx_unregister() silently returns. As can_rx_register() stores rcv->sk without a reference, the remaining receivers point to the freed socket (isotp) or

items.title: CVE-2026-99673: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: replace ARPHRD_CAN type checks with can_get_ml_priv() Commit 4e096a18867a ("net: introduce CAN specific p
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: can: replace ARPHRD_CAN type checks with can_get_ml_priv() Commit 4e096a18867a ("net: introduce CAN specific pointer in the struct net_device") introduced an explicit way to assign the midlayer private pointer (dev->ml_priv) to named users like ML_PRIV_CAN. A valid pointer returned by can_get_ml_priv() therefore identifies a real CAN device. The referenced commit only converted the j1939 and proc code to this check, while the other parts of the CAN subsystem still rely on dev->type == ARPHRD_CAN. The TUNSETLINK ioctl allows a down TUN/TAP device to set its hardware type to ARPHRD_CAN while dev->ml_priv remains NULL. Such a repurposed netdevice passes the ARPHRD_CAN checks. Commit 8aa59e355949 ("can: af_can: fix NULL pointer dereference in can_rx_register()") already made can_rx_register() reject such devices. But can_rx_unregister() still only checks dev->type and dereferences the NULL ml_priv when it walks the receive lists of the device. CAN_ISOTP reaches this path: isotp_bind() ignores the return values of can_rx_register() and binds the socket anyway. When the socket is released or the device is unregistered, i

items.title: CVE-2026-99660: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/userfaultfd: write-lock the VMA before waking waiters when unregistering userfaultfd_unregister() wakes pen
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/userfaultfd: write-lock the VMA before waking waiters when unregistering userfaultfd_unregister() wakes pending missing faults before clearing the VMA's userfaultfd registration. With per-VMA fault locking, holding mmap_lock for write does not prevent another fault from queuing after the wakeup but before userfaultfd_clear_vma() write-locks the VMA. That waiter can then remain asleep indefinitely. Call vma_start_write() before waking waiters. Existing fault handlers queue themselves before dropping the VMA read lock, and new readers are excluded until mmap_write_unlock().

items.title: CVE-2026-99661: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: check for overflow when converting nr_pages to bytes in GUP-fast The overflow check in gup_fast_fallba
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: check for overflow when converting nr_pages to bytes in GUP-fast The overflow check in gup_fast_fallback() only covers the addition to start. The preceding nr_pages << PAGE_SHIFT can already have truncated the length on 32bit. Users such as RapidIO's rio_dma_transfer() can derive such page counts from a 64-bit userspace length. Let's just check_shl_overflow() to reject any such overflow with -EOVERFLOW early.

items.title: CVE-2026-99662: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: fix out-of-bounds write for nr_pages == 0 in GUP-fast With nr_pages == 0, GUP-fast still enters its pa
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: fix out-of-bounds write for nr_pages == 0 in GUP-fast With nr_pages == 0, GUP-fast still enters its page table walk and can write past the caller's page array. The old end <= start check caught empty ranges, but was replaced with an overflow check. Users such as OrangeFS can pass a zero page count derived from a userspace-supplied length. So let's return zero for nr_pages == 0 before starting the walk, just like GUP-slow. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99663: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: fix clearing folios in memfd_pin_folios() memfd_pin_folios() pins folios obtained directly from the pa
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: fix clearing folios in memfd_pin_folios() memfd_pin_folios() pins folios obtained directly from the page cache without checking whether they are uptodate. However, shmem fallocate() can leave newly allocated folios uncleared and not uptodate. Callers such as udmabuf can then expose uninitialized memory to userspace. Clear non-uptodate folios and mark them uptodate under the folio lock before returning them to the caller. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify description and comment ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99664: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: recheck the PUD under PTL in follow_pud_mask() follow_pud_mask() reads the PUD without a lock. If it i
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: recheck the PUD under PTL in follow_pud_mask() follow_pud_mask() reads the PUD without a lock. If it is a leaf, it takes the lock and calls follow_huge_pud(), which reads the entry again, but only tests whether it is present. A leaf can be zapped concurrently and a page fault can fill the empty entry with a page table. This currently only applies when device-dax makes use of PUD entries, and the fault after e.g., MADV_DONTNEED would find THPs to be disabled. That requires a sequence like 1) Fault in the PUD 2) Disable THP 3) Have GUP race against concurrent MADV_DONTNEED + refault Which is rather unlikely to happen in practice, which is why we never received a report about such a problem. Before commit 1b1676180246 ("mm/gup: handle huge pud for follow_pud_mask()"), we performed that check in follow_devmap_pud() by testing for pud_devmap(). Let's fix it by just structuring follow_pud_mask() similar to follow_pmd_mask(), minus protnone stuff that does not apply and minus FOLL_SPLIT_PMD handling. That makes it much easier to spot any such inconsistencies. Perform the pud_bad() check early in follow_pmd_mask()

items.title: CVE-2026-99665: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/khugepaged: preserve dirty bits when collapsing PTE-mapped THPs try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() clears PTEs w
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/khugepaged: preserve dirty bits when collapsing PTE-mapped THPs try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() clears PTEs without transferring their dirty bits to the folio. A shmem read fault can map a clean folio writable, so a later store only dirties the PTE. Losing that dirty bit allows reclaim to discard modified data. The assumption that regular files are read-only is also obsolete since commit 1b6444331bebb ("mm/khugepaged: enable clean pagecache folio collapse for writable files"). In any case, transferring PTE dirty bits to the folio when removing mappings (and while the folio is still mapped) is the right thing to do. Use get_and_clear_ptes() to collect the dirty bits and mark the folio dirty before unmapping it. Update the comment. This was reproduced with shmem using MADV_COLLAPSE followed by MADV_PAGEOUT. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: adjust comment; simplify description; cover file-thp as well ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99666: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/khugepaged: fix PMD table lock leak in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() For a private mapping with userfaultfd
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/khugepaged: fix PMD table lock leak in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() For a private mapping with userfaultfd, try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() takes the PMD table lock before it maps the page table for the second time. If that (pte_offset_map_rw_nolock) fails, because the page table vanished in the meantime due to concurrent page table reclaim, it leaves through the abort label, where the PMD table lock is unlocked if it differs from PTE table lock. In case the PMD table lock and the PTE table lock match, which is the case without CONFIG_SPLIT_PTE_PTLOCKS after pte_offset_map_rw_nolock() failed, we miss to unlock the PMD table. To fix it, forget the PTE table lock when we unmap+unlock the PTE table. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private. [ david: move the ptl = NULL handling; rewrite description, drop wrong comments ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99653: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix unkillable fault loop on MAP_DROPPABLE memory handle_mm_fault() suppresses VM_FAULT_OOM for VM_DROPPAB
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix unkillable fault loop on MAP_DROPPABLE memory handle_mm_fault() suppresses VM_FAULT_OOM for VM_DROPPABLE mappings. For user-mode faults, pending signals are processed before retrying the access. Kernel-mode faults on user buffers instead return directly to the faulting instruction. With persistent allocation failures (esp. memcg limits), a syscall, such as write(), can therefore loop while not dropping locks. Only suppress VM_FAULT_OOM when FAULT_FLAG_USER is set, allowing kernel-mode faults and GUP to fail and signal allocation errors. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99654: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix unmap_mapping_range() beyond 4 GiB on 32-bit Commit 9eab0421fa94 ("mm: fix unmap_mapping_range high bi
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix unmap_mapping_range() beyond 4 GiB on 32-bit Commit 9eab0421fa94 ("mm: fix unmap_mapping_range high bits shift bug") made holebegin and holelen unsigned before they are shifted, by casting them to pgoff_t. That is an unsigned long: on a 32-bit kernel the cast cuts off the upper half of the two loff_t values, so a hole which begins at 4 GiB or beyond is taken for one in the first 4 GiB of the file. truncate_pagecache() passes the new size of the file and asks for private COWed pages to be unmapped as well. If a file of 6 GiB is truncated to 5 GiB, everything from 1 GiB on is unmapped, and what a process has written to a private mapping of the range between 1 GiB and 5 GiB is lost: it reads the contents of the file again. Where the range has an end, the wrong range is unmapped instead of the right one. The page cache copes with that, as it unmaps every folio that it removes. The callers which only have unmap_mapping_range() to get rid of user mappings do not, for example drm_vma_node_unmap(), whose fake offsets reach beyond 4 GiB on 32-bit, and revoke_iomem() with physical addresses of more than 32 bits. Cast

items.title: CVE-2026-99655: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/memory: reject remote COW faults on PFN mappings When handling a COW fault without a normal source page (PF
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/memory: reject remote COW faults on PFN mappings When handling a COW fault without a normal source page (PFN mappings), __wp_page_copy_user() copies from the faulting user address. For remote faults, this accesses the wrong address space, resulting in wrong data getting copied. For example, user_events updates an enable bit in the registering process's memory. If that memory needs to be faulted in, user_event_enabler_fault_fixup() calls fixup_user_fault() from a work item. Placing the enable bit in a private PFN mapping can trigger this remote COW path. Reject these faults with VM_FAULT_SIGBUS when the target mm differs from current->mm: remote faults. Ordinary (non-PFN) mappings are not affected. The user-address copy dates back to commit 6aab341e0a28 ("mm: re-architect the VM_UNPAGED logic"); likely, actual ways to get remote faults in there on COW PFN mappings appeared afterwards. But the fix is simple and straight forward. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify comment and description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99656: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/madvise: fix data loss from MADV_FREE on a KSM page MADV_FREE can clear the dirty flag of a singly mapped K
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/madvise: fix data loss from MADV_FREE on a KSM page MADV_FREE can clear the dirty flag of a singly mapped KSM folio. The folio remains in the stable tree and can gain new mappings without being dirtied again. Once marked lazyfree, reclaim can discard data that those mappings still need. KSM always marks a folio dirty when converting it to a KSM folio in try_to_merge_one_page(). Marking a folio lazyfree clears PG_swapbacked but leaves PG_dirty unchanged. Preserving PG_dirty makes reclaim restore PG_swapbacked instead of discarding the folio. This also protects folios that were already lazyfree when KSM converted them. Skip KSM folios before clearing their dirty flag, checking under the folio lock to serialize with KSM conversion.

items.title: CVE-2026-99657: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_notifier: set ->mm only after mmgrab() Radeon uses a non-NULL notifier->mm to decide whether to call mm
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_notifier: set ->mm only after mmgrab() Radeon uses a non-NULL notifier->mm to decide whether to call mmu_interval_notifier_remove() when freeing a buffer object. __mmu_interval_notifier_insert() sets ->mm before validating the range, so a wrapping userptr range can leave ->mm set after insertion fails. Cleanup then tries to remove an unregistered notifier for which no mm reference was acquired. Set ->mm only after mmgrab(), once insertion can no longer fail. While we could fix radeon's code instead, setting ->mm on success only makes the code more robust. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: simplify description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99658: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_notifier: finish non-blocking interval invalidation on error When an ordinary MMU notifier rejects a no
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_notifier: finish non-blocking interval invalidation on error When an ordinary MMU notifier rejects a non-blocking invalidation, the interval invalidation started beforehand is left unfinished: the caller skips mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_end(). Subsequent interval notifier operations can then wait forever. The only in-tree trigger is nouveau SVM, which uses both notifier types and rejects non-blocking invalidations. Reaping via the OOM reaper or process_mrelease() can therefore leave the GPU fault worker stuck, holding a reference that prevents the dying process's address space and memory from being freed. End the interval invalidation when an ordinary notifier fails a non-blocking invalidation, like mn_itree_invalidate() already does when an interval notifier fails. Make that handling clearer in the documentation of mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_start_nonblock(). Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private. [ david: simplify description, update function doc ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99659: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_gather: fix flushing ranges with 4 GiB or larger __tlb_adjust_range() takes the size of the range which
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/mmu_gather: fix flushing ranges with 4 GiB or larger __tlb_adjust_range() takes the size of the range which has to be flushed as an unsigned int. Its callers, tlb_flush_{pte,pmd,pud,p4d}_range(), get and pass an unsigned long. Consequently, a range that is 4 GiB or larger gets truncated, possibly to 0. On arm64 with hugetlb, a 64k kernel can have 16 GiB hugetlb folios mapped contiguously at the PMD level and flush them when unmapping, and a 16k kernel can flush 64 GiB PUDs through tlb_unshare_pmd_ptdesc(). So at least these two scenarios are affected. Fix it by flushing the proper range instead of the truncated one by properly using "unsigned long" for range_size. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private. [ david: use two-tab indent, simplify description ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99645: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/cma: don't release CMA pages still in use When a driver calls dma_free_contiguous() before quiescing DMA, t
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/cma: don't release CMA pages still in use When a driver calls dma_free_contiguous() before quiescing DMA, the page might still have a reference from the device. put_page_testzero() there returns false, WARN fires, but the code proceeds to free_contig_frozen_range() putting a live page onto buddy and clearing the bitmap. A subsequent allocation can hand the same PFN to a new owner while the original holder still references it. A concurrent put_page() that drops the last reference between the testzero loop and free_contig_frozen_range() can double-queue the page via page->lru, corrupting buddy lists. Avoid the corruption by not freeing a CMA region if any of the pages inside are still in use. Make it explicit in the warning that the driver allowed a leak. While at it, use page_ref_freeze() to make the semantics clearer and switch to pr_warn_ratelimited(). [ david: use page_ref_freeze() + pr_warn_ratelimited() ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99646: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/vma: don't leak the charge for stack growth acct_stack_growth() charges stack expansion even without VM_ACC
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/vma: don't leak the charge for stack growth acct_stack_growth() charges stack expansion even without VM_ACCOUNT. This can happen for read-only or MAP_NORESERVE mappings created with MAP_GROWSDOWN. Unmapping these VMAs does not release the charge, leaking Committed_AS. Only check and charge growth for VM_ACCOUNT VMAs, matching mremap(). Unaccounted growth skips the overcommit check while remaining subject to the other stack-growth limits.

items.title: CVE-2026-99647: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: split huge PUDs when adjusting VMA boundaries PFN mappings such as VFIO PCI BAR mappings can u
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/huge_memory: split huge PUDs when adjusting VMA boundaries PFN mappings such as VFIO PCI BAR mappings can use PUD leaves while allowing VMA splits at page granularity. However, vma_adjust_trans_huge() only handles PMDs. After faulting a writable PUD-sized VFIO BAR mapping, changing its first page to read-only with mprotect() makes the PMD walk treat the PUD leaf as a PMD table. Applying MADV_DONTFORK to the first PMD-sized chunk leaves the PUD spanning two VMAs: the PMD-aligned boundary skips splitting. Walk the page tables once at each adjusted boundary and split a huge PUD or PMD leaf as needed. Handle PUD leaves even when the boundary is PMD-aligned.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/vma: call ->may_split() before a partial merge A driver can use the ->may_split() hook to forbid a VMA boundary at certain addresses. A device-dax device is a character device that gives raw access to a range of memory through mmap(). device-dax refuses any address that is not a multiple of the device's alignment through vm_ops->may_split. vma_merge_existing_range() can move boundaries, but does not call vm_ops->may_split. If a range at the edge of a VMA gets the attributes of the adjacent VMA, the function moves only that range over to the neighbour: one VMA shrinks and the other grows. This is a partial merge, and vma_modify() tries it before any split. Take a device-dax VMA that lies next to another VMA of the same file. The user calls mprotect() on the one page of the first VMA that touches the second VMA, and asks for the protection that the second VMA already has. The result is a partial merge. It puts the boundary inside a 1 GiB mapping, which is a single leaf entry at the PUD level. As part of the merge, the kernel looks for a huge PMD to split at the new boundary. items.title: CVE-2026-99649: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: check large swap-cache folios before mapping them KSM folios are always small, but their shared swap s
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: check large swap-cache folios before mapping them KSM folios are always small, but their shared swap slots can be read back as part of a large folio in the swap cache. ksm_might_need_to_copy() skips large folios, so another process can map a page with an incompatible anon_vma or page index. Reverse mapping then cannot find the new mapping, preventing migration or reclaim. Apply the same compatibility checks to large folios as to small ones. Pass the page corresponding to the swap entry and copy only that page when necessary. In do_swap_page()'s copy path, decrement only that slot's swap count, because the source swap-cache folio can now be large. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

items.title: CVE-2026-99650: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: fix use of a freed anon_vma at swap-in A folio read from a swap slot previously shared by KSM can rema
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: fix use of a freed anon_vma at swap-in A folio read from a swap slot previously shared by KSM can remain in the swap cache after the process that first mapped it exits. Its anon_vma can then be freed, so ksm_might_need_to_copy() must not dereference it to compare roots. Doing so can result in some false-positives, resulting in the reverse mapping missing the new folio mapping, preventing migration and reclaim. SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU allows individual anon_vma objects to be reused immediately after freeing. A stale pointer can then refer to another anon_vma whose root matches, even though the target VMA is not linked to that anon_vma. Move the anonymous rmap compatibility checks into folio_anon_rmap_compatible(). Keep the page-index check and compare the folio's anon_vma pointer against the VMA's own anon_vma and root first. If neither matches, bite the bullet and walk the VMA's anon_vma_chain. The VMA keeps these anon_vmas alive, and finding a match guarantees that reverse mapping can find the new mapping. items.title: CVE-2026-99651: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: reset the unstable trees of all nodes Each full scan resets ksm_nr_node_ids unstable tree roots. Enabl
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/ksm: reset the unstable trees of all nodes Each full scan resets ksm_nr_node_ids unstable tree roots. Enabling merge_across_nodes resets this count to 1, even if per-node roots were previously allocated. So when toggling "merge_across_nodes" 0 -> 1 -> 0, a scan that starts while the setting is 1 and continues after switching back to 0 can encounter stale unstable tree roots, resulting in UAF. Only root is allowed to change "merge_across_nodes", and the documented sequence is: "merge_across_nodes setting can be changed only when there are no ksm shared pages in the system: set run 2 to unmerge pages first, then to 1 after changing merge_across_nodes, to remerge according to the new setting." Let's fix it by tracking in ksm_nr_node_ids the actual number of allocated tree roots. remove_all_stable_nodes() and ksm_check_stable_tree() will now scan more tree roots (skipping the empty ones), which is harmless.

items.title: CVE-2026-99652: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix deadlock of mremap() against UFFDIO_MOVE With per-VMA locks, UFFDIO_MOVE can run concurrently with mre
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm: fix deadlock of mremap() against UFFDIO_MOVE With per-VMA locks, UFFDIO_MOVE can run concurrently with mremap() on different VMAs in the same mm. Those VMAs can share page tables, so both operations can acquire the same pair of page-table locks. UFFDIO_MOVE orders the locks by address, while mremap() takes the source lock first. These conflicting orders can deadlock; mremap() holding mmap_lock for writing no longer helps. Move double_pt_lock() and double_pt_unlock() to mm/internal.h and use them for all page-table moves in mremap(). Preserve the source entry checks after acquiring both locks. Remove the comments claiming that exclusive mmap_lock makes lock ordering irrelevant. In move_ptes(), make sure to just recheck source and destination PMD after taking the locks and drop the overly-long comment. Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private. [ david: use new helpers consistently; simplify description and comments; move_ptes() fixup ]

Drivers that index their rings from skb_get_queue_mapping() (ex: ifb) go out of range the same way. - On enqueue, taprio_enqueue() indexes q->qdiscs[] with the same value; the array is sized dev->num_tx_queues. With casefolded directories, both dentries can be unhashed: - The target. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: do not let chattr change the casefold flag chattr +F or -F on an overlay directory can make the directory, or the whole mount, unusable. It then passes FS_CASEFOLD_FL on to the upper filesystem. The upper filesystem accepts the change if the upper directory is empty, regardless of what the merged directory contains. items.title: CVE-2026-99641: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: fail the mount if the casefold flag has changed An unprivileged user in a user namespace can repeatedly t
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: fail the mount if the casefold flag has changed An unprivileged user in a user namespace can repeatedly trigger a kernel warning with their own overlay mounts. They do so by changing the casefold flag of the topmost layer's empty root, the top directory of that layer, after the layers are set and before the mount is created. The casefold flag of a directory makes name lookups in that directory case-insensitive. The mount is created later, by another fsconfig() call with FSCONFIG_CMD_CREATE. The casefold flag of an empty directory can be changed. The casefold flag of the overlay root must match ofs->casefold. ovl_get_root() copies the flag from the topmost layer root, as it is when the mount is created. On a mismatch, ovl_get_root() only does a WARN_ON(), and the mount continues. The check is not a WARN_ON_ONCE(), so each such mount warns again. items.title: CVE-2026-99642: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: check folio->mapping under folio lock in memfd_pin_folios() memfd_pin_folios() pins folios from the pa
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: check folio->mapping under folio lock in memfd_pin_folios() memfd_pin_folios() pins folios from the page cache without taking the folio lock. khugepaged or MADV_COLLAPSE can therefore replace a folio after checking its refcount while memfd_pin_folios() still pins the old folio. The caller then receives a folio which is no longer part of the memfd. For udmabuf and iommufd, this can cause data corruption: DMA accesses the detached folio rather than the live memfd contents. DMA reads can return stale data, while DMA writes update the detached copy and are lost from the live memfd. The detached folio remains pinned, so these accesses do not constitute a use-after-free or target another application's memory. For memfd live update, the stale contents can reappear in the memfd after handover. Lock the folio and recheck folio->mapping before pinning it, like other page cache users do. If the folio was removed, retry the folio lookup from the index that was removed.

items.title: CVE-2026-99643: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: khugepaged: fix readahead lock inversion in collapse_file() collapse_file() can call page_cache_sync_readahead
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: khugepaged: fix readahead lock inversion in collapse_file() collapse_file() can call page_cache_sync_readahead() while still holding source folios locked. If truncate holds mapping->invalidate_lock exclusively and waits for one of those folios, readahead waits for invalidate_lock and neither side can make progress. We need to release those folio locks before starting readahead. On a page cache miss, roll back first, populate the collapse range, and retry once. Doing readahead after rollback avoids an extra pass when all folios are already present. If another miss occurs on retry, give up rather than keep retrying while truncate or reclaim removes folios. Keep page_cache_sync_readahead() and wait for read I/O with filemap_lock_folio(), releasing each folio before moving to the next. The existing uptodate check during collapse still handles read errors. Shmem uses shmem_get_folio() for swapin and fallocated folios without taking mapping->invalidate_lock, so it is unaffected.

items.title: CVE-2026-99644: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/memory-tiers: unregister empty tiers outside memory_tier_lock When offlining a node's last memory empties i
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/memory-tiers: unregister empty tiers outside memory_tier_lock When offlining a node's last memory empties its tier, clear_node_memory_tier() calls device_unregister() while holding memory_tier_lock. A concurrent sysfs read can hold a kernfs active reference and block in nodelist_show() on that mutex. device_unregister() then waits in kernfs_drain() for the read to finish and release its active reference, while the reader waits for the offlining task to release the mutex. Return the node's former tier from clear_node_memory_tier(), making the helper more similar to set_node_memory_tier(), which also returns a memory_tier pointer. Let the caller unlink an empty tier under memory_tier_lock before rebuilding demotion targets, then unregister its device after dropping the lock.

items.title: CVE-2026-99630: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu/userq: validate the moved individual BOs on restore An individual BO of a user queue VM, i.e. one w
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu/userq: validate the moved individual BOs on restore An individual BO of a user queue VM, i.e. one which doesn't share the root reservation, goes to the individual needs_update list when it is evicted. The user queue restore looked at vm->invalidated for them, which the VM state machine rework turned into the always_valid evicted list and commit 18decfc9e8cc ("drm/amdgpu/userq: actually validate userq BOs") into the individual evicted one. That list only holds imported DMA-bufs of compute VMs though, so for a user queue VM nothing is validated. The restore then neither locks such a BO nor moves it back. Its PTEs are updated to wherever it is now, cleared if it went to system memory, and it doesn't get the new eviction fence, so it can move again under the running queue. On navi48, once the BOs of an SDMA user queue are evicted from GTT (debugfs amdgpu_evict_gtt) the queue faults on its ring and rptr: amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: in page starting at address 0x0000000100000000 from client 10 amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: Faulty UTCL2 client ID: SDMA0 (0xd) amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: in page starting at address 0x0000000100101000

items.title: CVE-2026-99631: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: check amdgpu_vm_ready() in dma-buf move notify amdgpu_dma_buf_move_notify() touches the page table
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amdgpu: check amdgpu_vm_ready() in dma-buf move notify amdgpu_dma_buf_move_notify() touches the page tables without first calling amdgpu_vm_ready(). When a process is SIGKILLed, its VM entities are stopped. Teardown of an imported dma-buf then tries to clear PTEs by submitting to one of those stopped entities. That eventually hangs the task. Commit aa5fc4362fac ("drm/amdgpu: fix task hang from failed job submission during process kill") added the stopped entity check in amdgpu_vm_ready() and used it in amdgpu_cs_vm_handling(). That did not cover a call in amdgpu_dma_buf_move_notify(), what was already mentioned in: https://lists.freedesktop.org/archives/amd-gfx/2025-October/133076.html Tested by SIGKILLing a GPU workload holding imported dma-bufs. Without the patch "Trying to push to a killed entity" errors are logged, then a task hangs. With the patch there are no hung tasks. This was tested on a 6.18 kernel. (cherry picked from commit bee5c9d7a34cb1b510ad3b4c18c30f9d38b0ab7d)

items.title: CVE-2026-99634: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mptcp: do not use Fast Open on MP_JOIN subflows tcp_fastopen_create_child() hands the SYN packet itself to sub
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mptcp: do not use Fast Open on MP_JOIN subflows tcp_fastopen_create_child() hands the SYN packet itself to subflow_syn_recv_sock(). For an MP_JOIN request this takes the fatal fallback: the cloned child is destroyed and handed back with drop_req flagged, but tcp_fastopen_create_child() does not check the flag and queues it, so accept() can expose the freed child. MP_JOIN cannot use Fast Open: data on a subflow requires the completed HMAC exchange (RFC 8684, sec. 3.2). Refuse it (only the TFO path passes a SYN skb here) and let tcp_conn_request() fall back to the regular MP_JOIN handshake; also strip the Fast Open cookie from MP_JOIN SYN/ACKs. [ Moving code to avoid clearing TS and consolidating checks. ]

items.title: CVE-2026-99635: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vhost/vsock: size receive SKBs from declared payload vhost_vsock_alloc_skb() sizes the skb from iov_length(),
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: vhost/vsock: size receive SKBs from declared payload vhost_vsock_alloc_skb() sizes the skb from iov_length(), the total guest descriptor length. virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt() instead adds hdr->len to rx_bytes and buf_used, and budgets each queued skb as SKB_TRUESIZE(0). The guest controls the descriptor length and hdr->len independently. A guest can therefore provide a 64 KiB descriptor while declaring a zero payload. The descriptor-sized skb remains queued, rx_bytes and buf_used remain unchanged, and only the fixed queue-entry budget limits retention. On Linux v7.2, 455 such descriptors retained 30,255,680 bytes for a 262,144-byte receive buffer; a full-payload control retained 265,984 bytes. Vhost previously read hdr->len and allocated pkt->buf from that value. The conversion from virtio_vsock_pkt to sk_buff instead allocated receive skbs from the descriptor length, introducing the allocation-accounting mismatch. items.title: CVE-2026-99636: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: reject a negative TCP header offset in qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() stores skb_tra
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: reject a negative TCP header offset in qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init() stores skb_transport_offset(), or the inner offset, in the unsigned hdr_len. A header in front of skb->data gives a negative offset. For an offset a little below zero, pskb_may_pull() gets a small length and succeeds. Then a 64-bit kernel reads the TCP header far after the skb and can crash. Further below zero pskb_may_pull() fails. Commit 28a57fb2c5df ("net: iptunnel: fix stale transport header during tunnel decapsulation") fixed one source of such offsets. Other code that removes bytes from the front of a packet can leave the same stale header. Return SKB_DROP_REASON_SKB_BAD_GSO for a negative offset in the TCP branch. SKB_GSO_UDP_L4 and the other GSO types read no header and still get a wrong qdisc_pkt_len(). On a 64-bit kernel only packets that cause the read after the skb today get a new result. Then __dev_queue_xmit() drops them and returns -EINVAL, but sch_handle_ingress() ignores the result. Their content can be valid. Thus the code that leaves the header stale needs its own fix.

items.title: CVE-2026-99637: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: inherit FMODE_NONOTIFY when opening directory realfiles When fanotify hands a listener an fd for a permis
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: inherit FMODE_NONOTIFY when opening directory realfiles When fanotify hands a listener an fd for a permission event on an overlay directory, ovl_dir_open_realfile() opens the real directory via dentry_open(), not backing_file_open(), so the lower open could still raise FS_OPEN_PERM and deadlock a listener that also marks the backing filesystem. items.title: CVE-2026-99626: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amd/display: Fix NULL deref in dcn401_update_clocks_update_dtb_dto [Why] resource_get_otg_master_for_strea
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/amd/display: Fix NULL deref in dcn401_update_clocks_update_dtb_dto [Why] resource_get_otg_master_for_stream() can return NULL if no OTG master pipe is found for a given stream. The current code dereferences this pointer without a NULL check. This may lead to a possible NULL pointer dereference. [How] Add an explicit NULL check and skip the stream if the OTG master is not found. This is similar to dcn60_update_clocks_update_dtb_dto(). The open can also succeed for a file that was removed, where it has to fail with ESTALE. This happens with a handle that has one byte changed. items.title: CVE-2026-99617: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: arm64: mm: validate /dev/mem mmap ranges without overflow An arm64 syzkaller reproducer creates a FUSE charact
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: arm64: mm: validate /dev/mem mmap ranges without overflow An arm64 syzkaller reproducer creates a FUSE character device with major:minor 1:1, so opening it uses the /dev/mem file operations. It maps one page from offset 0xfffffffffffff000 at user address zero. The next openat() with a NULL pathname triggers a synchronous external abort (SEA, ESR 0x96000010) in strncpy_from_user() via do_getname(), panicking the kernel. valid_mmap_phys_addr_range() checks the exclusive end by adding the mapping size to the starting address. For this offset, the sum wraps to zero and passes the PHYS_MASK test, allowing an out-of-range PFN to reach remap_pfn_range(). The inclusive-end overflow check in mmap_mem_prepare() does not catch it because the end is ULONG_MAX. Reject starting PFNs outside PHYS_MASK and compare the inclusive length against the remaining physical range without overflowing. This also allows mappings that end exactly at PHYS_MASK, which the old check incorrectly rejects. [catalin.marinas@arm.com: changed the check to look more like __access_ok()]

items.title: CVE-2026-99618: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nvmet: don't return memory contents beyond valid data when reading ANA log page The host side does not know ho
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nvmet: don't return memory contents beyond valid data when reading ANA log page The host side does not know how much valid data will be returned by the target so it will typically provide a buffer larger than the amount of valid data in the ANA log page. The memory allocation used by the target does not guarantee that prior kernel memory contents will not be returned past the end of the valid page data. Fix this to ensure that the SGL is zeroed before copying the data.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: caiaq: free the EP4 URB when input setup fails The three controllers that use the EP4 input URB allocate it before checking the endpoint type and before registering the input device. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: hda/tas2781: Only accept CRC-less V1 data if all entries are valid Commit 408249089c48 ("ALSA: hda/tas2781: Accept V1 calibration data without CRC") only checked the first device entry. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: udf: check the unallocated space table when it is loaded udf_table_new_block() hands out the first block of the extent closest to its goal and trusts that the extent covers at least one whole block inside the partition. Nothing checks that. A zero-length extent makes it return the block the extent points at, which need not be free, and the subtraction of one block then underflows the length into the type bits, turning the entry into a bogus continuation. An extent running past the end of the partition makes it return blocks behind the partition. Such tables are not only found on crafted images: until the previous commit, udf_table_new_block() itself left zero-length extents behind in tables written by mkudffs, and then converted them into extents running past the partition. Check every extent once when the table is loaded, and refuse read-write access if one is empty, is not a whole number of blocks, or does not lie inside the partition, in the same way as for other allocation information the kernel cannot use. items.title: CVE-2026-99602: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: udf: don't let the extent type hide an exhausted free-space table extent udf_table_new_block() takes the first
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: udf: don't let the extent type hide an exhausted free-space table extent udf_table_new_block() takes the first block of the free-space table extent closest to the goal. It keeps that extent's type and length together in goal_elen, subtracts one block, and deletes the extent only if goal_elen then reaches zero. UDF 2.60 section 2.3.7.1 requires the free-space extents of an Unallocated Space Entry to be of type 1 (allocated but not recorded), and mkudffs writes them that way. For such an extent the type bits keep goal_elen non-zero, so taking its last block leaves a type-1 extent of length zero behind, starting at the block after the extent, which is in use. The next allocation that picks this empty extent returns that in-use block. items.title: CVE-2026-99603: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mptcp: pm: kernel: use RCU to free endpoint listeners mptcp_pm_nl_create_listen_socket() starts the TCP listen
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mptcp: pm: kernel: use RCU to free endpoint listeners mptcp_pm_nl_create_listen_socket() starts the TCP listener directly instead of going through mptcp_listen(). It consequently misses setting SOCK_RCU_FREE on the parent MPTCP socket. tcp_child_process() can invoke the listener's subflow_data_ready() callback without holding the MPTCP parent lock or a reference to the parent. An authenticated MP_JOIN racing with endpoint teardown can therefore access the parent after its last reference has been dropped. The ADD_ADDR error path can also close an already published listener. Set SOCK_RCU_FREE before __inet_listen_sk() publishes the TCP listener, matching mptcp_listen(). This protects the parent on every subsequent close path, including a failed endpoint addition.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/etnaviv: Flush the tile status cache through both the PE and BLT Since commit f232d9ec029c ("drm/etnaviv: fix TS cache flushing on GPUs with BLT engine"), jobs on GPUs with a BLT engine use a BLT command to flush the tile status cache instead of TS_FLUSH_CACHE, which is broken on most of these GPUs. GC7000 r6008/r6009 and GC8200 r6401 are the other way around: TS_FLUSH_CACHE works, but the BLT command does not flush the cache. The vendor driver handles these GPUs using TS_FLUSH_CACHE, but the etnaviv kernel driver has no way to identify them. As a result, dirty tile status cache lines survive the end of a job. They are written back by the next cache flush, using the page table of the job issuing it. If that job belongs to another process, the write goes to the wrong address space. On GC7000 r6009 this causes MMU faults and GPU recoveries blamed on an innocent process. I see around 1100 per run of a multisample depth/stencil test running alongside two other GPU clients. items.title: CVE-2026-99605: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/etnaviv: Fix NULL dereference on unbind without PPU flop reset flop_reset_data_ppu is only allocated on GP
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: drm/etnaviv: Fix NULL dereference on unbind without PPU flop reset flop_reset_data_ppu is only allocated on GPUs that need the PPU flop reset. However, etnaviv_unbind(..) frees it unconditionally, and etnaviv_cmdbuf_free(..) dereferences cmdbuf->suballoc before checking whether cmdbuf is NULL. items.title: CVE-2026-99606: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/smc: don't spin in smc_rx_recvmsg() while a pipe holds spliced data While bytes spliced off the RMB are st
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/smc: don't spin in smc_rx_recvmsg() while a pipe holds spliced data While bytes spliced off the RMB are still in a pipe, recvmsg() waits for the pipe to release them before it copies the data behind them. The path to that wait skips the timeout and signal checks, and smc_rx_wait() returns at once on RCV_SHUTDOWN. With a signal pending, after SHUT_RD, or once the peer closes or shuts down writing, recvmsg() spins on a CPU until the pipe is drained, and SIGKILL cannot stop it. MSG_DONTWAIT and an expired SO_RCVTIMEO wait there too instead of returning -EAGAIN. Check the timeout and signals before that wait, and end it when the pipe releases the data or the connection is killed, not on RCV_SHUTDOWN. A zero-length read returns 0 without waiting for the pipe; a non-blocking one returns -EAGAIN while poll() still reports the socket readable (splice() can still take those bytes). The wait sets SOCKWQ_ASYNC_WAITDATA like smc_rx_wait(), so a byte arriving behind the pipe raises no SIGIO on a reader already asleep for it, and a full barrier orders its wait queue entry before its read of splice_pending, so no wake is lost

items.title: CVE-2026-99607: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ext2: preserve IOMAP_F_DIRTY for extending direct writes ext2_iomap_begin() sets IOMAP_F_DIRTY for writes that
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ext2: preserve IOMAP_F_DIRTY for extending direct writes ext2_iomap_begin() sets IOMAP_F_DIRTY for writes that may extend i_size, but clears the flag after ext2_get_blocks(). When the write uses an existing mapped block, iomap can then use FUA and skip generic_write_sync(), even though ext2_dio_write_end_io() updates the inode size. An O_DSYNC write can therefore return without persisting the new size. For example, on a FUA-capable device, a 512-byte O_DIRECT|O_DSYNC write at offset 512 into a fsynced one-byte file returns successfully and extends the in-memory size to 1024, while an immediate read of the on-disk inode still shows size 1. An explicit fsync persists the new size. Move setting of IOMAP_F_DIRTY after the initialization.

items.title: CVE-2026-99608: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: usx2y: Guard the playback copy usx2y_urb_play_prepare() sums the packet lengths of a whole URB, copies t
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: usx2y: Guard the playback copy usx2y_urb_play_prepare() sums the packet lengths of a whole URB, copies that many frames with a single wrap, and sizes each playback packet from the capture packet's actual_length. Three things are unchecked: that the URB fits in the ring buffer, that a packet fits in the playback endpoint's maxpacksize, from which tmpbuf is allocated, and that actual_length is a whole number of frames. The ISO descriptors take the raw actual_length while transfer_buffer_length and the copies take count * stride, so a packet that is not a multiple of the stride makes the descriptors add up to more than the buffer, by up to stride - 1 bytes per packet. Return -EPIPE, as the existing packet-size check does, when the URB is larger than the buffer or a packet is larger than maxpacksize, and size each descriptor from whole frames, so the descriptors add up to transfer_buffer_length and each stays within maxpacksize. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: srcu: Add list_splice_init_srcu() list_splice_init_rcu() makes a list look empty to new readers, waits for the current ones with the given sync function, and only then links the entries into the new list. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: udf: fix preallocation discarding before an empty allocation extent udf_discard_prealloc() finds the last extent of a file by peeking at the next one with udf_next_aext() and stopping when that returns 0. items.title: CVE-2026-99587: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ata: libata-scsi: reject data-in commands with a data-out buffer SG_IO can submit a data-in SCSI command with
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ata: libata-scsi: reject data-in commands with a data-out buffer SG_IO can submit a data-in SCSI command with DMA_TO_DEVICE. The scatterlist can then contain pages pinned without write access. ata_scsi_rbuf_fill() writes simulated replies to that scatterlist; in the reported case, the copy tried to write the shared zero page and faulted in the kernel. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: batman-adv: tt: clear ROAM flag when re-adding a pending local client When a ROAMING_ADV is received for an announced local client, batadv_tt_local_mark_removed() sets BATADV_TT_CLIENT_ROAM, queues a DEL|ROAM change and marks the entry as BATADV_TT_CLIENT_PENDING. If the client sends a frame again before the next TTVN commit, batadv_tt_local_add_existing() only clears the PENDING flag and returns early. The ADD cancels the queued DEL, but the entry keeps the ROAM flag: * batadv_is_my_client() reports the client as not served by this node * batadv_tt_local_client_is_roaming() reroutes unicast frames for it to the node which sent the ROAMING_ADV The ROAM flag is only removed with the next frame of the client. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ceph: clamp the inline data length in ceph_fill_inline_data() The MDS decides how much inline data to attach to a reply, and the client parses inline_len without any upper bound: ceph_decode_need() only verifies that the message actually carries that many bytes. ceph_fill_inline_data() then copies the data into a single folio with no length check, so a malicious or buggy MDS returning more inline data than the folio can hold writes past its end. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: iommu/amd: Force device table to maximum size IOMMU can perform out-of-bounds read of the device table entry (DTE) that is adjacent to the last DTE and falls outside the device table. For example, if the device table can hold 0 to N-1 entries, then the IOMMU can be made to fetch the Nth entry, which falls outside the device table. The device table is owned by the hypervisor (HV) and is assigned in 4KB pages that are contiguous in system physical address (SPA). If the out-of-bound DTE falls on a guest-owned page, then the guest can exploit this bug to setup malicious table walks to corrupt HV pages and/or bring down the system. Note that this bug does not manifest when the device table size is set to its maximum size of 2MB. Therefore, force the device table size to the maximum 2MB on affected processors. These are CPU family 0x17 (Zen1/Zen2) through family 0x1a (Zen5/BRH). This is a mitigation for CVE-2024-21963. kdump reuses the previous kernel's device table only when the size encoded in the IOMMU device-table register matches pci_seg->dev_table_size. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: x86/mm: Fix global ASID handed out to two processes On AMD CPUs with INVLPGB, two live processes can get the same MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE global ASID value. The two then hit each other's TLB entries, so each can read or corrupt the other's memory. The global ASID space is managed lazily. When a global ASID is freed, its bit is set in the global_asid_freed bitmap. Once the free ASID search reaches the end of the global_asid_used bitmap, a global flush is done to really reclaim the lazily freed global ASIDs. However, the current code can assign the same global ASID to two different processes, if one process is assigned MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE - 1, another process MAX_ASID_AVAILABLE, and both stick around (keeping their global ASID numbers in use) until the search wraps around again. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: arm64: sdei: Preserve the interrupted context's exception registers An SDEI event is dispatched by firmware regardless of PSTATE.DAIF, so it can interrupt the kernel where the exception registers are live: - exception entry, before kernel_entry has saved ELR_EL1/SPSR_EL1 and before the C handler has read ESR_EL1/FAR_EL1; - exception return, after kernel_exit has loaded ELR_EL1/SPSR_EL1 and before the ERET. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/shmem: honour F_SEAL_EXEC when an ACL is set The owner of a memfd sealed with F_SEAL_EXEC can still change its execute bits by setting a POSIX access ACL. items.title: CVE-2026-99582: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: sctp: re-point retained control chunks on association migration sctp_sock_migrate() transfers DATA chunk owner
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: sctp: re-point retained control chunks on association migration sctp_sock_migrate() transfers DATA chunk ownership but leaves retained control chunks pointing at the old socket. A later retransmission can therefore access the socket after it has been freed. Extend the migration walk to cover retained control chunks and use sctp_control_set_owner_w() to assign their new owner. Reuse the DATA ownership check so each chunk is processed once per pass, even when it is reachable through multiple lists or retained pointers.
