An unauthenticated remote attacker can thereby cause script code to be executed in the browser of a visitor or administrator who opens a crafted link; in the case of an administrator, actions can be performed with the administrator's privileges. Third-party plugins whose portlets evaluate property values as templates can additionally be made to execute template code through the same entry point. This is a separate flaw in such plugins and does not affect the portlets of JTL-Shop itself.

items.title: CVE-2026-130811: @fastify/static is the Fastify plugin for serving static files. In versions up to and including 10.1.11, when it is configured to deny or ignore dotfiles together with directory li
items.summary: @fastify/static is the Fastify plugin for serving static files. In versions up to and including 10.1.11, when it is configured to deny or ignore dotfiles together with directory listing enabled, a request for a denied dot-directory returns its directory listing instead of being refused. The underlying send step answers with a forbidden response, but the listing fallback misreads that response on a path ending in a slash as a directory without an index file and serves the listing anyway. An unauthenticated client can enumerate the names of files and subdirectories, recursively, inside dot-directories the operator explicitly denied, such as version control, backup, and key file names. File contents remain protected and only names are disclosed. The issue is fixed in @fastify/static 10.1.12, and users should upgrade to 10.1.12 or later. As a workaround, disable directory listing or do not serve a root that contains dot-directories.

items.title: CVE-2026-129231: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10
items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. items.title: CVE-2026-129233: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 u
items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. items.title: CVE-2026-129229: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 u
items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. items.title: CVE-2026-128138: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.3 u
items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.6.7 until 3.10.4, nltk.downloader follows collection membership without tracking already visited collection nodes. A self-referencing or mutually referencing collection index can therefore make the package-closure walk loop indefinitely while its queue and memory usage grow, denying service when a victim processes the attacker-influenced index. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: CVE-2026-129221: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10
items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, nltk.classify.weka.ARFF_Formatter writes attacker-controlled class labels into the Weka ARFF @ATTRIBUTE '-label-' declaration without safely formatting the label tokens. Crafted labels can alter the generated ARFF schema or records, corrupting classifier input and causing integrity loss or processing failure. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: CVE-2026-128135: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.9.4 to
items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.9.4 to 3.10.3, NLTK ZIP package extraction can write through an existing in-root hardlink whose other link points outside the NLTK data root. A local attacker who can prepare the extraction target can cause a package member write to overwrite an out-of-root file, violating the pathsec containment boundary and affecting integrity and availability. This issues is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. items.title: CVE-2026-120298: InfoScan fails to properly handle certain malformed or incomplete requests to its login and password-reset endpoints. These requests can trigger unhandled server exceptions that re
items.summary: InfoScan fails to properly handle certain malformed or incomplete requests to its login and password-reset endpoints. These requests can trigger unhandled server exceptions that return detailed Node.js stack traces to the requester. The responses disclose internal filesystem paths, application directory names, source file locations, and line numbers.

items.title: CVE-2026-115515: @fastify/static is the Fastify plugin for serving static files. In versions before 10.1.8, the allowedPath guard receives only the requested pathname, but the underlying send step
items.summary: @fastify/static is the Fastify plugin for serving static files. In versions before 10.1.8, the allowedPath guard receives only the requested pathname, but the underlying send step selects the file to serve afterwards, so a request for a directory resolves to its default index file and an extensionless request resolves through the configured extensions to a matching file. The selected file is streamed without being re-checked against allowedPath, so a guard that denies a specific file is bypassed by requesting its directory or extensionless form. An unauthenticated client can read files inside the static root that the application meant to keep private whenever the denied file is reachable as a directory index or an extension match. The issue is fixed in @fastify/static 10.1.8, and users should upgrade to 10.1.8 or later. As a workaround, also deny the directory and extensionless forms in allowedPath, or disable the index and extensions options.

items.title: CVE-2026-117659: The InfoScan Electron desktop client improperly handles TLS certificate errors by accepting certificates without validating their trustworthiness. The client also configures Electr
items.summary: The InfoScan Electron desktop client improperly handles TLS certificate errors by accepting certificates without validating their trustworthiness. The client also configures Electron with nodeIntegration enabled, contextIsolation disabled, and webSecurity disabled. These settings weaken the client’s security boundaries. An attacker who is able to intercept or manipulate network communications may be able to present an untrusted certificate without the application rejecting the connection.

items.summary: The publicly distributed InfoScan Electron installer contains configuration files identifying hostnames associated with customer installations and internal development, testing, and database infrastructure. items.title: CVE-2026-120255: InfoScan uses hard-coded cryptographic keys and initialization-vector values in its database-encryption implementation. The application uses these values to encrypt the MongoDB pas
items.summary: InfoScan uses hard-coded cryptographic keys and initialization-vector values in its database-encryption implementation. The application uses these values to encrypt the MongoDB password before storing it in the Windows registry. Because the cryptographic material is embedded in the distributed application, an individual with access to the encrypted registry value and the application code may be able to recover the database password.

items.summary: InfoScan contains an unauthenticated information disclosure vulnerability in its mobile-enumeration and version-reporting endpoints. items.title: CVE-2026-77377: Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.4, the authenticated URL-upload endpoint and authenticated embed endpoint fet
items.summary: Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. items.summary: Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. items.title: CVE-2026-77379: Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.4, the public Relation API lacks an access-control filter. Unauthenticated us
items.summary: Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.4, the public Relation API lacks an access-control filter. Unauthenticated users can query its REST endpoints and GraphQL endpoints to discover metadata about unpublished, draft, and viewless content. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.4.

items.title: CVE-2026-77380: Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.5, the /bolt/async/upload-url and /bolt/async/embed endpoints validate only a
items.summary: Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.5, the /bolt/async/upload-url and /bolt/async/embed endpoints validate only a submitted URL before fetching it server-side. The fetchers then follow redirects without revalidating each destination, allowing an authenticated user to bypass UrlSafetyChecker and cause the server to request internal or cloud-metadata addresses. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.5.

items.title: CVE-2026-77382: falcon-rust is a Rust implementation of the Falcon post-quantum signature scheme. Prior to 0.2.0, the discrete-Gaussian sampler in src/samplerz.rs evaluates approx_exp, ber_exp, an
items.summary: falcon-rust is a Rust implementation of the Falcon post-quantum signature scheme. Prior to 0.2.0, the discrete-Gaussian sampler in src/samplerz.rs evaluates approx_exp, ber_exp, and sampler_z acceptance probabilities with FixedPoint64 values having only 32 fractional bits. The scaling in approx_exp quantizes its input and limits relative precision to about 2^-33, below Falcon's required bound, causing reference known-answer vectors to diverge and invalidating the proof assumption that secret-dependent signature and key distributions are negligibly close to the ideal discrete Gaussian. This is a cryptographic-soundness defect and no practical key-recovery attack has been demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 0.2.0.

items.title: CVE-2026-77318: Jupyter MCP Server is a Model Context Protocol server for Jupyter. Prior to 1.0.3, standalone streamable-http mode can enforce MCP_TOKEN on /mcp while leaving the state-changing /a
items.summary: Jupyter MCP Server is a Model Context Protocol server for Jupyter. Prior to 1.0.3, standalone streamable-http mode can enforce MCP_TOKEN on /mcp while leaving the state-changing /api/connect and /api/stop management routes unauthenticated. An unauthenticated network caller can use /api/connect to replace runtime_url and document_url values and their tokens, reset ServerContext, and start a kernel client against attacker-controlled infrastructure, causing the server to send Jupyter API and WebSocket traffic to that backend. The caller can also use /api/stop to stop the current notebook kernel. This boundary failure does not require explicit insecure no-auth mode and occurs outside normal MCP JSON-RPC tool dispatch. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.3.

items.title: CVE-2026-77336: Aperi'Solve is an open-source steganalysis web platform. Prior to 3.4.2, an unauthenticated user can submit a PNG to POST /upload, which reaches aperisolve/utils/png.py through ana
items.summary: Aperi'Solve is an open-source steganalysis web platform. Prior to 3.4.2, an unauthenticated user can submit a PNG to POST /upload, which reaches aperisolve/utils/png.py through analyze_image, PCRTAnalyzer, PNG.repair(), and check_idat(). A malformed IDAT chunk can make attacker-controlled length and newline data drive an unbounded combinations search in PNG._fix_dos2unix(), causing repeated CRC checks that occupy a worker and delay or block image analysis for other users. Per-IP upload limits and eventual job termination bound the denial of service, and the issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 3.4.2.

items.title: CVE-2026-77338: Sprout Track is a self-hosted baby tracking application. Prior to 1.3.5, Sprout Track uses a publicly known hardcoded signing secret when JWT_SECRET is unset, and standard setup do
items.summary: Sprout Track is a self-hosted baby tracking application. Prior to 1.3.5, Sprout Track uses a publicly known hardcoded signing secret when JWT_SECRET is unset, and standard setup does not generate a unique secret. On a network-reachable affected deployment, an unauthenticated attacker can sign JWTs with arbitrary claims, including system-administrator claims, to access administrative functionality and read or modify family, child activity, account, and email data. Deployments with a strong unique JWT_SECRET are not affected. Managed and hosted instances were reported remediated. This issue is fixed in version 1.3.5.

items.title: CVE-2026-77359: Jupyter MCP Server is a Model Context Protocol server for Jupyter. Prior to 1.0.3, standalone streamable-http mode validates Host and Origin values for /mcp but does not apply the
items.summary: Jupyter MCP Server is a Model Context Protocol server for Jupyter. Prior to 1.0.3, standalone streamable-http mode validates Host and Origin values for /mcp but does not apply the same browser-origin controls to the state-changing /api/connect and /api/stop management routes. A malicious website can use DNS rebinding so that its hostname resolves to a loopback, LAN, VPN, or published-container MCP listener, then send a browser-shaped request that /api/connect accepts to replace runtime_url and document_url values and start a kernel client against attacker-controlled infrastructure. The attacker can thereby cause Jupyter API and WebSocket traffic to reach that infrastructure and can use /api/stop to stop the current notebook kernel. The default broad bind can increase exposure, but the vulnerability is the missing management-route origin boundary, not a lack of Host validation on /mcp. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.3.

items.title: CVE-2026-77367: Daptin is a GraphQL/JSON-API headless CMS. Prior to 0.12.30, the generic GET /api/{entity} list endpoint accepts attacker-controlled sort values in PaginatedFindAllWithoutFilters i
items.summary: Daptin is a GraphQL/JSON-API headless CMS. Prior to 0.12.30, the generic GET /api/{entity} list endpoint accepts attacker-controlled sort values in PaginatedFindAllWithoutFilters in server/resource/resource_findallpaginated.go without validating the requested column against the table schema. The code uses those values for SELECT and ORDER BY identifier construction, so an embedded identifier quote can terminate the quoted identifier and make the remainder parse as SQL, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to extract unauthorized table data through blind or error-based behavior or repeatedly trigger query failures. This issue is fixed in version 0.12.30.

items.title: CVE-2026-77369: Daptin is a GraphQL/JSON-API headless CMS. From 0.11.4 until 0.12.30, the generic GET /yjs/:documentName WebSocket route in InitializeYjsResources requires a session but does not a
items.summary: Daptin is a GraphQL/JSON-API headless CMS. From 0.11.4 until 0.12.30, the generic GET /yjs/:documentName WebSocket route in InitializeYjsResources requires a session but does not authorize the database resource selected by a typename.referenceId.columnName room name. The YJS initial-content provider then reads the selected file.* column without CanRead or CanUpdate checks, and bidirectional synchronization allows a low-privileged authenticated user to read or modify restricted row content. Unauthenticated requests are rejected, and standalone non-canonical room names remain shared-by-name rooms. This issue is fixed in version 0.12.30.

items.title: CVE-2026-47278: Frappe is a full-stack web application framework. Prior to 15.108.0 and 16.18.3, the add_comment handler in frappe/templates/includes/comments/comments.py trusts the client-provide
items.summary: Frappe is a full-stack web application framework. Prior to 15.108.0 and 16.18.3, the add_comment handler in frappe/templates/includes/comments/comments.py trusts the client-provided comment_by and comment_email fields. A caller can submit chosen identity metadata that is stored with a comment, causing the comment to appear to originate from another name or email address. This issue is fixed in versions 15.108.0 and 16.18.3.

items.title: CVE-2026-59988: django-docutils provides reStructuredText support for Django. Prior to 0.30.0, public rendering paths including publish_doctree, publish_html_from_source, publish_html_from_doctree
items.summary: django-docutils provides reStructuredText support for Django. Prior to 0.30.0, public rendering paths including publish_doctree, publish_html_from_source, publish_html_from_doctree, publish_parts_from_doctree, the {% rst %} template tag, the rst template filter, DocutilsTemplates, and DocutilsView pass lower-trust reStructuredText to Docutils without disabling file_insertion_enabled, raw_enabled, ambient docutils.conf processing, or unsafe URI schemes and without consistently sanitizing doctrees. An attacker who can influence rendered reStructuredText can use include or csv-table directives to read local files or cause server-side URL requests, or use raw HTML and unsafe URI output to inject stored script-capable content. Applications that render only trusted static reStructuredText are not affected unless attackers can influence it. This issue is fixed in version 0.30.0.

items.title: CVE-2026-69260: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.5.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS does not format the SSH URL path component as a single argument when constructing remote obje
items.summary: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.5.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS does not format the SSH URL path component as a single argument when constructing remote object-transfer or authentication commands. Shell metacharacters in the SSH URL can therefore escape the intended path argument and cause arbitrary command execution when the remote Git LFS service passes received commands to a shell without adequate sanitization. Git LFS also incorrectly encodes default HTTPS URLs when an SSH URL is configured and the remote host either does not support Git LFS remote commands over SSH or supports HTTP authentication over SSH but git-lfs-authenticate does not return an explicit HTTP URL. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

items.title: CVE-2026-69261: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.5.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS may forward a Cookie header after an HTTP redirect to a host other than the one for which the
items.summary: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.5.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS may forward a Cookie header after an HTTP redirect to a host other than the one for which the header was intended. That unintended host can therefore receive cookies containing credentials or other confidential values. Authorization headers are never forwarded to inappropriate hosts and are not the affected secret in this vulnerability. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

items.title: CVE-2026-22309: The visitor tracking of JTL-Shop automatically registers unknown crawler user agents without filtering the value, and the stored value is rendered without output encoding on severa
items.summary: The visitor tracking of JTL-Shop automatically registers unknown crawler user agents without filtering the value, and the stored value is rendered without output encoding on several pages of the administration backend (search engine statistics, crawler dashboard widget, crawler edit form, sitemap export download list and campaign details). An unauthenticated remote attacker can store script code with a single request. The code is executed in the browser session of an administrator who opens one of these pages, allowing actions to be performed with the administrator's privileges.

items.title: CVE-2026-22310: When the setting for saving requests to non-existent pages (404) is enabled, JTL-Shop stores the raw requested URL in its redirect table, and the administration backend renders it
items.summary: When the setting for saving requests to non-existent pages (404) is enabled, JTL-Shop stores the raw requested URL in its redirect table, and the administration backend renders it without output encoding in the form used to edit a redirect. An unauthenticated remote attacker can store script code with a single request, which is executed in the browser session of an administrator who opens the affected redirect, allowing actions to be performed with the administrator's privileges. The setting is disabled by default in new installations but may still be enabled in older ones.

items.title: CVE-2026-133324: A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct an authentic
items.summary: A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct an authentication bypass attack due to improper handling of authentication. items.title: CVE-2026-133307: ClassiCube before 1.4.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Png_Decode in src/Bitmap.c that allows malicious servers to corrupt client memory by sending a PN
items.summary: ClassiCube before 1.4.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Png_Decode in src/Bitmap.c that allows malicious servers to corrupt client memory by sending a PNG with a duplicate IHDR chunk. Attackers can supply crafted PNGs via texture pack URLs or player skins so the unreset bufferIdx underflows remaining space, letting IDAT data overflow the buffer to crash clients or execute code.

items.summary: ClassiCube before 1.4.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Png_Reconstruct in src/Bitmap.c that occurs when AVERAGE and PAETH filters process zero-width PNG images. items.summary: @scalar/typebox before 0.1.4 contains a code injection vulnerability in TypeCompiler that allows attackers to execute JavaScript by supplying crafted schema strings. items.summary: Wing FTP Server before 8.2.8 contains a file mask bypass vulnerability allowing attackers to upload restricted files via an embedded NUL byte in Upload Link filenames. items.title: CVE-2026-133311: A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker, with knowledge of a sp
items.summary: A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker, with knowledge of a specific system-generated random identifier or pre-staged content, to conduct an unauthorized access attack due to improper authentication mechanisms. The vulnerability is limited to the affected functionality and does not provide unrestricted access to arbitrary files elsewhere on the system. This is MTLVULN-1863.

items.title: CVE-2026-133323: A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct a blind comm
items.summary: A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct a blind command injection attack due to insufficient parameter sanitization. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. This is MTLVULN-1864.

items.title: CVE-2026-133276: When extra data is allowed (extra=Extra.allow), providing a __pydantic_initialised__ key when validating a Pydantic V1 dataclass makes it considered as already validated, resulting
items.summary: When extra data is allowed (extra=Extra.allow), providing a __pydantic_initialised__ key when validating a Pydantic V1 dataclass makes it considered as already validated, resulting in field values not being validated. The __init__() method of Pydantic V1 dataclasses stores all the provided keyword arguments in the instance __dict__ before validation, so a __pydantic_initialised__ keyword argument overrides the internal flag used to skip validation of already validated instances. As a result, data returned by validation doesn't match the declared type. Affected are applications validating untrusted data into Pydantic V1 dataclasses allowing extra data. The issue was fixed in Pydantic 1.10.27. Users relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2 should upgrade to 2.14.2 or later.

items.title: CVE-2026-133303: A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to leverage pre-staged
items.summary: A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to leverage pre-staged malicious content to conduct an XML injection attack due to insufficient parameter validation. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. This is MTLVULN-1862.

items.title: CVE-2026-133305: sqlmap before 1.10.11.89 contains a credential exposure vulnerability that allows attackers to capture user-supplied Cookie and Authorization headers by redirecting requests to ano
items.summary: sqlmap before 1.10.11.89 contains a credential exposure vulnerability that allows attackers to capture user-supplied Cookie and Authorization headers by redirecting requests to another host. Attackers controlling the scanned target or abusing an open redirect can make RedirectHandler.http_error_302 forward session cookies or bearer tokens to an attacker-controlled host.

items.title: CVE-2026-133306: VideoLAN libaacs 0.7.0 through 0.12.0 on non-macOS, non-Windows builds contains stack-based buffer overflows in aacs_resolve_path() in src/file/path.c from length checks against th
items.summary: VideoLAN libaacs 0.7.0 through 0.12.0 on non-macOS, non-Windows builds contains stack-based buffer overflows in aacs_resolve_path() in src/file/path.c from length checks against the wrong buffer. Local attackers can place a symlink with a long target on a disc path a user opens to overflow resolved_path[] and link[], crashing the process or potentially executing code if mitigations are bypassed.

items.title: CVE-2026-133200: A flaw was found in quarkus-vertx-utils. When a client disconnects while receiving a streaming response, the server fails to detect the closed connection and continues processing t
items.summary: A flaw was found in quarkus-vertx-utils. When a client disconnects while receiving a streaming response, the server fails to detect the closed connection and continues processing the data indefinitely. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this issue by repeatedly initiating streaming requests and disconnecting, exhausting worker threads and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

items.title: CVE-2026-133189: A command injection vulnerability was found in OpenStack Cinder's SSH-based storage-driver support. Incomplete validation of shell metacharacters allows an authenticated user who o
items.summary: A command injection vulnerability was found in OpenStack Cinder's SSH-based storage-driver support. Incomplete validation of shell metacharacters allows an authenticated user who owns a volume on an affected backend to supply crafted connection information and inject additional commands into the storage array's management interface. Commands execute with the privileges of Cinder's configured backend account. This can disclose storage configuration information and, where that account has administrative permissions, could allow changes that affect the integrity or availability of other tenants' storage.

items.title: CVE-2026-133007: A flaw was found in GIMP. Opening a crafted XCF with a truncated uncompressed tile can expose uninitialized main-process stack memory through the imported layer's pixel data, which
items.summary: A flaw was found in GIMP. Opening a crafted XCF with a truncated uncompressed tile can expose uninitialized main-process stack memory through the imported layer's pixel data, which may include process addresses that weaken ASLR.

items.title: CVE-2026-131610: In ConnectWise Automate versions prior to 2026.11, a condition in Web Control Center (WCC2) authorization handling could allow an authenticated contact user to access information a
items.summary: In ConnectWise Automate versions prior to 2026.11, a condition in Web Control Center (WCC2) authorization handling could allow an authenticated contact user to access information associated with other clients on the same Automate server through API requests. This may result in disclosure of information outside the user’s assigned access scope. The issue is limited to information disclosure and does not extend existing modification or command execution permissions. This issue is resolved in ConnectWise Automate 2026.11.

items.title: CVE-2026-129232: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10
items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, XMLCorpusView.read_block rebuilds the full root-to-node context path with "/".join(context) for every start tag while searching for a matching element. Deeply nested attacker-influenced corpus XML therefore causes quadratic pure-Python work and can pin a processing worker, resulting in denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: CVE-2026-129234: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10
items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, Prover9Parent.config_prover9 and Mace accept a relative binary_location and pass it to find_binary as path_to_bin, disabling the bare-name absolute-path guard. A local attacker who can plant prover9 or mace4 in the resolved working directory can cause subprocess.Popen to execute that binary with the invoking user's privileges. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.title: CVE-2026-105802: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.6.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS reads Git configuration options defined for a submodule without checking certain values for e
items.summary: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.6.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS reads Git configuration options defined for a submodule without checking certain values for embedded line-ending control characters. A malicious repository can insert control characters such as line feed (LF) into those values to mimic options that cause Git LFS to execute an attacker-controlled command or binary while fetching or adding objects. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

items.title: CVE-2026-105803: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 1.3.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS does not correctly filter the limited set of options permitted in a repository's .lfsconfig f
items.summary: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 1.3.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS does not correctly filter the limited set of options permitted in a repository's .lfsconfig file when option keys contain certain additional components. Crafted keys can mimic options that configure Git LFS to use a custom command to transfer objects, causing Git LFS to execute an attacker-selected command or binary while fetching objects. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

items.title: phpAfterShell Explained: How Hackers Could Turn a PHP Session Flaw Into Code Execution
items.summary: PHP's default file-based session storage can be made to return objects an attacker chose, by cutting off a session write at the right moment. When combined with a second weakness, such as a suitable gadget chain in the app, those objects can allow the attacker to run code on the server. Today's PHP releases fix the flaw, called phpAfterShell. The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-126714 and rated

items.title: CVE-2026-63390: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the BCF reader can experience an integer overflow in a record-le
items.summary: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the BCF reader can experience an integer overflow in a record-length check that verifies whether a record contains enough bytes for the expected number and size of stored items. A crafted BCF record can bypass this check, causing reads beyond the stored data and, in some cases, writes beyond the heap buffer when the reader sets the least significant bit of accessed bytes. Opening such a file can crash the process, corrupt data or heap structures, and may permit arbitrary code execution. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

items.title: CVE-2026-62259: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the experimental CRAM v4 functions cram_xpack_decode_char and cr
items.summary: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the experimental CRAM v4 functions cram_xpack_decode_char and cram_xrle_decode_char do not validate that attacker-controlled decode sizes remain within their expanded input arrays. Crafted CRAM data can therefore make either decoder read beyond the supplied input buffer, potentially disclosing process-state information or crashing the process through invalid memory access. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

items.title: CVE-2026-62260: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the CRAM BETA decoder functions cram_beta_decode_long, cram_beta
items.summary: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the CRAM BETA decoder functions cram_beta_decode_long, cram_beta_decode_int, and cram_beta_decode_char, and the experimental CRAM v4 XPACK functions cram_xpack_decode_long and cram_xpack_decode_int, have bounds-checking flaws caused by integer overflow after a multiplication. The resulting incorrect bounds check can allow decoding to read beyond the supplied input buffer, potentially leaking process-state information or crashing the process. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

items.title: CVE-2026-62255: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, cram_index_load does not verify that the number of reference seq
items.summary: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, cram_index_load does not verify that the number of reference sequences in a CRAM .crai index does not exceed the CRAM header reference count. A malformed index can drive unbounded index-array allocation, and when the number of references in the index is within two of INT_MAX, the growth calculation can wrap, read beyond a heap buffer, and use the resulting value as a pointer for an unchecked memory write. Any region query can trigger the flaw, causing denial of service or memory corruption. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

items.title: CVE-2026-62256: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, fai_retrieve does not verify that the line width recorded in a F
items.summary: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, fai_retrieve does not verify that the line width recorded in a FASTA .fai index is greater than or equal to the number of bases per line. When the line width is exactly one less than the base count, retrieval allocates an undersized heap buffer and writes one byte beyond its end; larger discrepancies instead cause an allocation failure that is handled. This issue can corrupt heap memory and crash the process. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

items.title: CVE-2026-62257: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the experimental CRAM v4 XPACK and XRLE decoders cache expanded
items.summary: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the experimental CRAM v4 XPACK and XRLE decoders cache expanded block pointers at indexes beyond the 512-element slice->block_by_id array. An array index partially controlled by data in the input file first causes an out-of-bounds read to determine whether a block is cached; a null value then causes allocation of a block and an out-of-bounds pointer write to the same element. The invalid read may crash the process, while the write may corrupt heap state and could permit arbitrary code execution. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

items.title: CVE-2026-62258: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the CRAM decoder validates the 254-character query-name limit on
items.summary: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the CRAM decoder validates the 254-character query-name limit only after decoding the name into a 1024-byte stack array. An attacker-controlled CRAM record can provide an overlong query name and overflow the local stack buffer before the later validation runs; all CRAM format versions are affected. Opening such a file can crash the process, corrupt stack data, and may permit arbitrary code execution. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

items.summary: parse5 7.0.0 before 8.1.1 contains an uncaught exception vulnerability in Preprocessor#_processSurrogate that allows remote attackers to crash applications by supplying two consecutive low surrogates. items.summary: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP UpdateFirmware Out-Of-Bounds Write Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. items.title: CVE-2026-99564: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: smbdirect: don't wait for RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED in smbdirect_socket_destroy_sync() smbdirect_socket_
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: smbdirect: don't wait for RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED in smbdirect_socket_destroy_sync() smbdirect_socket_destroy_sync() waited for RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED after smbdirect_socket_cleanup_work() called rdma_disconnect(). That can take very long, e.g. if the peer just disappeared, until the rdma cm gives up, or forever if the event already happened, but the status was overwritten afterwards. This is not needed: smbdirect_socket_destroy() drains the qp under rdma_lock_handler(), destroys it and calls rdma_destroy_id(), which only waits for a currently running event handler and makes sure no further events are delivered. The rest of the disconnect protocol (DREQ/DREP and timewait for IB, abrupt close for iWarp) is handled by the rdma core asynchronously. drivers/nvme/host/rdma.c also just calls rdma_disconnect() and ib_drain_qp() before rdma_destroy_id(). So smbdirect_socket_destroy() now also accepts SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_DISCONNECTING and changes the status to SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_DISCONNECTED itself under rdma_lock_handler(). We could still get RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED in the small windows between rdma_unlock_handle

items.title: CVE-2026-99565: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: wait for negotiation before receiving another PDU The receive thread queues a request and can read the
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: wait for negotiation before receiving another PDU The receive thread queues a request and can read the next PDU before the negotiation worker finishes. While need_neg is set, the next PDU can cause ksmbd_init_smb_server() to replace conn->ops. A pipelined SMB2 request can therefore make the worker handle an earlier, shorter SMB1 request with SMB2 operations and read beyond its buffer. An SMB1 multi-protocol negotiate may be followed by an SMB2 NEGOTIATE that changes conn->ops again. Wait for work queued while the connection is new or needs negotiation to complete before reading another PDU. This keeps the operations stable for both stages of negotiation without changing when need_neg is cleared.

items.title: CVE-2026-99556: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: serialize directory emptiness checks with readdir SMB2 QUERY_DIRECTORY holds fp->readdir_lock while it
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: serialize directory emptiness checks with readdir SMB2 QUERY_DIRECTORY holds fp->readdir_lock while it calls iterate_dir() on fp->filp. An SMB2 SET_INFO request with FILE_DISPOSITION_INFORMATION can resolve the same FileId and call ksmbd_vfs_empty_dir() on the same filp without that lock. iterate_dir()'s inode read lock permits concurrent readers and does not serialize per-file iterator state. ext4 stores its dx readdir cursor and fname RB tree in file->private_data. Concurrent reset or refill can therefore free a fname node while the other worker still traverses it or retains its RB-tree link, resulting in use-after-free accesses. An authenticated SMB client with list and delete rights on a directory in a writable KSMBD share backed by ext4 can trigger this when the directory takes the dx readdir path. The client overlaps an SMB2 QUERY_DIRECTORY request with an SMB2 SET_INFO request carrying FILE_DISPOSITION_INFORMATION on one live FileId. In one x86_64 SMP KASAN multi-shot guest using ksmbd-for-next at 171df27077fb, the unmodified kernel reported a cross-worker use-after-free before a panic. The first repo

items.title: CVE-2026-99559: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ARM: 9524/1: mm: align hugetlb mappings to the huge page size mmap(MAP_HUGETLB) on 32-bit Arm can return an ad
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ARM: 9524/1: mm: align hugetlb mappings to the huge page size mmap(MAP_HUGETLB) on 32-bit Arm can return an address which is not aligned to the huge page size. In a QEMU virt guest, unmapping the VMA then hits the alignment check in __unmap_hugepage_range(): kernel BUG at mm/hugetlb.c:5213! Internal error: Oops - BUG: 0 [#1] SMP ARM PC is at __unmap_hugepage_range+0x540/0x584 LR is at __zap_vma_range+0x13a0/0x1410 Commit 7bd3f1e1a9ae ("mm: make hugetlb mappings go through mm_get_unmapped_area_vmflags") made hugetlb mappings use the architecture's arch_get_unmapped_area(). The generic implementations handle hugetlb alignment, but the Arm implementations only account for the optional SHMLBA cache-colouring constraint. A 4 KiB-page kernel can therefore align the mapping to 4 KiB or 16 KiB instead of the required 2 MiB. Set the alignment mask from the file's hstate for hugetlb mappings in both Arm implementations. Huge-page alignment also satisfies the SHMLBA constraint.

items.title: CVE-2026-99561: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: fork: don't create io threads once PF_POSTCOREDUMP is set zap_process() skips every thread that already has PF
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: fork: don't create io threads once PF_POSTCOREDUMP is set zap_process() skips every thread that already has PF_POSTCOREDUMP set. Such a thread is past synchronize_group_exit(), so a coredump can't catch it anymore. It isn't counted in core_state->threads_remaining and it isn't sent SIGKILL. do_exit() sets PF_POSTCOREDUMP in synchronize_group_exit() and calls io_uring_files_cancel() right after that. The cancellation runs task work and a create_worker_cb() that io-wq queued before the exit creates a new io-wq worker from there. If another thread started a coredump in the meantime that worker joins a thread-group which is already being dumped. zap_process() never saw it so it was never counted. But when it exits it sees signal->core_state in synchronize_group_exit() and decrements threads_remaining like any other thread. So the count reaches zero one thread early and the dumper leaves coredump_wait_inactive() while a thread it counted is still running. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: smbdirect: release failed pending sockets of a listener A child of a listener only left the listen.pending or listen.ready list via smbdirect_socket_accept() or when the listener was destroyed. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: usb: pegasus: do not advance rx_skb->data on dropped frames For the 0x8513 chip, read_bulk_callback() skips the 2-byte receive header by advancing pegasus->rx_skb->data in place. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix parent dentry lifetime in directory enumeration ksmbd_populate_dot_dotdot_entries() builds the ".." entry from the open directory's d_parent and passes that pointer to ksmbd_vfs_fill_dentry_attrs() without taking a reference. That pointer is only valid while the directory stays under this parent. If a concurrent rename moves the directory elsewhere, the old parent loses its last reference; a following rmdir then turns it into a negative dentry with d_inode cleared, and after the RCU grace period the dentry itself is freed. The worker still holds the raw pointer and dereferences d_inode through vfs_getattr() and vfs_getxattr(). items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix OOB read and cross-share confusion in ksmbd_validate_name_reconnect() ksmbd_validate_name_reconnect() indexes ab_pathname[share->path_sz + 1] without checking that the path is longer than share->path_sz + 1 (d_path() fills the buffer from the end). A durable fp is not bound to its original share, so a client can preserve a file from a short-path share and reconnect it on a long-path share, making strcmp() read past the PATH_MAX buffer - with a long enough share path this oopses the kernel, and on a mapped page it also gives a byte-equality oracle on adjacent heap (the reconnect succeeds exactly when the out-of-bounds string equals the requested name). A same-share variant with the durable fp at the share root reads 1 byte past the buffer (strlen(ab_pathname) == share->path_sz). Check before comparing: the path must be longer than share->path_sz, it must start with share->path, and the next character must be '/'. The share root itself is accepted only for an empty name.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: deny access for an empty DACL instead of granting the request smb_check_perm_dacl() returns the access mask it computes to the SMB2 CREATE handler, which uses it as the granted access for the open. For a security descriptor whose DACL is present but contains no ACEs, the function is supposed to deny access: an empty (non-NULL) DACL grants no access to anyone except the object owner's implicit READ_CONTROL and WRITE_DAC (MS-DTYP 2.4.5). The empty-DACL branch only denies when both - the DACL has no trailing bytes (pdacl_size == sizeof(struct smb_acl)), and - the request contains bits beyond READ_CONTROL / WRITE_DAC. In every other case it takes the shared "goto err_out" with rc still 0, which returns success without modifying *pdaccess, so the caller grants the full requested access. Three problems follow: - The READ_CONTROL / WRITE_DAC carve-out models the owner's implicit rights, but the check runs before is_owner is computed, so those rights are handed to *every* caller, not just the owner. For READ_CONTROL the SMB2 CREATE path does not fall back to inode_permission(), so any user can read the security desc

items.title: CVE-2026-99544: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: Drivers: hv: vmbus: Bounds check the shared ring buffer indices In a CoCo VM the host is untrusted. Since the
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: Drivers: hv: vmbus: Bounds check the shared ring buffer indices In a CoCo VM the host is untrusted. Since the VMBus ring buffer read and write indices live in shared memory, the guest has to treat both as potentially malicious. hv_ringbuffer_write() copies into the ring at write_index with no bounds checking, so the host can make the guest write packet data at any offset up to 4 GiB past the start of the ring buffer. read_index matters too: the available space derived from both indices is the only bound on how much is copied, and an out-of-range index can make it far larger than the ring. The fix is to validate both indices before use and to use the validated snapshot instead of re-accessing. For invalid indices, hv_ringbuffer_write() logs and returns -EIO. One re-read of write_index is left unchecked in this patch: hv_get_ring_bufferindices() fetches it again for the prev_indices trailer. The value is only returned to the host and is not used as an offset or length for indexing. Since this is not a security issue, it is addressed later in the series. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net/sched: cls_flower: avoid stale mask references after delete Flower releases a mask reference when a filter is removed from the classifier. The filter object can remain alive while dump, walk, or hardware reoffload paths hold a reference to it. Those paths can then dereference f->mask after the mask has already been released. Keep the mask reference until the filter reference count reaches zero. Release the mask synchronously from the final __fl_put() while the caller still holds the tcf_proto reference, and leave the existing RCU work to free the mask. This keeps the mask available to every reader that still holds the filter. The filter is still removed from the classifier indexes immediately. Therefore, a deleted filter can temporarily retain an otherwise empty mask; fl_delete() uses the handle IDR, rather than the mask list, to determine whether the classifier has become empty. Failed mask assignment can leave fnew->mask as an error or borrowed pointer without an owned mask reference. Clear it before the common failure path so the final put cannot release an unowned reference. This fix does not add fields, sn

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: thunderbolt: Do not RPM complete unrelated subtrees on unplug When a Thunderbolt device is unplugged, that switch and every switch subsequent to it on the bus device list is `complete()`d, not just its child devices. In the case of multiple domains, it may cause, eg, an attempt to `complete()` the uninitialized domain 1 root switch RPM completion on unplug of a switch from domain 0 (though ordering is not guaranteed numerically sorted). I initially noticed this issue on a Dell XPS9720 when the system would seem to sporadically not wake after unplugging a Thunderbolt dock. I tried multiple kernel versions including v7.2.7 and v7.3-rc4 to see if that resolved the issue, but the issue persisted. Eventually I found that I could consistently generate a kernel Oops reporting a page fault at 0xffff_ffff_ffff_fff8 on unplug from one side of the laptop and went bug hunting. I became suspicious of the `bus_for_each_dev()` walk that I ultimately ended up changing. items.title: CVE-2026-99532: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: validate security descriptor offsets before pointer arithmetic parse_sec_desc() constructs SID and DACL
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: validate security descriptor offsets before pointer arithmetic parse_sec_desc() constructs SID and DACL pointers by adding untrusted 32-bit offsets to the security descriptor before checking their bounds. The existing checks reject offsets into the descriptor header, but do not reject offsets beyond the descriptor's length. On a 32-bit kernel, a large offset can wrap the pointer before the descriptor. The end-only checks in parse_sid() and parse_dacl() can then accept it, allowing an authenticated SMB2 SET_INFO request to access memory outside the security descriptor and fault the kernel. Check each nonzero offset against acl_len before constructing its pointer. Initialize the optional owner and group SID pointers to NULL so an omitted SID remains absent when parsing the DACL.

items.title: CVE-2026-99534: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: prevent stale data from being written by SMB2 WRITE requests Initialize the compatibility byte in reque
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: prevent stale data from being written by SMB2 WRITE requests Initialize the compatibility byte in request buffers without zeroing the entire allocation. Keep the one-byte compatibility exception for SMB2 messages so valid zero-length WRITE requests remain compatible, and validate the data range in the WRITE handlers against the current compound request before accessing it. This prevents stale request-buffer data from being written to files or sent to IPC pipes.

items.title: CVE-2026-99535: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: prevent share root removal through empty paths A FileLinkInformation request can supply "/" as the new
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: prevent share root removal through empty paths A FileLinkInformation request can supply "/" as the new link name. smb2_get_name() strips the trailing slash and passes an empty string to ksmbd_vfs_kern_path_start_removing(). ksmbd_vfs_path_lookup() resolves an empty pathname as the configured share path, without LOOKUP_BENEATH. With ReplaceIfExists set, smb2_create_link() can therefore remove the share root from its parent before link creation fails. An authenticated client with a writable share and DELETE access to a file can trigger this if the share root is empty and the mapped user has write and search permission on its parent directory. Return -EINVAL for empty pathnames when for_remove is set, before resolving the share path or acquiring removal resources. Ordinary lookups continue to accept empty pathnames for opening the share root.

items.title: CVE-2026-99536: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: prevent session binding in compound requests A failed multichannel binding can retain its target sessio
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: prevent session binding in compound requests A failed multichannel binding can retain its target session on the work item so that the error response can be signed. Subsequent compound commands can then use that session together with a tree connection left over from an earlier command. Limit binding SESSION_SETUP requests to standalone messages during message validation, before smb2_sess_setup() can replace work->sess. Check both NextCommand and the current request offset to cover binding in the first, middle and last positions of a compound. The existing validation error path returns STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER and stops processing the remaining commands. This intentionally limits support for compounded binding. It is not a protocol requirement that binding be standalone. Standalone binding and non-binding compounds retain their existing behavior, without changing session, tree or response encryption handling.

items.title: CVE-2026-99537: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: preserve unreadable named streams on open A write-only client can open an existing named stream with FI
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: preserve unreadable named streams on open A write-only client can open an existing named stream with FILE_OPEN_IF without permission to read the underlying file. The case-insensitive lookup finds the xattr name, but querying its value length then fails with -EACCES. smb2_set_stream_name_xattr() treats every negative result as a missing stream and replaces the existing xattr with an empty value. A failed xattr list is not proof that the stream is absent either: for example, -ENOMEM can lead to the same empty replacement. Preserve listing errors and create a stream only for -ENOENT or -ENODATA. The latter can occur if the xattr is removed between listing its name and querying its value. Return other lookup errors without changing the stream. A write-only FILE_OPEN now reports access denied instead of name not found. FILE_OVERWRITE_IF and FILE_SUPERSEDE on an unreadable stream also fail instead of appearing to replace it. Stream writes and EOF changes already need to read the old value, so such handles cannot update the stream after opening either.

items.title: CVE-2026-99538: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: ignore network devices of other namespaces With no interface list configured, ksmbd binds every interfa
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: ignore network devices of other namespaces With no interface list configured, ksmbd binds every interface that comes up. ksmbd_netdev_event() does not look at the device's namespace, and create_socket() opens the listener in the namespace of the task raising NETDEV_UP. A container with its own address on a bridge brings up its interface and finds port 445 in its namespace already taken by ksmbd, so an SMB server running inside the container fails with "Address already in use". Interfaces are also matched by name only, so a container's eth0 going down would stop the listener on the host's eth0. Only handle netdev events for devices in init_net.

items.title: CVE-2026-99539: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix session reference leak on compounded SESSION_SETUP A compound request can place SESSION_SETUP after
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix session reference leak on compounded SESSION_SETUP A compound request can place SESSION_SETUP after another command. That earlier command leaves a reference to its session in work->sess. smb2_sess_setup() then overwrites work->sess with the session it looks up or creates, and the dispatcher later puts work->sess only once. The inherited reference is never dropped. That leaks the session, together with its setup connection and socket, and every repeat of the compound leaks another. unreferenced object (size 512): __kmalloc_cache_noprof+0x32c/0x3a0 ksmbd_smb2_session_create+0xf6/0x9c0 [ksmbd] smb2_sess_setup+0xda4/0x6280 [ksmbd] handle_ksmbd_work+0x88c/0x1cb0 [ksmbd] Save the inherited session on entry. After the request has been processed, release it once, but only when smb2_sess_setup() has replaced work->sess with its own session or cleared it. Do this after ksmbd_conn_unlock() so the put does not run under srv_mutex. An error path may instead leave the inherited session in work->sess. Keep it there, so the dispatcher still puts it and the error response is still signed or encrypted with it as before.

items.title: CVE-2026-99524: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: sched_ext: Fix use-after-free of a local reenq node left on an inactive cpu A local DSQ reenq is queued on the
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: sched_ext: Fix use-after-free of a local reenq node left on an inactive cpu A local DSQ reenq is queued on the rq through a per-sched node and run from deferred work. When the scheduler is freed, scx_sched_free_rcu_work() warns and frees the pcpu with the node still linked, and the list is walked again once the cpu comes back. An inactive cpu's local DSQ holds only tasks that are bound to it or are being moved off, so the reenq is pointless. Ignore reenqs of an inactive cpu's

items.title: CVE-2026-99525: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: fix use-after-free in cifs_ses_add_channel() The error path of cifs_ses_add_channel() calls cifs_
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: fix use-after-free in cifs_ses_add_channel() The error path of cifs_ses_add_channel() calls cifs_put_tcp_session() before cifs_chan_clear_need_reconnect(). The latter reaches cifs_ses_get_chan_index(), which dereferences server->terminate; if the put was the final reference, TCP_Server_Info is already freed and this is a use-after-free. Same put-then-use pattern as the recently fixed sibling in commit 717e0a25036b ("cifs: Fix server use-after-free in cifs_chan_skip_or_disable()"). Move the put last, but do not read chan->server after dropping chan_lock: chan points into ses->chans[], and once chan_count is decremented a concurrent add_channel can reuse the slot and overwrite the pointer, so the put would act on the new channel's server. Cache the pointer under chan_lock, clear the reconnect bit and decrement chan_count while still holding the reference, and release it after the unlock. This issue was discovered by Tencent CodeBuddy Security.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: spmi: Fix potential use-after-free by grabbing of_node reference As noticed by Sashiko during a review run of an unrelated patch, in of_spmi_register_devices(), for_each_available_child_of_node() is used to loop through children, and to also assign a node to a newly created SPMI child device. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: cgroup: serialize migrations of newly forked processes With favordynmods enabled, a cgroup.procs migration takes the target threadgroup's cgroup_threadgroup_rwsem for writing. A process fork holds the forking threadgroup's semaphore for reading. These are different semaphores when fork creates a new process. copy_process() publishes the child's PID before cgroup_post_fork() links the child to its css_set. A writer can find the child in that interval, take its uncontended semaphore, and migrate it while child->cgroups still points to init_css_set and child->cg_list is empty. Migration links the node into init_css_set.mg_tasks. cgroup_post_fork() then adds the same node to the intended css_set as though it were unlinked, corrupting both task lists and their css_set ownership. This regresses the fork/migration race fixed by commit b12b533fa523 ("cgroups: add lock for child->cgroups in cgroup_post_fork()") and restored again in 2012 after the lock had been removed. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: verify transform SessionId matches the decrypted header When an encrypted request comes in, the decryption key is picked by the SessionId in the transform header, but the request is then authorized under whatever session the decrypted inner header names. Nothing ever compares the two, so on a connection with more than one session a client can get a request decrypted with one session's key and run it as another session. Encrypted requests are exempt from signing too, so a valid AEAD tag is the only proof of session identity, and it is checked against the wrong session. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: platform/x86: asus-wmi: fix use-after-free unregistering kbd_led led kbd_led_update_all() registers asus->kbd_led with devm_led_classdev_register() on the platform device, but kbd_led is embedded in struct asus_wmi, which asus_wmi_remove() frees at its end. The driver core calls .remove() before devres_release_all(), so the deferred devres release runs led_classdev_unregister() on memory that has already been freed. Whether that faults depends on whether the slab has been reused in between, which makes the crash on module unload intermittent and silently corrupts the led classdev state in the remaining runs. Unregister the led classdev explicitly in asus_wmi_led_exit(), after the led workqueue has been destroyed: kbd_led_work can then neither run nor be queued anymore, since asus_ref.asus is NULL too, so kbd_led_registered is stable and the classdev can be released while the memory embedding it is still alive. devm_led_classdev_unregister() also drops the devres entry, leaving nothing to run at unbind cleanup time; it warns when no devres entry exists, hence the kbd_led_registered check.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: rapidio: mport_cdev: fix use-after-free in mport_mm_close() A use-after-free vulnerability was identified in mport_mm_close() in drivers/rapidio/devices/rio_mport_cdev.c, identical to the pattern previously addressed in dma_req_free(). This is observable from userspace when an application creates an mmap mapping via the RapidIO character device and subsequently unmaps it (or terminates, triggering exit_mmap()). During munmap, mport_mm_close() is invoked and drops the mapping reference via kref_put(). items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: media: ipu-bridge: Fix use-after-free in IVSC error path ipu_bridge_get_ivsc_acpi_dev() returns an ACPI device with a reference held. If no matching CSI device is found, ipu_bridge_check_ivsc_dev() drops that reference before passing the device to dev_err(). Concurrent CSI device and ACPI namespace removal can drop the other references, making this the final put. dev_err() then reads the freed struct acpi_device and its kobject name. This was reproduced without kprobes by racing normal CSI platform-device unregistration and ACPI configfs table removal against the production ipu_bridge_init() entry. KASAN reported the final free through device_release(), followed by invalid reads through _dev_err(). Emit the error message while the lookup reference is still held, then drop the reference as before. items.title: CVE-2026-99509: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: media: imon: fix use-after-free in display_close via dev_dbg ictx->dev is a raw pointer to the usb_interface's
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: media: imon: fix use-after-free in display_close via dev_dbg ictx->dev is a raw pointer to the usb_interface's embedded device. On disconnect, usb_disconnect() can drop the last reference on the interface and free it while a userspace fd for /dev/lcd0 is still open. When that fd is later closed, display_close() dereferences the now-freed ictx->dev via dev_dbg(), causing a use-after-free. Remove the dev_dbg() calls that dereference ictx->dev in display_close() and free_imon_context(), rather than taking a reference on the device.

items.title: CVE-2026-99510: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: media: hackrf: fix use-after-free in hackrf_alloc_urbs() error path hackrf_alloc_urbs() frees the URBs it allo
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: media: hackrf: fix use-after-free in hackrf_alloc_urbs() error path hackrf_alloc_urbs() frees the URBs it allocated so far when one allocation fails, but leaves the entries in dev->urb_list[] and dev->urbs_initialized untouched. The caller, hackrf_start_streaming(), then calls hackrf_free_urbs() on the error path, which walks dev->urbs_initialized entries and calls usb_free_urb() a second time on the already-freed URBs, causing a use-after-free (slab-use-after-free Write in usb_free_urb()). Drop the redundant cleanup loop inside hackrf_alloc_urbs() and let hackrf_free_urbs(), which the caller already invokes on error, own the cleanup of the successfully allocated URBs.

items.title: CVE-2026-99511: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: media: cx23885: Fix use-after-free in cx23885_finidev due to race condition In cx23885_v4l2_dev_notify_init, &

items.title: CVE-2026-99512: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: media: au0828: fix use-after-free in bulk_timeout timer on disconnect start_urb_transfer() arms dev->bulk_time
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: media: au0828: fix use-after-free in bulk_timeout timer on disconnect start_urb_transfer() arms dev->bulk_timeout, whose callback au0828_bulk_timeout() queues dev->restart_streaming; that work in turn calls start_urb_transfer() and re-arms the timer. au0828_dvb_unregister() cancels restart_streaming on disconnect but does not sync bulk_timeout. au0828_usb_release() then frees dev with kfree(), so a timer still armed or pending at that point can fire after the free and dereference dev through timer_container_of(). Sync the timer with timer_shutdown_sync() before cancel_work_sync(). The timer callback queues the work, so the timer must be stopped first; the shutdown variant is needed because the work re-arms the timer through start_urb_transfer(). The dvb->frontend == NULL early return guards the register-failure path where the timer was never set up. This bug was found by static analysis.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: lockd: Fix use-after-free in nlmsvc_retry_blocked nlmsvc_retry_blocked() examines the block at the head of nlm_blocked under nlm_blocked_lock, then releases the lock before calling nlmsvc_grant_blocked() or retry_deferred_block(). The nlm_blocked list reference is all that keeps the block alive across that window. nlmsvc_grant_blocked() does take one of its own, but not until after the lock has been dropped. Unmounting the nfsd filesystem while a lock request is still blocked reaches nlmsvc_traverse_blocks(), which drops the list reference and frees the block along with the nlm_rqst hanging off it. BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in nlm_async_call+0xd6/0x230 Read of size 8 at addr ffff88811b04c808 by task lockd/8377 nlm_async_call+0xd6/0x230 nlmsvc_retry_blocked+0x61c/0x800 lockd+0x144/0x1c0 Freed by task 8392: nlmsvc_release_block+0x231/0x290 nlmsvc_traverse_blocks+0x139/0x1b0 nlm_traverse_files+0x1aa/0xa00 nlmsvc_free_host_resources+0x12/0x60 nlm_shutdown_hosts_net+0x127/0x280 lockd_down+0xd5/0x1c0 Take a reference before releasing nlm_blocked_lock and drop it once the retry has run.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: landlock: Fix superblock use-after-free in release_inode() Without this fix, release_inode() (task 1) can race with a umount operation in hook_sb_delete() (task 2). The caller is the unmount operation and proceeds to release the superblock. * task 1: Runs wake_up_var(&landlock_superblock(sb)->inode_refs), *dereferencing the sb_security on the freed-up superblock*. Notably, wake_up_var() does not dereference the pointer passed to it, and only uses it to determine an overapproximated set of tasks to wake up. So while it's potentially possible for an attacker to provide a different value for that pointer, this only results in the wrong set of tasks getting woken up, and in this scenario, no further tasks are actually waiting. items.title: CVE-2026-99515: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: iommufd: Fix event queue release use-after-free iommufd_eventq_fops_release() drops the file's users reference
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: iommufd: Fix event queue release use-after-free iommufd_eventq_fops_release() drops the file's users reference before reading eventq->ictx. Once that reference is dropped, IOMMU_DESTROY in another thread can remove and free the event queue, so the later load accesses freed memory. Read ictx while the users reference still pins the event queue, then drop the reference and put the saved context. The context reference taken by iommufd_eventq_init() keeps ictx valid until the put. Fault and vEVENTQ file descriptors share this release path.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: s390/pci: Fix resource leak in zpci MSI setup If airq_iv_create() fails in __alloc_airq(), the zpci_sbv bit allocated by airq_iv_alloc_bit() is never freed. This permanently leaks one of the ZPCI_NR_DEVICES summary bits, reducing system capacity with each failed device hotplug. In systems with repeated device insertion failures or under memory pressure, all summary bits can be exhausted, preventing new PCI devices from being added until reboot. Add proper error handling to free the zpci_sbv bit and reset zdev->aisb if the AIBV creation fails.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: s390/pci: Fix MSI directed-mode teardown IRQ bit count On s390 with directed interrupts enabled, zpci_msi_teardown_directed() frees the platform's maximum number of MSI bits (zdev->max_msi) instead of the actual allocated count (zdev->msi_nr_irqs). This corrupts the shared IRQ bitmap used by all PCI functions, causing lost interrupts and heap corruption. Fix zpci_msi_teardown_directed() to only free the actual allocated IRQ bit count.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: s390/pci: Fix double-free and NULL deref in zpci MSI domain cleanup zpci_remove_parent_msi_domain() dereferences zbus->msi_parent_domain unconditionally and does not clear it afterwards. zpci_bus_create_pci_bus() removes the domain when pci_create_root_bus() fails, then zpci_bus_release() removes it again on the last kref_put(), reading ->fwnode from the freed irq_domain and freeing it twice. If zpci_alloc_domain() or zpci_create_parent_msi_domain() fails, no domain is created at all; zbus is kzalloc'd, so the same release path dereferences NULL. Return early when there is no domain, and clear the pointer after removing one.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: apparmor: fix a use-after-free in aa_lookupn_ns() aa_lookupn_ns() takes a reference on the namespace it finds with aa_get_ns(), which is kref_get() on the reference count that the namespace is released through, without checking whether the namespace is still in use. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/hugetlb: fix use-after-free of a new anon folio For a fault in a private mapping with nothing in the page cache, hugetlb_no_page() allocates a folio, locks it and maps it.
