items.title: CVE-2026-99414: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: skip copy up of empty security.capability ovl_copy_xattr() gives up if it can't read an attribute that li
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: skip copy up of empty security.capability ovl_copy_xattr() gives up if it can't read an attribute that listxattr() has named. An empty security.capability, which anybody has been able to store on any file for a long time, is such a case: it is listed, and getxattr() has nothing to return for it. A file in a lower layer that carries one can't be copied up: it can't be written to, renamed or have its mode changed. There is nothing to copy if there are no data. Go on with the next one. [amir: treat -EINVAL as no capability too, and do the same in ovl_copy_up_meta_inode_data()]

items.title: CVE-2026-99415: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: set the revalidate flags after d_instantiate() stat() of a file on an overlayfs mount triggers a kernel w
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: set the revalidate flags after d_instantiate() stat() of a file on an overlayfs mount triggers a kernel warning and fails with ECHILD if another task is creating that file at the same time. This happens on an overlay with a FUSE upper layer, which is the layer where overlayfs creates new files. Write access to a directory on such an overlay is all a user needs to run the two tasks. The revalidate flags are DCACHE_OP_REVALIDATE and DCACHE_OP_WEAK_REVALIDATE. They tell path walk to call ->d_revalidate() or ->d_weak_revalidate() on a dentry, so that the filesystem can check that the cached dentry is still valid. An overlay dentry only has one of these flags if a dentry in one of its layers has it. FUSE dentries have the first one. When a flag is set on an overlay dentry, path walk calls ovl_dentry_revalidate_common(). That function only expects a dentry without an inode in RCU walk, while the dentry is being destroyed. For such a dentry outside of RCU walk, it hits a WARN_ON() and returns -ECHILD. So a negative overlay dentry must never have the flags set. ovl_instantiate() breaks this rule. When a task creates a

items.title: CVE-2026-99416: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: read the nlink xattr of every indexed non-dir With nfs_export=on, data written through a file handle to a
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: read the nlink xattr of every indexed non-dir With nfs_export=on, data written through a file handle to a lower file, i.e. a file that exists only in a lower layer of the overlay, can be lost on the next mount. A lookup of the file by name then returns -EIO. Also, a file with one name reports st_nlink 2 once it has been copied to the upper layer. After such a file is removed, its file handle can still open it until the next mount. Before a lower file is changed for the first time, overlayfs copies it to the writable upper layer. This is called copy up. The index directory is $workdir/index, where $workdir is the directory given by the workdir= option. Each entry is named after the file handle of a lower inode, so that overlayfs can get from the handle to the copied up inode. With nfs_export=on, copy up indexes every non-directory: it copies the file to an entry in the index directory and then hard links that entry into the upper directory. The index entry is an extra link to the upper inode, so overlayfs stores the link count that users should see in the overlay.nlink xattr. A file can also be opened by handle

items.title: CVE-2026-99417: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: fix a torn path in ovl_get_redirect() A hard link of a metacopy file that races with a rename of an ances
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: fix a torn path in ovl_get_redirect() A hard link of a metacopy file that races with a rename of an ancestor stores a redirect to the wrong lower file. Each component of an absolute redirect must be the name that a dentry has in the parent that the walk continues with. ovl_get_redirect() copies the name under d_lock and calls dget_parent() after the unlock, and the callers for a hard link hold no lock that stops a rename across directories. A rename between the two steps combines the old name with the new parent. With delays in ovl_get_redirect(), an unprivileged user hard-linked a metacopy file while renaming its ancestor to another directory, the stored redirect named another lower path, and after a remount the file showed the data of a root-only file. Fix this by taking the parent first and checking it again under d_lock.

items.title: CVE-2026-99418: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: do not copy up an xattr value that was never read Copy-up stores uninitialized kernel memory in an xattr
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: do not copy up an xattr value that was never read Copy-up stores uninitialized kernel memory in an xattr of the upper file, where the user can read it. ovl_copy_xattr() may only pass bytes to ovl_do_setxattr() that ovl_do_getxattr() has read. When the read fails with -ERANGE the function asks for the size again, and if the new size fits the buffer it stores the buffer although nothing was read into it. The buffer comes from kvmalloc(), or it still holds the value of the previous xattr. A FUSE lower layer that answers every sized GETXATTR with -ERANGE made copy-up store 4096 bytes that the server never sent, with a kernel pointer in them, as an xattr of the upper file. Fix this by failing the copy-up with -EIO when the size that follows -ERANGE fits the buffer.

items.title: CVE-2026-99419: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: do not copy up a dentry that was removed A change to a removed file through an open descriptor replaces w
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: do not copy up a dentry that was removed A change to a removed file through an open descriptor replaces whatever has its old name in the upper layer. Copy up must only create a name in the upper directory, never replace one. After an unlink, an rmdir or a rename over a lower dentry, a dentry that an open file keeps alive still has its old parent and name, but in the upper directory that name is now a whiteout or a new object. ovl_copy_up_workdir() renames the copy over it, which brings back the removed object and destroys whatever took its name. An unprivileged user opened a lower FIFO and unlinked it, root created a file at that name, and fchmod on the old descriptor replaced the file of root with the FIFO. Fix this by looking up the target name of the rename in ovl_copy_up_workdir() with LOOKUP_EXCL, so that copy up fails with -EEXIST if the name is taken, as copy up with O_TMPFILE already does when it links the copy to the name. [amir: use LOOKUP_EXCL instead of relying on d_unhashed()]

items.title: CVE-2026-99420: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: check that the parents of volatile/dirty are dirs An unprivileged user crashes the kernel by mounting ove
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: check that the parents of volatile/dirty are dirs An unprivileged user crashes the kernel by mounting overlayfs with the volatile option. A dentry that serves as the parent of a lookup must be a directory. ovl_create_volatile_dirty() walks work/incompat/volatile/dirty by name, and ovl_lookup_or_create() returns an existing entry whatever its type. A file or a symlink that another task creates during the mount becomes the parent of the next lookup, which calls a NULL ->lookup. An unprivileged user mounted overlayfs with "volatile" in a user namespace while a second process created a symlink named work/incompat, and the mount task oopsed on a NULL ->lookup call. Fix this by returning -ENOTDIR from ovl_lookup_or_create() when the caller asked for a directory and the existing entry is a non-dir.

items.title: CVE-2026-99421: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: always encode the origin fh when index is enabled On an overlay with index=on,nfs_export=on, copy up of a
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ovl: always encode the origin fh when index is enabled On an overlay with index=on,nfs_export=on, copy up of a directory crashes the kernel once an LSM has started to deny CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH to the mounter, the task that mounted the overlay. The mount and the LSM policy change require root. After that, any user who can write to a directory that exists only in a lower layer triggers the oops by doing so. Before a file or directory that exists only in a lower layer is changed for the first time, overlayfs copies it to the writable upper layer. This is called copy up. On copy up, ovl_get_origin_fh() encodes the file handle of the lower inode, called the origin. It returns NULL if ovl_can_decode_fh() says that the lower filesystem cannot decode handles. Whether the callers can handle NULL depends on the index option: - Without an index, NULL is fine: the callers store an empty origin xattr. - With index enabled, overlayfs keeps entries for copied up inodes in an internal index directory. The name of an index entry is derived from the handle, so ovl_get_origin_fh() must return a handle or an error. The mount only enabl

items.title: CVE-2026-99405: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: abort dirtree repair if the live update hook dies LOLLM notices that if the live update hook for the dire
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: abort dirtree repair if the live update hook dies LOLLM notices that if the live update hook for the directory tree repair code hits an error, it will set dl->aborted and stops working. If the repair code ever sees that condition, it ought to bail out immediately instead of continuing with obsolete data.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: fix lost errno returned from xfarray_foliosort LOLLM noticed that we stop the sort early but don't actually pass along the error code, which could enable repair code to continue running with an unsorted array. Fix that.

items.title: CVE-2026-99407: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: don't repair fs summary counters with garbage LOLLM noticed that if we scan the filesystem and come up wi
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: don't repair fs summary counters with garbage LOLLM noticed that if we scan the filesystem and come up with totally garbage numbers for the summary counters, we don't actually mark the scan incomplete. Because we don't do this, repair can install the garbage values into the filesystem, making things worse. Don't do that.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: don't proceed with xattr repair if the live update fails LOLLM observes that we ought to make one last check for failed live updates before replacing the xattr structure. Let's be cautious here.

items.title: CVE-2026-99409: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: don't fix the directory tree if live update fails LOLLM complains that we don't double-check dl->aborted
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: don't fix the directory tree if live update fails LOLLM complains that we don't double-check dl->aborted one last time to before committing repairs to the filesystem. This is important because the live update handler could have set ->aborted if it encountered a runtime error.

items.title: CVE-2026-99410: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: always reset incore attr fork buffer when resetting fork LOLLM noticed that the local format attr fork ve
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: always reset incore attr fork buffer when resetting fork LOLLM noticed that the local format attr fork verifier depends on if_bytes being set correctly. However, the fork reset function doesn't reset that correctly, which can cause post-repair verifier failures. Fix that.

items.title: CVE-2026-99411: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: actually lock the metafile reservation when adjusting after repair LOLLM reported that xrep_reset_metafil
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: actually lock the metafile reservation when adjusting after repair LOLLM reported that xrep_reset_metafile_resv performs unlocked loads and stores to the metadata file space reservation counters and thus can race with other threads. Fix this by taking the lock.

items.title: CVE-2026-99412: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: avoid cross-rtgroup reaping after a repair LOLLM notices that the extents stored in a xrtb_bitmap (aka xf
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: avoid cross-rtgroup reaping after a repair LOLLM notices that the extents stored in a xrtb_bitmap (aka xfs_rtblock bitmap) can span multiple rtgroups due to two circumstances. The first is that the size of an rtgroup is an exact power of two, which means that rtgroups are adjacent in the segmented xfs_rtblock_t address space. This is fairly common to reduce the amount of multiplication and division needed to handle space on the rt volume. The second is that (unlike in the original rtgroups design), rtgroups do not have fixed-location metadata like AGs do, which means that there's nothing to force a break between rtgroups. Therefore, we must loop through the rtgroups in xreap_rtmeta_extent to avoid running off the end of an rtgroup while reaping.

items.title: CVE-2026-99413: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: fix buffer overruns in xfs_ioc_attr_list When we converted the al_offset array in struct xfs_attrlist int
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: fix buffer overruns in xfs_ioc_attr_list When we converted the al_offset array in struct xfs_attrlist into a VLA, the size of the object shrank by 4 bytes. Unfortunately, the buffer size validation in the attrlist ioctl wasn't updated to notice this, so the al_offset[0] assignment blindly writes off the end of the buffer. LOLLM noticed the omitted check and complained.

items.title: CVE-2026-99396: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: bound da-node entry count against the correct geometry xfs_da3_node_verify() bounds the node entry count
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: bound da-node entry count against the correct geometry xfs_da3_node_verify() bounds the node entry count against the larger of the directory and attribute geometries because, as a buffer verifier, it cannot tell whether the block belongs to the directory or the attribute tree. When the directory block size exceeds the fs block size (e.g. mkfs.xfs -n size=64k -b size=4k), an attribute node buffer is a single fs block that holds only m_attr_geo->node_ents entries, yet a crafted attr node may claim a count up to m_dir_geo->node_ents and still pass the verifier. xfs_da3_node_lookup_int() then indexes btree[] up to that count during its binary search -- an out-of-bounds read via getxattr/listxattr on a mounted crafted image. The buffer verifier is the wrong place to tighten this: it has no fork context, and the transaction-less read path used by getxattr does not run xfs_da3_node_set_type() either. xfs_da3_node_lookup_int(), on the other hand, always runs on that path and holds args->geo, the geometry of the fork actually being searched. Bound the entry count against args->geo->node_ents there, before walking the e

items.title: CVE-2026-99397: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: always report inode repair setup failures LOLLM noticed that xchk_setup_inode silently discards errors be
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: always report inode repair setup failures LOLLM noticed that xchk_setup_inode silently discards errors being returned by xrep_setup_inode. Fix that, and fix the stub macro so that it actually "returns" a value.

items.title: CVE-2026-99398: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: always forget cached ACLs if the attr fork swap succeeds LOLLM complains that xrep_xattr_rebuild_tree omi
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: always forget cached ACLs if the attr fork swap succeeds LOLLM complains that xrep_xattr_rebuild_tree omits the xfs_forget_acl call if the attr fork swap succeeds (and hence the acls might have changed) but reaping the old attr fork fails. Fix it so that we always purge the cached acls if the swap succeeds, even if subsequent steps do not. This avoids some cache coherency problems with access controls.

items.title: CVE-2026-99399: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: reject remote xattr entries with an out-of-range value length xfs_attr3_leaf_verify_entry() validates a r
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: reject remote xattr entries with an out-of-range value length xfs_attr3_leaf_verify_entry() validates a remote attribute entry's name but never bounds its on-disk value length (xfs_attr_leaf_name_remote. valuelen, a __be32). A crafted leaf with valuelen = 0x80000000 passes the verifier and the CRC. That length is later assigned into the signed int args->rmtvaluelen (xfs_attr3_leaf_getvalue), becoming negative, which slips past the signed -ERANGE check in xfs_attr_copy_value(); a getxattr() with a small buffer then memcpy()s a full remote block into the small kvalue buffer (xfs_attr_rmtval_copyout) -- a heap out-of-bounds write with attacker-controlled content, from an unprivileged getxattr(2) on a mounted crafted image. Reject remote entries whose value length exceeds XFS_XATTR_SIZE_MAX in the leaf verifier, so the malicious block is rejected at read time.

items.title: CVE-2026-99400: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: reject out-of-range attribute value lengths in xfs_attr_copy_value xfs_attr_copy_value() takes the value
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: reject out-of-range attribute value lengths in xfs_attr_copy_value xfs_attr_copy_value() takes the value length as a signed int and, for a remote xattr, is handed args->rmtvaluelen. That field is filled from the on-disk __be32 xfs_attr_leaf_name_remote.valuelen in xfs_attr3_leaf_getvalue(), so a crafted length such as 0x80000000 is stored into the signed rmtvaluelen as a negative number. The "buffer too small" guard in xfs_attr_copy_value() is a signed comparison: if (args->valuelen < valuelen) return -ERANGE; A negative valuelen therefore compares as smaller than the caller's buffer size, skips the -ERANGE path, and is then used as a copy length, leading to an out-of-bounds copy of a full remote block into a small getxattr(2) buffer on a mounted crafted image. Reject a value length that is negative or larger than the maximum xattr size before it is used, so a bogus on-disk length can no longer slip through the value copier.

items.title: CVE-2026-99401: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: rtnetlink: wait for RCU readers in rtnl_link_unregister() rtnl_link_ops_get() finds ops on link_ops under rcu_
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: rtnetlink: wait for RCU readers in rtnl_link_unregister() rtnl_link_ops_get() finds ops on link_ops under rcu_read_lock() and only then takes ops->srcu. rtnl_link_unregister() unlinks ops, then calls synchronize_srcu() and cleanup_srcu_struct() without first waiting for RCU readers. A reader that found ops before list_del_rcu() and has not yet taken ops->srcu is not waited for. Such a reader then locks a cleaned-up srcu_struct and keeps using ops after the module that owns it is gone. rtnl_newlink() and rtnl_dump_ifinfo() both look up ops without RTNL, the latter for any user that dumps links filtered by kind. With delays added between the lookup and srcu_read_lock() in rtnl_link_ops_get(), and before rtnl_link_ops_put() in rtnl_dump_ifinfo(), running "ip link show type dummy" alongside "rmmod dummy" on a KASAN kernel gives: BUG: KASAN: vmalloc-out-of-bounds in __srcu_read_unlock+0x57/0x70 Read of size 8 at addr ffffffffc02ff318 by task ip/147 Call Trace: __srcu_read_unlock+0x57/0x70 rtnl_dump_ifinfo.cold+0x30/0x3b rtnl_dumpit+0x7a/0x1b0 netlink_dump+0x486/0x11b0 __netlink_dump_start+0x661/0x910 rtnetlink_rcv_msg+0

items.title: CVE-2026-99402: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: netfilter: nft_payload: restrict checksum offsets to known values We need to prevent userspace from corrupting
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: netfilter: nft_payload: restrict checksum offsets to known values We need to prevent userspace from corrupting e.g. tcp->doff, because many locations in conntrack and conntrack helpers rely on nf_conntrack_in() having validated the packet headers. nft_payload allows to alter headers later which invalidates this assumption. The 'Fixes' commit restricts writes to safe fields, but there is another side channel: the checksum location. Restrict this too. Reported via sashiko/gemini.

items.title: CVE-2026-99403: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: mark overfull dabtree node blocks as corrupt LOLLM observes that we need to range-check the dabtree node
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: mark overfull dabtree node blocks as corrupt LOLLM observes that we need to range-check the dabtree node record count before using it to index an array. Fix that.

items.title: CVE-2026-99404: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: check fork type against dabtree block magic number LOLLM complains that we fail to flag dabtree blocks th
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: check fork type against dabtree block magic number LOLLM complains that we fail to flag dabtree blocks that should never be associated with the file fork -- data forks can't point to xattr leaves, and attr forks can't point to dirent blocks. Add the missing checks.

items.title: CVE-2026-99388: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: smbdirect: fix buffer length underflow in RDMA transfers When a remote buffer descriptor is larger than t
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: smbdirect: fix buffer length underflow in RDMA transfers When a remote buffer descriptor is larger than the remaining local buffer, smbdirect_connection_rdma_xmit() clamps its length and sets buf_len to zero. The common accounting code then subtracts the clamped length from buf_len, causing it to underflow. If another descriptor follows, the loop processes it with a wrapped remaining length and includes memory beyond the local buffer in the RDMA transfer. A client can trigger an out-of-bounds kernel write with an SMB WRITE request, or an out-of-bounds kernel read with an SMB READ request, by supplying multiple RDMA buffer descriptors with an oversized descriptor before the last one. Remove the premature assignment to buf_len. Subtracting the clamped length already consumes the remaining buffer, so the next iteration stops and only descriptors within the local buffer are used to build work requests.

items.title: CVE-2026-99389: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: server: size directory name conversion buffer correctly A 2048-byte ASCII directory name needs 4098 bytes
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: server: size directory name conversion buffer correctly A 2048-byte ASCII directory name needs 4098 bytes when converted to UTF-16, including the terminator. ksmbd_convert_dir_info_name() caps its allocation at PATH_MAX and writes past the end of that buffer. Allocate space for one UTF-16 code unit per input byte plus the terminator. Use kmalloc_array() to check the size calculation.

items.title: CVE-2026-99390: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: fix correction of unwritten extents in quota file data fork LOLLM noticed a couple of problems with the c
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: fix correction of unwritten extents in quota file data fork LOLLM noticed a couple of problems with the code that fixes unwritten mappings in the quota file's data fork: first, we should zero the ondisk contents as part of converting them to "unwritten" just in case we crash shortly after the conversion. Second, and more importantly, it noticed that we fail to resynchronize the iext tree cursor after modifying the iext tree. If the tree shape changes, we could be in a world of hurt. Third, we should force a quotacheck if we reset an ondisk dquot. Fix all issues.

items.title: CVE-2026-99391: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: don't try to scrub self-referential dirent in metapath checker LOLLM observes that the _ilock_both helper
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: don't try to scrub self-referential dirent in metapath checker LOLLM observes that the _ilock_both helper will loop forever trying to double-lock the same inode if mpath->dp == sc->ip. Callers are not supposed to call us with parent == child because that makes no sense. Trigger an assertion, mark the scan incomplete, and return IO error so that this fails noisily.

items.title: CVE-2026-99392: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: don't subtract excess usage twice when computing agf_btreeblks LOLLM noticed that the free space btree re
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: don't subtract excess usage twice when computing agf_btreeblks LOLLM noticed that the free space btree repair code calculates agf_btreeblks from the number of blocks we wrote to rebuild the free space btrees (minus the roots). That's correct. However, it observes that we subtract the "excess" reservation, which is not correct. Fix this accounting problem.

items.title: CVE-2026-99393: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: don't overrun incore inode when cleaning attr forks LOLLM noticed that xrep_dinode_check_afork doesn't ch
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: don't overrun incore inode when cleaning attr forks LOLLM noticed that xrep_dinode_check_afork doesn't check for a di_forkoff value that is so large that the attr fork would begin after the end of the inode space. This causes afork_{ptr,size} to be nonsense. What we really ought to do here is zap the attr fork.

items.title: CVE-2026-99394: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: complain loudly when dirtree checker finds broken links LOLLM observed that the directory tree walk code
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: complain loudly when dirtree checker finds broken links LOLLM observed that the directory tree walk code bails out if it finds broken parent pointers along the way. However, it flattens the return code to zero, which means that we can end up in the repair code having not completed the scan. We should never proceed with a repair in this state, so let's mark the scrub incomplete and exit.

items.title: CVE-2026-99395: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: bound inode fork length against the fork size during log recovery xlog_recover_inode_commit_pass2() copie
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: bound inode fork length against the fork size during log recovery xlog_recover_inode_commit_pass2() copies an inode log item's data/attr fork region into the inode buffer using the on-log region length without bounding it against the fork capacity, e.g.: len = item->ri_buf[2].iov_len; memcpy(XFS_DFORK_DPTR(dip), src, len); The only guard is an ASSERT, which is a no-op on production kernels (CONFIG_XFS_DEBUG off), and xfs_dinode_verify() runs only after the copy. A crafted image with a dirty log can therefore drive a heap out-of-bounds write at mount time. The XFS_ILOG_DBROOT sibling already passes XFS_DFORK_DSIZE as a bound; the DDATA/DEXT and ADATA/AEXT memcpy paths did not. Bound each logged fork region against the destination fork size before copying it, and reject the log item with -EFSCORRUPTED when it does not fit. Because the recovered inode is only verified after the fork data has been copied in, the checks are done up front, before any memcpy into the on-disk inode.

items.title: CVE-2026-99380: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: validate NT transaction response layout and offsets validate_ntransact() assumes that the respons
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: validate NT transaction response layout and offsets validate_ntransact() assumes that the response uses the fixed 18-word NT transaction layout. A different WordCount makes get_bcc() locate the byte count at a different offset from pSMBr->ByteCount, allowing the subsequent bounds checks to use inconsistent response boundaries. The function also turns the 32-bit ParameterOffset and DataOffset fields into pointers before checking their bounds. On a 32-bit client, a large offset can wrap the pointer below end_of_smb and pass the one-sided pointer comparison. The caller then dereferences the parameter pointer or copies from the data pointer. Require the expected WordCount before reading the byte count. Check each offset and count against the received SMB length as integers before forming either pointer. Use subtraction after validating the offset so that the range checks cannot overflow.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: reject short or out-of-range FIND response parameters CIFSFindFirst() and CIFSFindNext() read the SearchHandle, SearchCount, EndofSearch and LastNameOffset of a TRANS2_FIND_FIRST2 or TRANS2_FIND_NEXT2 response at ParameterOffset. validate_t2() bounds the offset at 1024 and ParameterCount below 512, and nothing compares them with the number of bytes SendReceive() copied into the buffer or with the size of the response parameters. smb_init() places the request and the response in the same cifs_request allocation and cifs_buf_get() clears only the start of it, so a short response with a ParameterOffset past its end has the search handle, the entry count, the end-of-search flag and the last-entry offset read out of the request that was just sent, or out of whatever the allocation held before, and a ParameterCount smaller than the parameters has them read past the end of the parameter block. The reads stay inside the allocation, but what they return is not part of the response, and CIFSFindFirst() then hands back a search handle the server never sent. items.title: CVE-2026-99382: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: reject FIND data areas that run past the received response CIFSFindFirst() and CIFSFindNext() tak
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: reject FIND data areas that run past the received response CIFSFindFirst() and CIFSFindNext() take the directory entries of a TRANS2_FIND_FIRST2 or TRANS2_FIND_NEXT2 response from DataOffset for DataCount bytes. validate_t2() bounds DataOffset at 1024 and ParameterCount + DataCount by the byte count, and nothing compares DataOffset + DataCount with the number of bytes SendReceive() copied into the buffer. smb_init() places the request and the response in the same cifs_request allocation and cifs_buf_get() clears only the start of it, so a short response whose data area extends past its end has srch_entries_start point at bytes of the request that was just sent, or at whatever the allocation held before, and those bytes are parsed as directory entries. cifs_readdir() and find_cifs_entry() walk the entries with nxt_dir_entry(), which checks every entry but the first of a response against the end of the SMB; cifs_query_path_info() and cifs_backup_query_path_info() read the first entry with no check at all. Those reads stay inside the allocation, but what they return is not part of the response. The last e

items.title: CVE-2026-99383: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: reclaim credits for decrypted reads with no matching mid When a decrypted SMB2 READ response carr
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: reclaim credits for decrypted reads with no matching mid When a decrypted SMB2 READ response carries a MessageId that matches no outstanding request, both the inline receive_encrypted_read() and the offloaded smb2_decrypt_offload() paths drop the frame without accounting the credits the server granted in it. The plaintext unknown-frame path in cifs_demultiplex_thread() already reclaims them with smb2_add_credits_from_hdr(), so encrypted reads leak credits that the plaintext path would not. This also happens for legitimate frames - e.g. a reply that arrives after the client has timed out and dropped the mid - so over a long-lived connection the client's credit count drifts down and can eventually starve it of the ability to issue requests. The frame is AEAD-authenticated, so the granted credits in the decrypted header come from the real server and are safe to apply. Reclaim the credits from the decrypted header before dropping the frame, and export smb2_add_credits_from_hdr() so the SMB2 receive paths can use it.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: fix OOB read of the resume name sent in TRANS2_FIND_NEXT2 cifs_fill_dirent() reads the fixed part of a directory entry and the name length it holds, or for SMB_FIND_FILE_UNIX scans the name for its terminating NUL, without knowing where the response ends. cifs_save_resume_key() calls it for the entry at the LastNameOffset the server chose, after every FindNext and after the FindFirst of a search rewind, and records the name it returns as the resume name of the search without bounding it; the next CIFSFindNext() copies up to PATH_MAX - 1 bytes from that name into its request and sends them to the server. cifs_filldir() bounds the name against the end of the response since commit f8cf09a53a0d ("smb: client: bound dirent name against end of SMB response in cifs_filldir"), but only after cifs_fill_dirent() has read the entry, and nxt_dir_entry() checks the entries it walks only against sizeof(FILE_DIRECTORY_INFO), for every level but SMB_FIND_FILE_INFO_STANDARD, and never sees the first entry of a response. items.title: CVE-2026-99385: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: fix buffer overflow in SMB2_tcon() In SMB2_tcon(), unc_path is allocated with a fixed buffer size
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: fix buffer overflow in SMB2_tcon() In SMB2_tcon(), unc_path is allocated with a fixed buffer size of MAX_SHARENAME_LENGTH * 2 bytes (672 bytes). However, the user-controlled UNC path (tree) length is passed to cifs_strtoUTF16(), which assumes the destination buffer is large enough and writes strlen(tree) + 1 UTF-16 code units. Commit 62a1a439e0fd ("cifs: clean up handling of unc= option") removed the length check on UNC mount options, allowing mount paths to exceed MAX_SHARENAME_LENGTH while retaining the fixed-size buffer allocation in SMB2_tcon(). Consequently, an oversized UNC string causes cifs_strtoUTF16() to write past the end of the heap object, resulting in a slab-out-of-bounds write. Furthermore, if a tree exceeds MAX_TREE_SIZE characters, strscpy() truncates it in cifs_tcon::tree_name, causing subsequent reconnects or failovers to fail. Fix this by first verifying that the length of tree does not exceed MAX_TREE_SIZE, returning -EINVAL if it does. Then, dynamically allocate unc_path based on the length of tree so that it safely accommodates all UTF-16 code units for paths within MAX_TREE_SIZE

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: don't resurrect an exiting tcon from cached dir workers cfids_laundromat_worker() bumps tcon->tc_count for every expired open cfid and queues cached_dir_offload_close() without checking whether the tcon is already being torn down. items.title: CVE-2026-99387: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: bound POSIX lock data area by response length CIFSSMBPosixLock() receives a TRANS2 response whose
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: bound POSIX lock data area by response length CIFSSMBPosixLock() receives a TRANS2 response whose server-provided DataOffset and DataCount are not required by validate_t2() to describe an interval inside the response. A server can therefore make the client read a cifs_posix_lock beyond the response buffer and return those kernel bytes through F_GETLK. Use smbCalcSize() to obtain the full response length after any multipart TRANS2 reassembly, then reject data areas that extend past it before dereferencing them.

items.title: CVE-2026-99372: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: cap the number of listeners accepted in listener_set nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() matches each requested
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: cap the number of listeners accepted in listener_set nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() matches each requested listener against the existing set. The nested loop that does this is O(N * M), where N is the requested count and M is the existing count. The loop runs under sv_lock with bottom halves disabled. A userland request with a very large listener list can therefore spin in atomic context for a long time. Reject a request that carries more than NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX (1024) entries. The check goes in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(), before the code takes any lock. The limit is far above any realistic configuration. This patch does not cap M. Only the message size bounded N; real sockets bound M. A listener_set result set is the requested set, so that path also holds M at the cap, but __write_ports_addxprt() adds two listeners per call and removes none, so repeated calls can push M past it. The worst case under sv_lock is therefore 1024 * M, plus 1024 nla_parse_nested() calls. Both interfaces require CAP_NET_ADMIN.

items.title: CVE-2026-99373: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFS/localio: detect a short read or write before the iterator has moved nfs_local_call_read() and nfs_local_ca
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFS/localio: detect a short read or write before the iterator has moved nfs_local_call_read() and nfs_local_call_write() issue a misaligned DIO as up to three segments and must stop at the first short one, or the next segment lands at the wrong file offset. They test for that by comparing the bytes transferred against iov_iter_count() of the segment, read after read_iter() or write_iter() has advanced the iterator, when the count is the residual rather than the request: before the call: count == expected after the call: count == expected - status The test is therefore status < expected - status, and it fires only when less than half of the segment was transferred. A short I/O that covers between 50% and 99% of a segment slips through: the loop moves on with ki_pos advanced by the short amount, the next segment is issued at the wrong offset, and the header's byte count is over-reported to the caller. A write that slips through also never sets NFS_CONTEXT_WRITE_SYNC, which is what makes the writes that follow a short one synchronous. Take the segment's count before issuing it and compare against that. This is the sam

items.title: CVE-2026-99374: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSv4/flexfiles: Use the full 64-bit stripe_unit ff_layout_alloc_lseg() decodes stripe_unit as the 64-bit valu
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSv4/flexfiles: Use the full 64-bit stripe_unit ff_layout_alloc_lseg() decodes stripe_unit as the 64-bit value the protocol defines and struct nfs4_ff_layout_segment stores it as one, but both consumers narrow it back to 32 bits: nfs4_ff_layout_calc_dss_id() divides with do_div(), which casts the divisor, and ff_layout_pg_test() copies it into a u32 first. A stripe_unit that does not fit is silently truncated, so the client stripes on a unit the server did not specify -- or divides by zero, if the low 32 bits happen to be clear. Divide by the full value, with div64_u64() and div64_u64_rem().

items.title: CVE-2026-99375: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSv4/flexfiles: fail I/O to the data server once a lock is lost When a client loses a byte-range lock, becaus
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSv4/flexfiles: fail I/O to the data server once a lock is lost When a client loses a byte-range lock, because its lease expired and it may not recover the lock (nfs.recover_lost_locks=0) or because reclaim failed, it marks the lock state NFS_LOCK_LOST and fails further I/O by that lock owner. Otherwise an application that believes it holds a lock over a range is never told that the lock is gone, and can overwrite data that another client has since written under its own lock on that range. The NFSv4 READ/WRITE and file layout I/O paths apply this in rpc_call_prepare, where nfs4_set_rw_stateid() returns -EIO for a lost lock. The flexfiles data server I/O path does not: the NFSv3 data server path never checked, and the check on the NFSv4 path was removed when the data server stateid began to be taken from the layout. Fail read and write RPCs to the data server in rpc_call_prepare when the lock is lost. items.title: CVE-2026-99376: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSv4/pnfs: Free the netid when draining a data-server address list nfs4_pnfs_ds_addr_free() releases all thre
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSv4/pnfs: Free the netid when draining a data-server address list nfs4_pnfs_ds_addr_free() releases all three of an address entry's allocations, but the four sites that drain a decoded list before it reaches a data server open-code the loop and free only da_remotestr and the entry, leaking da_netid. Both layout drivers drain that list when nfs4_pnfs_ds_add() returned a data server already in the cache, and again on their error exits. Lift the drain into nfs4_pnfs_ds_addr_list_free() so an address list has one owner. A striping mount reaches the cached case on nearly every GETDEVICEINFO, since many deviceIDs name the same data servers.

items.title: CVE-2026-99377: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSv4/pnfs: bound the CB_NOTIFY_DEVICEID array count before allocating decode_devicenotify_args() hands the se
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSv4/pnfs: bound the CB_NOTIFY_DEVICEID array count before allocating decode_devicenotify_args() hands the server's notification count straight to kmalloc_objs() as the array length, without checking it against the message that carried it. Bound it the way nfs4xdr.c bounds an attribute length, against xdr_stream_remaining().

items.title: CVE-2026-99378: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: pnfs/blocklayout: Complete a device upcall when the pipe is closed Once blkmapd has read a whole upcall, rpc_p
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: pnfs/blocklayout: Complete a device upcall when the pipe is closed Once blkmapd has read a whole upcall, rpc_pipe_read() unlinks the message from every pipe list, so the purges in rpc_pipe_release() and rpc_close_pipes() no longer reach it. bl_upcall_ops supplies no .release_pipe callback, and bl_pipe_destroy_msg() returns without completing the upcall because a downcall is expected to follow. A daemon that exits between the read and the write therefore strands its waiter: bl_resolve_deviceid() sleeps in wait_for_completion() and never returns, and it holds nn->bl_mutex across that wait, so every later device resolution in the net namespace blocks behind it. Add a .release_pipe that completes an upcall blkmapd has consumed and left unanswered. Completing an upcall retires it, so a message the framework has already purged is no longer in flight and is not completed a second time here.

items.title: CVE-2026-99379: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: validate SMB1 EA list bounds before parsing CIFSSMBQAllEAs() checks the server-provided EA list l
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: validate SMB1 EA list bounds before parsing CIFSSMBQAllEAs() checks the server-provided EA list length by adding it to the response pointer. On 32-bit systems, a positive length can wrap the pointer and pass the comparison. The parser then walks outside the received response while reading the next FEA header. A response with a list length of 0x40000000 reproduces this as a native i386 page fault and kernel panic from listxattr() against an SMB1 server. Check that the EA list starts within the SMB byte area before reading its header. Keep its length unsigned and compare it with the bytes left in the response without pointer addition. SMB1 is not negotiated by default and requires an explicit vers=1.0 mount.

items.title: CVE-2026-99364: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: Fix out-of-bounds read in the rpc_status dump nfsd_nl_rpc_status_get_dumpit() loads args->opcnt and args
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: Fix out-of-bounds read in the rpc_status dump nfsd_nl_rpc_status_get_dumpit() loads args->opcnt and args->ops separately, then walks ops[] before rechecking rq_status_counter. A COMPOUND that completes between the two loads runs nfsd4_release_compoundargs(), which zeroes opcnt and points ops back at the eight-entry inline array. A dump that already sampled an opcnt of 200 clamps it to the sixteen slots in rq_opnum, then indexes iops[0..15]. iops is the last member of struct nfsd4_compoundargs and rq_argp is allocated at exactly that size, so the walk runs off the end of the allocation. The trailing recheck discards the sampled data, but the read has already happened. NFSD_CMD_RPC_STATUS_GET carries no GENL_ADMIN_PERM, so an unprivileged local user can repeat the dump against a busy server until it lands in the window. Sample opcnt and ops into locals, then finish the counter recheck before dereferencing ops. An unchanged counter means both came from the same COMPOUND, where opcnt cannot exceed what ops holds.

items.title: CVE-2026-99365: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nfsd: Fix id-to-name cache entry leak in idtoname_parse() idtoname_lookup() returns the id-to-name cache entry
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nfsd: Fix id-to-name cache entry leak in idtoname_parse() idtoname_lookup() returns the id-to-name cache entry with a new reference. The name is parsed between the lookup and the update call, and when the parsed name is malformed (negative length or longer than IDMAP_NAMESZ), idtoname_parse() jumps to the error label without dropping the reference returned by idtoname_lookup(), leaking the cache entry. Release the reference with cache_put() before taking the error exit.

items.title: CVE-2026-99366: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nfsd: don't modify a session slot when replaying its cached reply nfsd4_sequence() claims a session slot by se
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nfsd: don't modify a session slot when replaying its cached reply nfsd4_sequence() claims a session slot by setting NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE under nn->client_lock. A reply served from the slot's reply cache does not claim it, and that distinction lived only in cstate->status, which nfsd4_sequence() set to nfserr_replay_cache. Commit cc028a10a48c ("NFSD: Hoist status code encoding into XDR encoder functions") moved nfsd4_proc_compound()'s cstate->status assignment below the out: label, and the replay path's goto out was the one path that relied on skipping it. The test in nfsd4_sequence_done() therefore no longer identifies a replay, and every replay now stores its reply and clears NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE as though it owned the slot. NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE is the interlock: check_slot_seqid() rejects every sequence id for a slot that is in use, before replay_matches_cache() runs. A replay never sets it, so two replays can be in flight on the same slot at once. One can read slot->sl_cred under nn->client_lock while the other's completion frees and rebuilds it from the XDR encoder without that lock. Two completions can also collide with e

items.title: CVE-2026-99367: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: Don't complete a cld upcall the daemon has not read cld_pipe_downcall() matches a reply to its upcall on
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: Don't complete a cld upcall the daemon has not read cld_pipe_downcall() matches a reply to its upcall on the xid alone. A write that arrives before the daemon has read that upcall completes __cld_pipe_upcall() while its struct rpc_pipe_msg is still queued on the pipe. The waiter returns, its stack frame goes away, and the pipe keeps a list_head that points into it. The next rpc_queue_upcall() walks that pointer: BUG: KASAN: vmalloc-out-of-bounds in __list_add_valid_or_report Read of size 8 at addr ffffc90007027950 by task syz.0.96/13066 __list_add_valid_or_report+0x6a/0x130 rpc_queue_upcall cld_pipe_upcall nfsd4_cld_grace_start nfsd4_cld_tracking_init The pipe is mode 0600 in rpc_pipefs, so the trigger is a broken or hostile nfsdcld rather than an unprivileged task. Record whether the daemon has consumed the whole message and complete only when it has. cld_pipe_destroy_msg() runs on every path by which the pipe releases a message, so it can maintain that flag under cn_lock. nfsdcld sends its -EINPROGRESS downcalls only after reading the upcall, so the new check does not break the GraceStart record stream.

items.title: CVE-2026-99368: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: Do not send CB_RECALL_ANY to NFSv4.0 clients deleg_reaper() sends CB_RECALL_ANY to every ACTIVE client h
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: Do not send CB_RECALL_ANY to NFSv4.0 clients deleg_reaper() sends CB_RECALL_ANY to every ACTIVE client holding delegations, but CB_RECALL_ANY is an NFSv4.1 operation. An NFSv4.0 client's callback service accepts only CB_GETATTR and CB_RECALL, so it replies OP_ILLEGAL. The decoder maps the unexpected opnum to -EIO, and nfsd4_cb_done() marks the client's callback channel down. Nothing brings the channel back. nfsd4_run_cb_work() sets NFSD4_CB_UP only for a minor version above zero, and the only nfsd4_probe_callback() call site an NFSv4.0 client reaches is nfsd4_setclientid_confirm(). One visit from the reaper therefore leaves the channel marked down until the client re-establishes its clientid. RENEW then returns NFS4ERR_CB_PATH_DOWN for as long as the client holds delegations. nfsd4_cb_channel_good() stops returning true, so the client is granted no further delegations. Skip clients at minor version zero.

items.title: CVE-2026-99369: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: Destroy a recalled delegation the client does not hold A client that answers CB_RECALL with NFS4ERR_BADH
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: Destroy a recalled delegation the client does not hold A client that answers CB_RECALL with NFS4ERR_BADHANDLE or NFS4ERR_BAD_STATEID has no record of the delegation, so the FREE_STATEID that clears it from cl_revoked never arrives. Every later SEQUENCE reply carries SEQ4_STATUS_RECALLABLE_STATE_REVOKED, and the client loops issuing TEST_STATEID. Destroy such a delegation when it is reaped rather than revoking it onto cl_revoked. RFC 8881 Section 20.2.4 completes the recall at the reply when its status is neither NFS4_OK nor NFS4ERR_DELAY, so a rejected recall leaves nothing to revoke. An administrative revoke keeps that path, since NFS4ERR_ADMIN_REVOKED reports it. A destroyed stateid returns NFS4ERR_BAD_STATEID instead of NFS4ERR_DELEG_REVOKED. A client that rejects the recall but still holds the delegation gets no notice that its state was revoked. CB_RECALL can outrun the reply that granted the delegation, so honor a rejection only once the client has seen that grant. items.title: CVE-2026-99370: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: copy SETXATTR data from all XDR buffer segments nfsd4_vbuf_from_vector() manually copies the head follow
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: copy SETXATTR data from all XDR buffer segments nfsd4_vbuf_from_vector() manually copies the head followed by whole pages starting at offset zero. This assumes that all remaining data starts at the beginning of the page array and that no data is stored in the tail. However, nfsd4_decode_setxattr() passes an xdr_buf returned by xdr_stream_subsegment(). Such a sub-buffer can have a nonzero page_base and can span its page and tail segments. Ignoring that layout can copy the wrong bytes into the value passed to vfs_setxattr(). Use read_bytes_from_xdr_buf(), which observes the complete xdr_buf layout.

items.title: CVE-2026-99371: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nfsd: clear XDR padding in GETXATTR replies nfsd4_vbuf_to_stream() uses a raw memcpy() for the first fragment
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nfsd: clear XDR padding in GETXATTR replies nfsd4_vbuf_to_stream() uses a raw memcpy() for the first fragment of an attribute value. xdr_reserve_space() aligns the reservation but does not initialize the extra bytes. If the complete value fits in that fragment, the loop that clears padding for the final fragment is never entered. A remote client reading an attribute whose length is not a multiple of four can therefore receive one to three stale bytes from the response page. Encode the first fragment with xdr_encode_opaque_fixed(), matching the final-fragment path and ensuring that any XDR padding is zeroed.

items.title: CVE-2026-99356: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: SUNRPC: Do not credit control-record octets to the RPC stream svc_tcp_sock_recv_cmsg() receives up to two octe
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: SUNRPC: Do not credit control-record octets to the RPC stream svc_tcp_sock_recv_cmsg() receives up to two octets into a local buffer, and returns that count for any record type other than TLS_RECORD_TYPE_ALERT. Nothing reached the caller's buffer, but svc_tcp_read_marker() adds the count to sk_tcplen and svc_tcp_read_msg()'s caller adds it to sk_datalen. The RPC stream advances over octets it never received. The fragment marker is assembled from stale sk_marker octets. The message body comes from pages nothing wrote. A conforming client reaches this. RFC 8446 Section 4.6.3 lets either peer send KeyUpdate once it has sent its Finished, and svcsock has no rekey path. kTLS leaves the partially consumed record on ctx->rx_list, so the body drains two octets per svc_tcp_recvfrom() call. Each pair is credited the same way. Return -EAGAIN for a record that is not an alert. That is what svc_tcp_sock_process_cmsg()'s default arm returned before the receive moved into a local buffer.

items.title: CVE-2026-99357: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: SUNRPC: Copy the deferred RPC Call from the head buffer svc_defer() snapshots the RPC Call for replay once a p
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: SUNRPC: Copy the deferred RPC Call from the head buffer svc_defer() snapshots the RPC Call for replay once a pending cache upcall resolves. Neither adjusts head[0].iov_len. Both lengths are size_t, so the subtraction underflows and the copy starts past head[0].iov_base. Every deferred integrity Call replays a shifted snapshot. A deferred replay skips GSS verification, so a shifted snapshot runs as an authenticated Call. With the privacy service the offset is client-chosen. items.title: CVE-2026-99358: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nfsd: zero NFSv4 COMPOUND tag padding nfs4svc_encode_compoundres() copies the tag bytes into reserved XDR spac
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nfsd: zero NFSv4 COMPOUND tag padding nfs4svc_encode_compoundres() copies the tag bytes into reserved XDR space and skips directly to the aligned end of the field. xdr_reserve_space() rounds the reservation up but does not initialize the padding bytes. A remote client can choose a tag length that is not a multiple of four, causing one to three stale bytes from the response page to be returned in the COMPOUND reply. Use xdr_encode_opaque_fixed() to copy the tag and clear its XDR padding.

items.title: CVE-2026-99359: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: validate transport name in listener_set before serv creation nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() holds nfsd_mute
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: validate transport name in listener_set before serv creation nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() holds nfsd_mutex for the whole listener teardown and rebuild. The code checks NFSD_A_SOCK_TRANSPORT_NAME for presence only, and not for content. An arbitrary name therefore reaches svc_xprt_create_from_sa(). There, a name that matches no registered class calls request_module("svc%s", name). That call is a TASK_KILLABLE usermode helper upcall, and it runs under nfsd_mutex. Check the name against the classes that NFSD can create: tcp, udp and rdma. The check goes in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(), which runs before the code takes nfsd_mutex. The rejection names the offending attribute through extack, since -EPROTONOSUPPORT on its own does not say which entry carried the bad name. This narrows the upcall. It does not remove it. NFSD accepts "rdma" without a condition, so on a kernel that does not build svcrdma the name still reaches request_module("svcrdma") under nfsd_mutex. That is necessary for the modular case, where the autoload is legitimate.

items.title: CVE-2026-99360: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: Set nn->cld_net before registering the cld pipe rpc_mkpipe_dentry() instantiates the pipe's dentry befor
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: Set nn->cld_net before registering the cld pipe rpc_mkpipe_dentry() instantiates the pipe's dentry before it returns, so the cld pipe can be opened as soon as nfsd4_cld_register_net() has run. __nfsd4_init_cld_pipe() does not store the new cld_net in nn->cld_net until after that call. cld_pipe_downcall() reaches the cld_net only through that pointer and takes cn_lock without checking it, so a write() that lands in the window oopses. Store nn->cld_net once @cn is fully initialized and before the pipe is registered, and clear it again when registration fails.

items.title: CVE-2026-99361: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nfsd: propagate SETXATTR value decode errors nfsd4_decode_setxattr() stores the status returned while assembli
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nfsd: propagate SETXATTR value decode errors nfsd4_decode_setxattr() stores the status returned while assembling a non-empty attribute value, but then unconditionally returns nfs_ok. An allocation failure can therefore leave a NULL value buffer paired with a non-zero length and allow compound processing to continue. Return the decoder status so that the operation stops on the original error.

items.title: CVE-2026-99362: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nfsd: preflight SEQUENCE replies before accepting a slot nfsd4_sequence() narrows the reply buffer to the sess
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nfsd: preflight SEQUENCE replies before accepting a slot nfsd4_sequence() narrows the reply buffer to the session's cached reply limit before it accepts the slot seqid. A client may negotiate ca_maxresponsesize_cached down to NFSD_MIN_HDR_SEQ_SZ, and nfsd4_alloc_slot() then gives every slot a zero-length sl_data[]. A COMPOUND tag can fill that narrowed buffer until it holds the SEQUENCE opcode but not the status word that follows. nfsd4_encode_operation() returns without running nfsd4_encode_sequence(), so cstate.data_offset stays zero. It leaves op->status at nfs_ok as well, so the COMPOUND is treated as having succeeded. nfsd4_store_cache_entry() declines to cache a lone SEQUENCE that returned an error. That test reads the status the operation reported, so it passes here. The copy starts at offset zero and takes the whole reply, RPC and COMPOUND headers included, into the zero-length sl_data[]. The COMPOUND tag is copied along with it, so the client picks most of the bytes written past the end of the slot: BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in read_bytes_from_xdr_buf+0x1bc/0x390 Write of size 80 at addr ffff888003a54

items.title: CVE-2026-99363: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: Map flex file layout IDs through the request's user namespace nfsd4_ff_proc_layoutget() and nfsd4_ff_enc
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: NFSD: Map flex file layout IDs through the request's user namespace nfsd4_ff_proc_layoutget() and nfsd4_ff_encode_layoutget() translate the file's owner and group with init_user_ns, but every other identity nfsd places on the wire goes through nfsd_user_namespace(). When the transport carries a credential from a non-initial user namespace, the flex file layout reports host-global IDs. The client copies those IDs into the AUTH_SYS credential it presents to the data server, and svcauth_unix_accept() resolves that credential in the transport's namespace, so data server I/O runs under an identity unrelated to the file's owner. Switching to the request's namespace introduces a second hazard. from_kuid() returns (uid_t)-1 when the target namespace has no mapping for the owner, and the IOMODE_READ arm adds one to that result to derive an identity for which the data server denies writes. The addition would wrap to zero, handing the client uid 0 instead of an identity distinct from the owner. items.title: CVE-2026-99348: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: afs: Fix afs to abort the rxrpc call on send error Fix afs_send_empty_reply() and afs_send_simple_reply() to a
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: afs: Fix afs to abort the rxrpc call on send error Fix afs_send_empty_reply() and afs_send_simple_reply() to always try to abort the rxrpc call rather than just aborting on -ENOMEM and otherwise abandoning it. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: rxrpc: Fix lack of short-send handling in rxrpc_kernel_send_data() Fix rxrpc_kernel_send_data() to loop around if it detects a short send. David Laight suggested doing it here rather than wrapping all the calls in loops. Further, remove the len argument and use the iterator count instead and return 0 on success, not the amount copied. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: rxrpc: Fix update of call->tx_pending without holding lock Currently, rxrpc_send_data() updates call->tx_pending just before it returns - but it won't be holding the call->user_mutex when it does this if a wait was interrupted by a signal. This would allow a parallel sendmsg() to race. Further, both the callers of rxrpc_send_data() call it with the lock held, and then it returns an indication through the parameter list to say whether it has dropped the lock or not - after which the callers both just drop the lock if it's still held. items.title: CVE-2026-99351: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: sunrpc: treat empty auth.unix.gid replies as negative entries When rpc.mountd cannot resolve a uid (getpwuid()
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: sunrpc: treat empty auth.unix.gid replies as negative entries When rpc.mountd cannot resolve a uid (getpwuid() or getgrouplist() failure, e.g. while winbind or sssd is briefly unreachable), it answers the auth.unix.gid upcall with zero groups. unix_gid_parse() installs that as a valid positive entry, and svcauth_unix_set_client() then replaces the credential's group list with the empty one on every request, RPCSEC_GSS included via svcauth_gss_set_client(). items.title: CVE-2026-99352: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: SUNRPC: trace an accepted transport before publishing it svc_handle_xprt() publishes a newly accepted transpor
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: SUNRPC: trace an accepted transport before publishing it svc_handle_xprt() publishes a newly accepted transport before tracing it. svc_add_new_temp_xprt() places the transport on sv_tempsocks and clears XPT_BUSY, so another nfsd thread can dequeue it at once. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: sunrpc: pin gss module across auth_domain RCU free A gss auth_domain stores a raw pointer to svcauthops_gss in dom->flavour, and its release queues svcauth_gss_domain_release_rcu() via call_rcu(). Both live in auth_rpcgss.ko text, and nothing pins the module while a domain referencing it is reachable. rmmod auth_rpcgss can therefore unmap that text while an NFSD export still holds a reference to the domain. The export cache is one such holder. When the export is finally released, the domain reference drops from module text: svc_export_put() auth_domain_put(exp->ex_client) auth_domain_release() dom->flavour->domain_release(dom) /* into module text */ svcauth_gss_domain_release() call_rcu(&dom->rcu_head, svcauth_gss_domain_release_rcu) Once auth_rpcgss is unloaded, the domain_release call lands in unmapped memory. The rcu_barrier() in exit_rpcsec_gss() does not help: it waits only for callbacks already queued, and this one is not queued until the export goes away. items.title: CVE-2026-99355: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: SUNRPC: fix oversized GSS proxy token copy gss_read_proxy_verf() allocates one page per token chunk, but it co
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: SUNRPC: fix oversized GSS proxy token copy gss_read_proxy_verf() allocates one page per token chunk, but it copies the entire linear head of an RPC request into in_token->pages[0]. A UDP datagram can leave more than PAGE_SIZE bytes in the linear head, so a large RPCSEC_GSS INIT token overwrites following pages. Copy the linear head in page-sized chunks before switching to the request page array. The linear head itself can span multiple pages.

items.title: CVE-2026-99340: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86: Take SRCU in kvm_zap_gfn_range() kvm_zap_gfn_range() walks memslots and rmaps and may drop mmu_lock
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86: Take SRCU in kvm_zap_gfn_range() kvm_zap_gfn_range() walks memslots and rmaps and may drop mmu_lock to reschedule. Callers that do not already hold kvm->srcu (or slots_lock) can race with memslot deletion: synchronize_srcu_expedited() does not wait, kvm_free_memslot() frees the old slot and its rmap, and the zap resumes on freed memory. The VFIO noncoherent-DMA path hits this by zapping the entire GPA space without SRCU. KASAN reported: BUG: KASAN: vmalloc-out-of-bounds in slot_rmap_walk_next+0x82/0x1c0 Read of size 8 at addr ffffc900005c1008 Call Trace: slot_rmap_walk_next+0x82/0x1c0 __kvm_rmap_zap_gfn_range+0x17a/0x280 kvm_zap_gfn_range+0x2a6/0x6a0 kvm_vfio_set_attr+0x576/0x770 kvm_device_ioctl+0x1ff/0x3b0 Take SRCU inside kvm_zap_gfn_range() so every caller is covered. Nesting with an existing kvm->srcu critical section is fine; the helper uses a local index. Drop the now-redundant SRCU pair from __kvm_set_or_clear_apicv_inhibit().

items.title: CVE-2026-99341: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86: Request event processing for exception VM-Exits Request event processing whenever kvm_queue_exceptio
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86: Request event processing for exception VM-Exits Request event processing whenever kvm_queue_exception_vmexit() queues an exception VM-Exit. Most callers reach the helper through kvm_multiple_exception(), which already sets KVM_REQ_EVENT, but nested asynchronous page faults call it directly. Without another event request, vcpu_enter_guest() skips kvm_check_and_inject_events() and re-enters L2. A subsequent VM-Exit can clear the pending exception while reconstructing vectoring state, losing the synthetic #PF VM-Exit. The APF reason remains PAGE_NOT_PRESENT and a later regular #PF can consume the stale value. Setting KVM_REQ_EVENT in the common helper ensures that L1 receives the queued VM-Exit before KVM re-enters L2.

items.title: CVE-2026-99342: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86/xen: Enforce 4-byte alignment of vcpu_info registration Xen's map_guest_area() enforces that vcpu_inf
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86/xen: Enforce 4-byte alignment of vcpu_info registration Xen's map_guest_area() enforces that vcpu_info is aligned to sizeof(xen_ulong_t). KVM has no such check, allowing a guest to register vcpu_info at an arbitrary byte alignment. Enforce unconditional 4-byte alignment regardless of the current shinfo mode. This is sufficient because subsequent commits ensure that all locked atomic operations on vcpu_info fields use at most 32-bit accesses. Return -ENXIO on failure, matching Xen's map_guest_area() behaviour for unaligned requests. Originally observed in review of an unrelated patch: https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260604193554.1BA311F00893@smtp.kernel.org/

items.title: CVE-2026-99343: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86/mmu: Bug the VM if KVM attempts to walk more levels than the MMU has Extend the "EFER.LMA && !CR4.PAE
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86/mmu: Bug the VM if KVM attempts to walk more levels than the MMU has Extend the "EFER.LMA && !CR4.PAE" check, which exists largely to guard against KVM configuring a paging32 MMU with more than 2 levels of paging, with a very explicit check for exactly that: that KVM isn't trying to walk more levels of paging than the MMU template provides. I.e. harden KVM against all bugs that would cause KVM to generates accesses beyond the bounds of guest_walker's arrays, regardless of how KVM ended up with the misconfigured MMU. Note, don't use w->cpu_role.base.level directly as the paging64 template only provides two levels of page tables for PAE paging on 32-bit hosts, and handles the third level by manually emulating the PDPTR access.

items.title: CVE-2026-99344: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: nSVM: Ignore EFER.LMA if EFER.LME=0 when preparing L2 state Force EFER.LMA=0 if EFER.LME=0 when preparing
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: nSVM: Ignore EFER.LMA if EFER.LME=0 when preparing L2 state Force EFER.LMA=0 if EFER.LME=0 when preparing L2 state for VMRUN, i.e. mimic real hardware's behavior of ignoring EFER.LMA if EFER.LME=0. VMRUN unfortunately allows the nonsensical combination, i.e. doesn't fail, but KVM itself has an invariant EFER.LMA can be set et if and only if EFER.LME is set. Breaking that invariant can lead to a variety of issue, particularly in MMU code that keys off EFER.LMA when determining whether to emulate/virtualization 4/5-level paging versus PAE paging.

items.title: CVE-2026-99345: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: nSVM: Reject KVM_SET_NESTED_STATE if L1 has EFER.LMA=1 && EFER.LME=0 Reject KVM_SET_NESTED_STATE if the i
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: nSVM: Reject KVM_SET_NESTED_STATE if L1 has EFER.LMA=1 && EFER.LME=0 Reject KVM_SET_NESTED_STATE if the incoming L1 host state has what is effectively an impossible EFER combination of LMA=1 but LME=0, i.e. if the state says long mode is active but not enabled. Unlike VMX, SVM doesn't have an explicit consistent check for the illegal combination; presumably hardware simply ignores EFER.LMA if EFER.LME=0. Unfortunately, KVM doesn't ignore EFER.LMA in this case and consumes the illegal state when constructing the shadow MMU for L2. E.g. if userspace also clears CR4.PAE, then kvm_calc_cpu_role() will compute a role with 4 or 5 levels of paging, but shadow_mmu_init_context() will wire up the MMU to use the paging32 template, which maxes out its levels at 2. Note, the "real badness" is effectively the same as what happened with the nVMX bug fixed by commit 112e66017bff ("KVM: nVMX: add missing consistency checks for CR0 and CR4"). items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: SVM: Trigger new ASID allocation in both VMCBs on pCPU switch When the pCPU where the VMCB was most recently used is switched, reset the ASID generation in both VMCBs, triggering new ASID allocation for the immediate VMRUN as well as the next VMRUN on the other VMCB. The ASID is shared between vmcb01 and vmcb02, and gets flushed on every nested transition. However, since pCPU tracking is done per VMCB, it is possible for one VMCB to allocate a new ASID when migrated to a new pCPU, and then the other VMCB reuses that ASID on the old pCPU. This can result in the same ASID being used by multiple vCPUs on the old pCPU. Example scenario: - vCPU runs on pCPU A, vmcb01 is active, asid=1. - vCPU migrates to pCPU B, vmcb01 pCPU changes, new asid=2. - Another vCPU runs on pCPU A and allocates asid=2 as well. - vCPU migrates back to pCPU A, and then switches to vmcb02 before it runs again with vmcb01. - No pCPU switch is detected for vmcb02, so VMRUN is done with asid=2. - Two vCPUs end up using asid=2 on the same pCPU. items.title: CVE-2026-99347: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: x86: hdmi: fix chmap array missing terminator entry had_build_channel_allocation_map() allocates a singl
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: x86: hdmi: fix chmap array missing terminator entry had_build_channel_allocation_map() allocates a single struct snd_pcm_chmap_elem via kzalloc() and stores it as intelhaddata->chmap->chmap. struct snd_pcm_chmap.chmap is expected to be a zero-terminated array (see snd_pcm_std_chmaps[]), but had_register_chmap_ctls() never overrides the TLV callback installed by snd_pcm_add_chmap_ctls(), so the generic pcm_chmap_ctl_tlv() from ALSA core is left in place. pcm_chmap_ctl_tlv() is reachable by any local user via SNDRV_CTL_IOCTL_TLV_READ on the "Playback Channel Map" control and walks the array with "for (map = info->chmap; map->channels; map++)". Since the driver's single element is never terminated, this walks past the allocation. The same pointer is also freed on hot-unplug and rebuilt on hot-plug under intelhaddata->mutex, while the TLV callback runs under card->controls_rwsem without that mutex, so the walk can also race a concurrent free of the array. items.title: CVE-2026-99332: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: core: Fix out-of-bounds left shift by 32 in s32ton() Syzbot reported an out-of-bounds shift (32-bit integ
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: core: Fix out-of-bounds left shift by 32 in s32ton() Syzbot reported an out-of-bounds shift (32-bit integer shifted left by 32) in the s32ton() routine in the HID core. This routine converts a signed 32-bit integer to a signed n-bit integer, and it caps the value of n at 32. But when n == 32 there's no need to do anything; it can simply return the input value. This will avoid calculating (1 << n) when n is 32, which was the cause of the invalid shift.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: amd_sfh: Use report type from request node Use report type from request node while sending feature and input reports to HID core. items.title: CVE-2026-99334: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: PPC: Book3S HV: Add preempt_disable() around virtual-mode HPTE bit-lock users kvmppc_hv_find_lock_hpte()
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: PPC: Book3S HV: Add preempt_disable() around virtual-mode HPTE bit-lock users kvmppc_hv_find_lock_hpte() requires virtual-mode callers to run with preemption disabled, because it can return with HPTE_V_HVLOCK still held until the caller later unlocks the HPTE.
