The handlers for H_ENTER, H_REMOVE, H_READ, H_CLEAR_MOD, H_CLEAR_REF, H_PROTECT, and H_BULK_REMOVE spin on try_lock_hpte() or lock_rmap(), and H_ENTER also reaches kvmppc_do_h_enter(), which uses arch_spin_lock() on kvm->mmu_lock. items.title: CVE-2026-99335: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: guest_memfd: Establish memslot guest_memfd bindings *after* memslot is ready Wait to bind a memslot to
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: guest_memfd: Establish memslot guest_memfd bindings *after* memslot is ready Wait to bind a memslot to a guest_memfd instance until *after* the memslot is fully prepared, as creating the binding in guest_memfd will effectively expose the memslot to readers. As pointed out by Sashiko, binding the memslot before it's ready to be exposed to the rest of the world can break various memslot assumption and rules. E.g. x86 could observe a NULL rmap pointer if a PUNCH_HOLE hit the guest_memfd after the binding was created, but before KVM made it through kvm_prepare_memory_region().

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: guest_memfd: take the invalidate lock when unbinding a dying file kvm_gmem_unbind() takes mapping->invalidate_lock only if the get_file_active() succeeds. When the guest_memfd file is dying, its reference count is already zero so get_file_active fails and the binding is removed without holding the invalidate lock. kvm_gmem_invalidate_{start,end}() checks f->bindings independently to decide whether to begin or end KVM MMU invalidation. So, the bindings must therefore remain stable between the two calls. Otherwise, unbind can remove a binding after start increments mmu_invalidate_in_progress, but before end finds the binding and decrements it. items.title: CVE-2026-99337: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: TDX: Enable Bus Lock VM exit Enable Bus Lock VM exit functionality for TDX guests. Bus Lock VM exit is a
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: TDX: Enable Bus Lock VM exit Enable Bus Lock VM exit functionality for TDX guests. Bus Lock VM exit is an existing feature supported by KVM. Userspace can enable Bus Lock VM exit through KVM_BUS_LOCK_DETECTION_EXIT when it's reported as supported. However, KVM reports the support of this CAP just based on the hardware capability but doesn't differentiate between VMX and TDX. This leads to the issue that userspace can enable this cap for TDX guests without getting an error, but the feature is not actually enabled because KVM doesn't call the TDX module API to program the relevant TD VMCS fields. Enable Bus Lock VM exit for TDX guests by programming the BUS_LOCK_DETECTION control in the TD VMCS and by adding the exit handler. Note, there is no enumeration bit for this feature by TDX module because all TDX modules support it and allow to set the TD VMCS as long as the hardware supports the feature.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: TDX: Enable Notify VM exit Enable Notify VM exit functionality for TDX guests. Notify VM exit is an existing feature supported by KVM. Userspace can enable Notify VM exit through KVM_CAP_X86_NOTIFY_VMEXIT when it's reported as supported. However, KVM reports the support of this CAP just based on the hardware capability but doesn't differentiate between VMX and TDX. This leads to the issue that userspace can enable this cap for TDX guests without getting an error, but the feature is not actually enabled because KVM doesn't call the TDX module API to program the relevant TD VMCS fields. Enable Notify VM exit for TDX guests by: - Invoking TDX module API calls to set NOTIFY_VM_EXITING and Notify Window in TD VMCS. It's done in tdx_vcpu_init() where other TD VMCS bits are set. Since TDX vCPU cannot be reset, it only needs to be configured once when initializing the TDX vCPU. - Adding corresponding exit handler for TDX Notify VM Exit. items.title: CVE-2026-99339: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86: Zero reserved synic flags when delivering message to avoid stack leak Ensure all reserved flags are
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86: Zero reserved synic flags when delivering message to avoid stack leak Ensure all reserved flags are zeroed when setting the msg_pending flag as part of SynIC message delivery, as setting only msg_pending can leak seven bits of kernel stack data to the guest. E.g. gcc typically uses a bitwise-OR to set the msg_pending flag, without initializing the on-stack variable. Precisely zero the flags, e.g. as opposed to zeroing the entire structure, to make it somewhat more obvious that the flags *need* to be zeroed. E.g. it would be quite easy to misread the initial read of guest memory and think that zeroing the entire structure is completely superfluous.

items.title: CVE-2026-99323: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix invalid pointer dereference when get_inode_acl() fails When get_inode_acl() fails, it returns an ER
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix invalid pointer dereference when get_inode_acl() fails When get_inode_acl() fails, it returns an ERR_PTR(), but ksmbd_acls_fattr() stored that pointer in smb_fattr without checking for errors. Later callers then passed the error pointer to security descriptor helpers or posix_acl_release(), resulting in an invalid pointer dereference. This was reproduced on an XFS-backed share when xfs_get_acl() returned ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM). Querying the SMB ACL from a CIFS client triggered the crash: BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: fffffffffffffff8 RIP: smb_acl_sec_desc_scratch_len+0x58/0x90 [ksmbd] Call Trace: smb2_query_info+0x40d/0x17c0 [ksmbd] handle_ksmbd_work+0x1ca/0x770 [ksmbd] Fix this by checking the return values from get_inode_acl() in ksmbd_acls_fattr(). Treat -EOPNOTSUPP as indicating that no ACL is available, and propagate all other errors to the callers. Update smb2_open() and smb2_get_info_sec() to handle these errors.

items.title: CVE-2026-99324: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix out-of-bounds read when padding the final compound response Compound response handling pads the las
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix out-of-bounds read when padding the final compound response Compound response handling pads the last response of a compound to an 8-byte boundary by growing the final iov and the RFC1002 length. smb2_allocate_rsp_buf() allocates exactly response_sz. A command can fill the response buffer to within 7 bytes of its end, for example a QUERY_INFO whose output is bounded only by the space left. The padding can then run past the allocation, and ksmbd_tcp_writev() reads those bytes when it sends the response. BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in _copy_from_iter+0x744/0x10e0 Call Trace: _copy_from_iter+0x744/0x10e0 tcp_sendmsg_locked+0x2290/0x3f80 ksmbd_tcp_writev+0x10c7/0x1ab0 [ksmbd] Allocate room for the padding when the request is a compound, as smb2_read() and smb2_read_pipe() do for their payloads. response_sz is unchanged, so commands still fill only up to it, and kvzalloc() zeroes the padding.

items.title: CVE-2026-99325: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: hid-lenovo-go-s: Add suspend function and gate access under bool. Currently a device can suspend while de
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: hid-lenovo-go-s: Add suspend function and gate access under bool. Currently a device can suspend while delayed work is pending or executing. Cancel delayed work if it was pending and restart it if it hasn't run yet. Gate access to show/store functions behind a bool to prevent access prior to cfg_setup() being completed.

items.title: CVE-2026-99326: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: hid-lenovo-go-s: Prevent deadlock if device removed during setup hid_gos_cfg_remove() calls a mutex befor
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: hid-lenovo-go-s: Prevent deadlock if device removed during setup hid_gos_cfg_remove() calls a mutex before canceling delayed work. That delayed work function calls mcu_property_out(), which holds the same mutex. Prevent deadlock my removing the mutex prior to stopping the work. Additionally, since cancel_delayed_work has the potential to re-arm, switch to disable_delayed_work.

items.title: CVE-2026-99327: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: roccat: kovaplus: reject short button reports The raw event callback runs before HID core validates and z
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: roccat: kovaplus: reject short button reports The raw event callback runs before HID core validates and zero-pads the report. It passes the buffer to helpers which inspect data[0] and read a complete struct kovaplus_mouse_report_button for button reports. A truncated report can therefore cause an out-of-bounds read. Require enough data for the button report before calling either helper. Commit 47669bec44fe ("HID: asus: refactor the two workqueues and init sequence") added the same kind of raw-event length validation to hid-asus.

items.title: CVE-2026-99328: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: picoLCD: check for fb_deferred_io_init() error fb_deferred_io_init() allocates deferred I/O state, popula
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: picoLCD: check for fb_deferred_io_init() error fb_deferred_io_init() allocates deferred I/O state, populating info->fbdefio_state, or leaving it NULL if an error occurs. Currently picolcd_init_framebuffer() ignores its return value. Therefore if an error arises in fb_deferred_io_init() (for instance, due to an allocation failure) info->fbdefio_state is left NULL. When the file is subsequently opened, fb_open() will dereference a NULL pointer (calling fb_deferred_io_open()). Fix this by checking for the error. Also correct cleanup ordering - defio is initialised after the sysfs file, so cleanup defio first.

items.title: CVE-2026-99329: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: mcp2221: always initialize and cancel init_work The writable gpio_mode_enforce parameter can change betwe
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: mcp2221: always initialize and cancel init_work The writable gpio_mode_enforce parameter can change between probe and remove. If it changes from false to true after probe, remove skips cancellation of init_work. Pending or running work can then access devm-managed driver state after teardown. Changing it from true to false can make remove cancel an uninitialized delayed work item. Initialize init_work whenever IIO is reachable and cancel it unconditionally on remove. Keep the parameter check only for scheduling the initialization. The false-to-true cancellation gap was previously reported by Sashiko. We also encountered this issue during our static-analysis research.

items.title: CVE-2026-99330: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: mcp2200: validate READ_ALL response length The HID core invokes raw_event callbacks before validating the
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: mcp2200: validate READ_ALL response length The HID core invokes raw_event callbacks before validating the report length. mcp2200_raw_event() casts a READ_ALL response to struct mcp_read_all_resp and reads fields through offset ten without checking that the response contains the structure. A one-byte READ_ALL response reproduced the issue under KASAN: BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in mcp2200_raw_event+0x24b/0x3a0 Read of size 1 by task hidtrigger/89 Call Trace: mcp2200_raw_event+0x24b/0x3a0 kasan_report+0x139/0x170 Reject an incomplete READ_ALL response with a protocol error before reading its fields. The common completion path then wakes the command waiter with the error instead of leaving it to time out. Commit 47669bec44fe ("HID: asus: refactor the two workqueues and init sequence") added the same kind of raw_event length validation to hid-asus.

items.title: CVE-2026-99331: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: cp2112: validate response report lengths The HID core invokes raw_event callbacks before validating the r
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: cp2112: validate response report lengths The HID core invokes raw_event callbacks before validating the report length. cp2112_raw_event() reads every field of a transfer status response without checking size. For a data response, it reads the length at offset two and copies that many bytes from offset three, again without ensuring that the input report contains them. Require a complete transfer status structure. For data responses, first require the header and then ensure the clamped payload length fits in the received report before copying it. Commit 47669bec44fe ("HID: asus: refactor the two workqueues and init sequence") added the same kind of raw_event length validation to hid-asus.

items.title: CVE-2026-87867: MRemoteNG establishes encrypted but unauthenticated channel with Microsoft SQL Server backend. Client accepts any certificate the server presents, including a self-signed certifica
items.summary: MRemoteNG establishes encrypted but unauthenticated channel with Microsoft SQL Server backend. Client accepts any certificate the server presents, including a self-signed certificate supplied by an attacker. An attacker positioned between the client and the SQL server (for example via ARP/DNS spoofing) can transparently pintercept the connection (man-in-the-middle) and read all traffic, including the encrypted connection-password table read and the database login. Vendor did not provide the range of vulnerable versions. Only version 1.76.20 was tested and confirmed vulnerable. Other versions may also be vulnerable.

items.title: CVE-2026-87868: MRemoteNG uses single MD5 hash with no salt and no iterations for key-derivation. An attacker who obtains the encrypted data can brute-force a weak or moderate passphrase offline a
items.summary: MRemoteNG uses single MD5 hash with no salt and no iterations for key-derivation. An attacker who obtains the encrypted data can brute-force a weak or moderate passphrase offline at extreme speed and then decrypt every stored connection password. When the default passphrase is in use, no cracking is needed at all; the key is derived from a publicly known value. Vendor did not provide the range of vulnerable versions. Only version 1.76.20 was tested and confirmed vulnerable. Other versions may also be vulnerable.

items.title: CVE-2026-99321: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: rust_binder: wake epoll on self-work queued to poll thread When a thread pushes work to its own todo list, Inn
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: rust_binder: wake epoll on self-work queued to poll thread When a thread pushes work to its own todo list, InnerThread::push_work() returns PushWorkRes::OkNotifyPoll if the thread uses epoll, but four call sites in thread.rs discard this return value. As a result, a non-blocking BC_* write that enqueues work onto the calling thread's todo list without also reading will not wake epoll. Check the return value and call self.process.notify_poll(false) when PushWorkRes::OkNotifyPoll is returned. This is similar to commit 97830f3c3088 ("binder: signal epoll threads of self-work"), but in C Binder pending thread work also prevented subsequent process work from waking epoll, causing a permanent hang, which is not the case in Rust Binder. This means that in practice, it merely delays notifications rather than completely failing to send them.

items.title: CVE-2026-99322: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: rebind completed CREATE replays without draining the old channel A completed DurableHandleReqV2 CREATE
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: rebind completed CREATE replays without draining the old channel A completed DurableHandleReqV2 CREATE can be replayed through another channel while its original channel is exiting. The existing replay path returns the open but leaves its connection and oplock references pointing at the old channel. Its open count also stays on that channel, and a later CLOSE through the surviving channel decrements the wrong counter. After checking the owner, lease key and persistent flag, verify that an active open is still published in the requesting session's file table. Do this even when no oplock was granted, and before processing a consumed replay. Do not read a borrowed opinfo session pointer for this check. Keep a healthy original binding. If the original channel is exiting or releasing, move the open and its own oplock references to the requesting channel. Serialize this with CLOSE using the session file-table lock, and with detach, reconnect and notification snapshots using m_lock. The earlier lock index and lease-table changes make their lifetimes independent of this connection change. No old-channel r_count wait

items.title: CVE-2026-15353: SOAP information disclosure through malformed array dimensions. The SOAP extension reads an uninitialized array position when decoding an encoded array whose arraySize attribute i
items.summary: SOAP information disclosure through malformed array dimensions. The SOAP extension reads an uninitialized array position when decoding an encoded array whose arraySize attribute is empty, whitespace-only or non-numeric, or when such dimensions come from a WSDL definition. Four bytes of unrelated heap data can then be used as an integer key in the decoded array. An unauthenticated remote client can trigger this with a crafted request to a SoapServer endpoint, and a malicious SOAP server with a response to SoapClient. Heap memory is disclosed only if the application returns or otherwise exposes the decoded array. This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.summary: MISP contains an authorization flaw in the handling of remote pull and feed operations. When a non-internal pull or a feed processes incoming data and encounters an existing sharing group, the application did not verify that the remote server's organization was actually a member of that sharing group before allowing the group's metadata to be updated. For non-internal pulls and feeds, the check was insufficient: a remote server whose organization was not a member of the target sharing group could still cause the group record to be modified (for example, altering the local flag, the modified timestamp, or other group properties). A feed, which has no associated server organization at all, could likewise trigger an update to an existing sharing group's metadata. items.summary: MISP contains an authorization and input-validation flaw in its event push mechanism. When a user with push permissions initiates a push of events to a remote MISP instance, the system fails to enforce two critical checks: (1) it does not verify that an event is published before including it in the push, allowing unpublished (i.e., not yet publicly shared) events to be transmitted to the remote server; and (2) it does not verify that the pushing user has read access to the event, causing events the user cannot fetch to be sent as empty event shells, thereby disclosing the existence and metadata of events the user is not authorized to view. Additionally, the remote server's reply selecting which offered events to accept is used without validating that the selected identifiers actually correspond to events in the offered set, potentially allowing the remote to reference events outside the intended scope. The vulnerability requires an authenticated user with push permissions on the source MISP instance and a configured push target. items.summary: Goproxy before 1.9.4 contains a weak key generation vulnerability in NewCounterEncryptorRandFromKey that derives RSA and Ed25519 leaf certificate private keys from public data due to misuse of hash.Sum. items.summary: MISP contains a vulnerability in the cryptographic signature verification of protected events. When a MISP instance signs a protected event for synchronization, it strips all whitespace from the JSON body before computing the PGP signature (preg_replace("/\s+/", "", $data)). The receiving instance accepts the modified event as authentic. The vulnerability affects the protected event synchronization path: event creation (EventsController::add), event editing (EventsController::edit), event viewing (EventsController::view1), and server-to-server pull synchronization (ServerSyncTool, Server model). items.title: CVE-2026-133190: MISP, a threat intelligence sharing platform, contains a vulnerability in its cryptographic key management for protected (PGP-signed) events. Two related defects allow a revoked PG
items.summary: MISP, a threat intelligence sharing platform, contains a vulnerability in its cryptographic key management for protected (PGP-signed) events. Two related defects allow a revoked PGP key to remain effective for signing and validating protected events. First, the validateProtectedEvent() method in the CryptographicKey model iterates over the event's stored cryptographic keys to verify a PGP signature but does not check the revoked flag on each key. A key explicitly marked as revoked is still used to validate signatures, meaning an entity whose key has been revoked can continue to sign protected events and have them accepted by the MISP instance. Second, the captureCryptographicKeyUpdate() method, responsible for synchronizing the key list when a sync user edits a protected event, contained a query bug (find('first') instead of find('all')) that caused only the first stored key to be considered. As a result, revocations of additional keys were never persisted, keys absent from the pushed list were not removed, and entries lacking an explicit fingerprint were mismatched and incorrectly deleted. Additionally, the revocation logic did not enforce the invariant that a revocation, once sto

items.title: CVE-2026-133178: flowintel allows users with editor-level access to author case and task fields, including aggregated tags. When these records are exported as CSV, the field values are written verb
items.summary: flowintel allows users with editor-level access to author case and task fields, including aggregated tags. When these records are exported as CSV, the field values are written verbatim into the output file. Because no sanitisation is applied to user-supplied text before CSV serialisation, an attacker can store values that begin with spreadsheet formula triggers (such as =, +, -, @, or their fullwidth Unicode equivalents, or leading control/whitespace characters). When a victim opens the exported CSV in a spreadsheet application (e.g. Microsoft Excel, LibreOffice Calc), the stored text is interpreted and executed as a live formula rather than displayed as literal text. This can lead to unintended data manipulation within the spreadsheet, potential data exfiltration via formula functions, or execution of downstream commands depending on the spreadsheet application and its configuration. The vulnerability requires the victim to actively open the CSV file in a spreadsheet application; the flowintel application itself is not directly compromised. Affected: <4.1.0

items.title: CVE-2026-133175: MISP contains an authorization bypass in its server-to-server proposal synchronization mechanism. Two related flaws were identified: 1. The events/pushProposals endpoint located t
items.summary: MISP contains an authorization bypass in its server-to-server proposal synchronization mechanism. Two related flaws were identified: 1. The events/pushProposals endpoint located the target event by UUID without enforcing any access-control check. A sync user with perm_sync could push shadow-attribute proposals to any event on the local instance, including events with restricted distribution (e.g., distribution level 0, visible only to the owning organisation). The stored proposal also carried the sender-supplied event_uuid and event_org_id rather than the local event's actual identity, corrupting the data model. 2. When accepting an edit proposal (old_id != 0), the code resolved the target live attribute by UUID alone (Attribute.uuid = shadow.uuid) without scoping the lookup to the proposal's own event. A malicious sync user could therefore craft a proposal whose uuid matched an attribute in a different event; upon acceptance, the wrong attribute would be modified or deleted. The same unscoped lookup existed in the ShadowAttribute::acceptProposal path. Preconditions: an authenticated user with sync permission (perm_sync) on a MISP instance that participates in server-to-server sync

items.title: CVE-2026-133177: MISP contains an authorization flaw in the sharing group capture logic. When a sharing group is re-captured with a newer modified timestamp and an updated roster, the application u
items.summary: MISP contains an authorization flaw in the sharing group capture logic. When a sharing group is re-captured with a newer modified timestamp and an updated roster, the application unconditionally overwrote the type, nationality, sector, and contacts fields of every organisation listed in the roster, including the host organisation. This behaviour was reachable by any user holding the perm_sync role, and additionally by any external server pulled from or any feed fetched, because those operations execute with the privileges of the site administrator who initiated them. As a result, a low-privileged sync user or a malicious/compromised external feed or pull source could silently corrupt organisation records on the receiving MISP instance without any site-admin or internal-sync authorization. The vulnerability does not disclose data or affect availability; the impact is limited to integrity of organisation metadata (type, nationality, sector, contacts). items.title: CVE-2026-133161: ### Summary ui With `strip_ansi=True`, Pydantic AI Harness's `ToolOutputLimits` capability removes ANSI escape sequences from tool output with a pattern that takes time quadratic
items.summary: ### Summary ui With `strip_ansi=True`, Pydantic AI Harness's `ToolOutputLimits` capability removes ANSI escape sequences from tool output with a pattern that takes time quadratic in the length of a line. A tool result of a few hundred kilobytes, crafted with many unterminated escape sequences, can occupy the event loop for tens of seconds to minutes, delaying every other request and agent run in the process. ### Details This affects applications that set `strip_ansi=True` on `ToolOutputLimits` (named `OverflowingToolOutput` before 0.13.0) and run tools whose output an attacker can influence, such as shell commands, file reads, fetched pages or MCP servers. Stripping runs on the event loop before the capability reduces the output, so its own size limits do not bound it. The assumed attacker can place text in content a tool returns. ### Mitigation Upgrade `pydantic-ai-harness` to 0.70.0 or later. Until then, leave `strip_ansi` at its default, `False`. On Pydantic AI v1, the harness cannot be upgraded past 0.4.0. Upgrade to Pydantic AI v2 and `pydantic-ai-harness` 0.70.0, or leave `strip_ansi` off.

items.title: CVE-2026-132039: In Eclipse Ditto versions before 3.9.9, Thing events delivered via WebSocket, Server-Sent Events and connections disclose field values which the policy does not allow the subscribe
items.summary: In Eclipse Ditto versions before 3.9.9, Thing events delivered via WebSocket, Server-Sent Events and connections disclose field values which the policy does not allow the subscriber to read. A READ revoke for one subject of the subscriber's authorization context is not applied when another of its subjects is granted READ. For subscribers with partial READ access, subscription RQL filters, the SSE `_context`, `thing-json` placeholders and extra fields are evaluated on the unfiltered event. This allows an authenticated subscriber with at least partial READ access to a Thing to obtain the values of fields it may not read when events for that Thing are emitted.

items.title: CVE-2026-129700: In Eclipse Ditto versions 2.4.0 to 3.9.8, Thing fields a requester is not allowed to read can be disclosed through the `condition` and `live-channel-condition` headers, which are e
items.summary: In Eclipse Ditto versions 2.4.0 to 3.9.8, Thing fields a requester is not allowed to read can be disclosed through the `condition` and `live-channel-condition` headers, which are evaluated against the full Thing: the READ check of `live-channel-condition` is skipped when a `condition` header is also present on Thing query commands (3.0.0 to 3.9.8); both headers are evaluated without any authorization on WoT Thing Description requests (`Accept: application/td+json`) when WoT TD permission filtering is not active (by default in 3.0.0 to 3.8.14, in 2.4.x with WoT integration enabled, and in 3.9.x with filtering disabled); the `condition` of live messages and live events is evaluated without a READ check, and of claim messages without any permission (3.1.0 to 3.9.8); and the twin response of a Thing query with a non-matching `live-channel-condition` is returned without filtering it by the policy (3.0.0 to 3.9.8). This allows an authenticated user to read Thing fields they are not allowed to read, in some cases without any permission on the Thing.

items.title: CVE-2026-129702: In Eclipse Ditto versions before 3.8.15 and 3.9.0 to 3.9.8, the policy enforcers do not let a revoke win over a grant in two kinds of permission checks. Checks of several permissio
items.summary: In Eclipse Ditto versions before 3.8.15 and 3.9.0 to 3.9.8, the policy enforcers do not let a revoke win over a grant in two kinds of permission checks. Checks of several permissions at once compare the highest grant weight with the highest revoke weight across all requested permissions instead of per permission, so the "check permissions" API (`POST /api/2/checkPermissions`, available since 3.7.0) can report a set of permissions as granted although one of them is revoked. Partial permission checks, which authorize retrieving Things and Policies and determine the receivers of events, count a grant on a sub-resource although the same permission is revoked on that sub-resource for another subject of the same authorization context (or, with the memory-optimized policy evaluator, for the same subject). A requester can thereby learn about the existence of Things and Policies and receive metadata without any readable content, and an application relying on the check permissions result may grant access the policy denies. The content of retrieved Things and Policies is still filtered correctly, and modifications are not affected.

items.title: CVE-2026-129916: In Eclipse Ditto versions 3.9.0 to 3.9.8, the resolved policy view (`GET /api/2/policies/{policyId}?policy-view=resolved`) does not restrict merged policy content to what the calle
items.summary: In Eclipse Ditto versions 3.9.0 to 3.9.8, the resolved policy view (`GET /api/2/policies/{policyId}?policy-view=resolved`) does not restrict merged policy content to what the caller may read in the policy it originates from. Imported and namespace-root entries are returned in full as soon as the caller may read any part of them in the source policy, entries of transitive imports and of the imports of namespace-root policies are only checked against the intermediate policy, and content copied into an entry by `references`, also from another entry of the same policy, is not checked against the referenced entry. An authenticated caller with READ on a policy can therefore read subjects, resources and granted/revoked permissions of policy entries that are hidden from them, including by explicit revokes, when reading the originating policy directly.

items.title: CVE-2026-129474: Use-after-free in magic method backtraces can lead to remote code execution. When collecting the arguments of a method call handled by __call() or __callStatic() for a backtrace,
items.summary: Use-after-free in magic method backtraces can lead to remote code execution. When collecting the arguments of a method call handled by __call() or __callStatic() for a backtrace, PHP can read stale values that may refer to freed memory. If a fatal error such as exceeding memory_limit occurs while an application enters such a call, with fatal_error_backtraces enabled (the default) and zend.exception_ignore_args disabled, a remote attacker who controls enough request data to influence memory allocation may cause memory corruption, crash the PHP worker or, with knowledge of memory addresses, execute arbitrary code. php.ini-production enables zend.exception_ignore_args, which prevents this. This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.title: CVE-2026-129481: Use-after-free after interrupted session shutdown. The session extension records the filename of the executing script when a session starts. If a fatal error occurs in an applicat
items.summary: Use-after-free after interrupted session shutdown. The session extension records the filename of the executing script when a session starts. If a fatal error occurs in an application callback while the session variables are destroyed at shutdown, such as stream_close() of a user-defined stream wrapper, the pointer is retained after the request memory is freed, and a later request handled by the same worker can free the stale string. An attacker who can trigger such a failing cleanup may crash the worker or corrupt memory; code execution has not been demonstrated. This requires the filename to be allocated in request memory, for example when the script is not cached by OPcache. This issue affects PHP versions 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.title: CVE-2026-129496: Timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution. In non-thread-safe builds, a diagnostic written to a file-based error_log during module startup, for example for a
items.summary: Timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution. In non-thread-safe builds, a diagnostic written to a file-based error_log during module startup, for example for an invalid date.timezone value or a session configuration warning, causes the timezone cache to be allocated in startup memory that is freed while a reference to it is kept. A diagnostic raised early in the first request of a worker, such as the max_input_vars warning, then accesses the freed cache. On such a deployment an unauthenticated remote attacker can crash PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php or CGI workers with a crafted request. Arbitrary code execution may be possible and has been demonstrated with known memory addresses. This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.title: CVE-2026-129501: Double free during DOM XML serialization. The XML serializer of Dom\XMLDocument and Dom\HTMLDocument can share ownership of a generated namespace prefix between the namespace-pref
items.summary: Double free during DOM XML serialization. The XML serializer of Dom\XMLDocument and Dom\HTMLDocument can share ownership of a generated namespace prefix between the namespace-prefix maps of an element and a descendant, so the prefix is used after being freed and then freed a second time. The document does not need to be malformed. An application that parses attacker-controlled XML or HTML with these classes and serializes it with saveXml() can be crashed, and repeated requests can cause denial of service. Code execution has not been demonstrated. This issue affects PHP versions 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.title: CVE-2026-129506: SOAP use-after-free when processing DTD entity references. The SOAP extension frees the document type definition (DTD) of a parsed XML document while attribute values can still re
items.summary: SOAP use-after-free when processing DTD entity references. The SOAP extension frees the document type definition (DTD) of a parsed XML document while attribute values can still refer to entities it owns, and can then read freed memory. Removing the DTD also bypasses the SOAP server's rejection of documents that contain one. An unauthenticated remote attacker who can send a crafted request to a SOAP endpoint, or who controls a WSDL or schema document loaded by the application, can crash the PHP process and cause denial of service. Memory disclosure and code execution have not been confirmed. This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.title: CVE-2026-129538: PHP-CGI out-of-bounds read and write during PATH_INFO correction. The PHP CGI binary (php-cgi), in CGI and FastCGI mode with cgi.fix_pathinfo enabled (the default), can perform an
items.summary: PHP-CGI out-of-bounds read and write during PATH_INFO correction. The PHP CGI binary (php-cgi), in CGI and FastCGI mode with cgi.fix_pathinfo enabled (the default), can perform an out-of-bounds read and write when the path removed from SCRIPT_FILENAME or PATH_TRANSLATED is longer than the supplied PATH_INFO, or when PATH_INFO is empty. This requires a web server mapping that passes such inconsistent values, or a FastCGI listener reachable by untrusted clients. An unauthenticated remote attacker can crash the process, may obtain process memory if the application exposes PATH_INFO or PATH_TRANSLATED, and may corrupt memory. PHP-FPM and the Apache module are not affected. This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.title: CVE-2026-129699: In Eclipse Ditto versions 2.0.0 to 3.8.14 and 3.9.0 to 3.9.8, the authorization check for JSON merge patch commands on Things (HTTP `PATCH` / Ditto Protocol `merge`) does not check
items.summary: In Eclipse Ditto versions 2.0.0 to 3.8.14 and 3.9.0 to 3.9.8, the authorization check for JSON merge patch commands on Things (HTTP `PATCH` / Ditto Protocol `merge`) does not check permissions for fields deleted or set to an empty object by the patch: fields with a `null` value or an empty object value (`{}`) are skipped by the check, and Ditto's regex-based key deletion with the documented `{{ ~ ~ }}` syntax is not recognized as a deletion. An authenticated user with WRITE permission on any part of a Thing can therefore delete other attributes, features and the definition of that Thing, or overwrite or create fields as empty objects, including parts the policy revokes or never grants WRITE on. -->

items.title: CVE-2026-128064: Mixed-case HTTPS and FTPS URLs can expose data in plaintext. The HTTP and FTP stream wrappers recognise URL schemes case-insensitively, but enable TLS only when the scheme contain
items.summary: Mixed-case HTTPS and FTPS URLs can expose data in plaintext. The HTTP and FTP stream wrappers recognise URL schemes case-insensitively, but enable TLS only when the scheme contains a lowercase "s" at a fixed position. A URL such as HTTPS:// or FTPS:// passed to file_get_contents(), fopen() or other stream functions, or received as an HTTP redirect target, is therefore handled over unencrypted HTTP or FTP. An attacker able to observe the network traffic can read data the application expected TLS to protect, including credentials, request bodies and transferred files. This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.title: CVE-2026-128090: PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass via algorithm downgrade. The Phar extension selects the signature verification method from the signature type stored in the archive, and only the Ope
items.summary: PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass via algorithm downgrade. The Phar extension selects the signature verification method from the signature type stored in the archive, and only the OpenSSL types consult the separate .pubkey file holding the trusted public key. An attacker who can modify an OpenSSL-signed Phar archive, but not its public key file, can switch the signature type to a keyless hash such as SHA-256 with a recomputed digest, so the altered archive passes verification even with phar.require_hash enabled. An application that loads the archive may then execute attacker-controlled PHP code. Native, tar-based and zip-based phars are affected. This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.title: CVE-2026-129182: Use-after-free via repopulation of last_fatal_error_backtrace global after shutdown. A fatal error raised while modified INI settings are restored during request shutdown can repo
items.summary: Use-after-free via repopulation of last_fatal_error_backtrace global after shutdown. A fatal error raised while modified INI settings are restored during request shutdown can repopulate the stored fatal error backtrace after the executor has been cleaned up. The request memory is then freed, and a diagnostic emitted before executor initialization in a later request handled by the same PHP-FPM or mod_php worker can access the stale backtrace. The shutdown error requires per-path configuration of max_memory_limit, or of zlib.output_compression together with output_handler (which .user.ini can also set). The early diagnostic requires Apache per-directory configuration or, for PHP-FPM, a PHP_VALUE or PHP_ADMIN_VALUE parameter sent by the front end. This can cause memory corruption and worker crashes, and may allow remote code execution. This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.title: CVE-2026-129289: PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body. PHP does not discard the unread part of an HTTP request body at request shutdown when the application has opened php
items.summary: PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body. PHP does not discard the unread part of an HTTP request body at request shutdown when the application has opened php://input without reading it to the end. When the front end reuses backend connections, which is not the default in nginx or Apache (for example nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, or Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on), PHP-FPM can parse the leftover bytes as a new FastCGI request. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use a single crafted multipart/form-data request to forge a backend request with chosen parameters such as SCRIPT_FILENAME, REMOTE_ADDR and PHP_ADMIN_VALUE, which can lead to execution of attacker-controlled PHP code. With LSAPI, subsequent requests on the connection can be disrupted. This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.title: CVE-2026-129291: PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation. When catch_workers_output is enabled and the epoll event backend is used, the PHP-FPM master can close a worke
items.summary: PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation. When catch_workers_output is enabled and the epoll event backend is used, the PHP-FPM master can close a worker's output pipe in fpm_child_close() without removing the associated event, and the delayed cleanup can free the worker record while its epoll registration is still active. A later event is then dispatched through a pointer into freed memory. A local attacker who can execute PHP code in an FPM worker can crash the master or execute code with its privileges, commonly root. catch_workers_output is disabled by default but enabled in the official PHP-FPM Docker images. This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.20 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.7 before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.title: CVE-2026-129292: PHP-FPM status endpoint XSS via unescaped user and script fields. The PHP-FPM full status output includes the request method, authentication user and script filename of each worke
items.summary: PHP-FPM status endpoint XSS via unescaped user and script fields. The PHP-FPM full status output includes the request method, authentication user and script filename of each worker without escaping them for the HTML, XML or JSON format. When the status endpoint is enabled, an unauthenticated remote attacker can store markup in a worker's scoreboard entry with an ordinary request, for example through the username of an HTTP Basic authentication header that the web server forwards to PHP-FPM, or through the script filename where the attacker can influence it. When a user views the full status page as HTML, the injected JavaScript runs in the origin of that page. The attacker does not need access to the status endpoint. Malformed XML or JSON output can also disrupt monitoring tools. This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.title: CVE-2026-129438: Incorrect RFC 3986 URI serialization for oversized input. The Uri\Rfc3986\Uri class does not correctly handle the output-size limit and errors of the uriparser library when conver
items.summary: Incorrect RFC 3986 URI serialization for oversized input. The Uri\Rfc3986\Uri class does not correctly handle the output-size limit and errors of the uriparser library when converting a URI back to a string. For a URI whose string representation reaches approximately 2 GiB, toString(), toRawString() and other serializing operations can return a truncated or invalid string instead of an error. An application that accepts attacker-controlled URI data of that size, has enough memory to process it and trusts the result may make incorrect validation or routing decisions, and the large allocations can exhaust memory. parse_url() and Uri\WhatWg\Url are not affected. This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.summary: In Eclipse Dataspace Components (EDC) – Connector (`org.eclipse.edc:decentralized-claims-*`, `org.eclipse.edc:jwt-verifiable-credentials`, `org.eclipse.edc:ldp-verifiable-credentials`) there's a credential verification bypass in Decentralized Claims Protocol (DCP) presentation handling: a participant can present credentials appearing to be issued by any trusted issuer without holding them.

items.title: CVE-2026-126714: Partially overwritten session files can lead to remote code execution. The files session save handler, which is the default, writes updated session data into the existing session
items.summary: Partially overwritten session files can lead to remote code execution. The files session save handler, which is the default, writes updated session data into the existing session file without first clearing it. If a write is interrupted, the file can contain the beginning of the new session followed by the end of the old one, and bytes of an ordinary string can later be unserialized as objects. An attacker who can influence the session data, for example through session upload progress, and interrupt a write at a suitable point may inject objects, which can lead to code execution when the application contains a suitable gadget chain. Session data can also be corrupted. This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.title: CVE-2026-127960: Denial of service through folded HTTP response headers. The HTTP stream wrapper joins each continuation line of a folded response header to the accumulated value by allocating a n
items.summary: Denial of service through folded HTTP response headers. The HTTP stream wrapper joins each continuation line of a folded response header to the accumulated value by allocating a new string and copying the whole value, so a response with many short continuation lines takes disproportionate CPU time to parse. An attacker who controls an HTTP or HTTPS response fetched through file_get_contents(), fopen() or other stream functions, by making the application request a chosen URL or by influencing a server it already contacts, can keep PHP workers busy. Repeated or concurrent requests can cause a denial of service. This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.32 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.28 before 8.2.36, from 8.3.18 before 8.3.37, from 8.4.5 before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.title: CVE-2026-120753: In Eclipse Ditto versions 1.1.0 to 3.9.8, when pre-authentication is enabled, the gateway service accepts the pre-authenticated subject not only from the `x-ditto-pre-authenticated
items.summary: In Eclipse Ditto versions 1.1.0 to 3.9.8, when pre-authentication is enabled, the gateway service accepts the pre-authenticated subject not only from the `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` HTTP header set by a trusted reverse proxy, but also from an undocumented `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` URL query parameter that a client can set. A reverse proxy that only overwrites the header therefore does not stop clients from supplying their own subject. With the default configuration of the Ditto Helm chart (`global.jwtOnly: false`, which implicitly enables pre-authentication), the bundled nginx skips HTTP Basic authentication for any request with an `Authorization: Bearer` header and forwards it without the pre-authentication header. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send an invalid Bearer token together with the query parameter to authenticate as any chosen policy subject. Pre-authentication succeeds before the JWT is validated, so the attacker can read and modify Things and Policies with that subject's permissions. As a mitigation, disable pre-authentication in the gateway (`ENABLE_PRE_AUTHENTICATION=false`) or, when using the Helm chart, configure `global.jwtOnly: true`.

items.title: CVE-2026-115560: Session serializer mismatch can lead to remote code execution. Session upload progress, when enabled, can store attacker-controlled data in a session key using the php_binary or p
items.summary: Session serializer mismatch can lead to remote code execution. Session upload progress, when enabled, can store attacker-controlled data in a session key using the php_binary or php_serialize session serializer. If the same session is later read with the php serializer, because session.serialize_handler is changed at runtime or differs between applications sharing a session store, bytes inside the key can be passed to the unserializer. A remote attacker able to submit a multipart upload can inject objects, which may lead to code execution when the reading application contains a suitable gadget chain, or to session corruption or denial of service. This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.summary: flowintel contains a CSV injection vulnerability in its audit log CSV export functionality. Attacker-influenced text recorded in audit logs could be interpreted as spreadsheet formulas when an administrator opened the exported CSV file in a spreadsheet application. items.title: CVE-2026-133163: MISP contains an authorization bypass affecting the event protection mechanism. In MISP, a protected event is designed to be modifiable only through the events/edit endpoint with a
items.summary: MISP contains an authorization bypass affecting the event protection mechanism. In MISP, a protected event is designed to be modifiable only through the events/edit endpoint with a valid cryptographic signature. However, the protection check was enforced solely on that single route. All other write endpoints that operate on an event—attributes (add, edit, delete), objects (delete), events (populate, publish, unprotect, upload_sample, upload_analysis_file), tags (attach, detach), event reports (edit, delete), galaxy clusters (attach, detach), and cryptographic keys (add, delete)—lacked the equivalent check. As a result, an authenticated user holding the sync permission (perm_sync) who is neither a site administrator nor an internal sync user (perm_sync_internal), and who belongs to the same organization as the event's creator (orgc_id), could modify, delete, or add data to a protected event without providing a valid signature. This included the ability to unprotect the event entirely, publish it to other instances, and add cryptographic signing keys that would subsequently permit signed edits, effectively nullifying the protection mechanism. items.title: CVE-2026-133165: MISP contains an authorization and scope flaw in the ObjectReference model's captureReference method. When a user saves an event (via REST API, sync, or feeds), any object referenc
items.summary: MISP contains an authorization and scope flaw in the ObjectReference model's captureReference method. When a user saves an event (via REST API, sync, or feeds), any object reference included in the payload is looked up by its UUID across the entire MISP instance rather than being scoped to the event being saved. An authenticated user with permission to add or edit events can therefore include the UUID of an object reference belonging to a different event—including events in other organizations that the user cannot view—and cause the system to overwrite that foreign reference's relationship_type, comment, deleted flag, and timestamp with attacker-supplied values. The affected reference is neither deleted nor recreated in the attacker's event; its fields are silently rewritten in place. This constitutes a cross-tenant integrity violation: data integrity of object references in events the attacker has no read or write access to is compromised. items.title: CVE-2026-110337: The Strava datasource plugin's resource handler POST /strava-api forwards a client-supplied endpoint string, and its query parameters, to the Strava API (https://www.strava.com/api
items.summary: The Strava datasource plugin's resource handler POST /strava-api forwards a client-supplied endpoint string, and its query parameters, to the Strava API (https://www.strava.com/api/v3/ ) without validation. When the datasource is not in OAuth pass-through mode, the request is made with the access token stored on the datasource, not the caller's identity. Grafana authorises plugin resource calls only on the datasources:query permission, which Viewers have by default. Any such caller could therefore request any Strava API path the connected account's OAuth grant allows, for example athlete/clubs or routes/{id}, and read the response. The plugin's frontend (stravaApi.ts) only needs a fixed set of paths: athlete, athlete/activities, activities/{id}, activities/{id}/streams and segments/{id}. Requests to Strava are GET only, so the issue is read-only. Affected: plugin versions 1.2.0 through 1.7.2. The fix restricts endpoint to those five patterns and is pending release. The check runs before the access token is resolved, so a rejected request never causes a token refresh or any call to Strava. Paths with .. segments are rejected as well.

items.title: CVE-2026-22311: The failed-login limiter of the JTL-Wawi synchronisation interface of JTL-Shop derives the client identity from the client-controlled X-Forwarded-For header and counts requests wit
items.summary: The failed-login limiter of the JTL-Wawi synchronisation interface of JTL-Shop derives the client identity from the client-controlled X-Forwarded-For header and counts requests without credentials as failed logins. An unauthenticated remote attacker can block the synchronisation between JTL-Shop and JTL-Wawi with a few requests and repeat this indefinitely, so that orders are no longer handed over to JTL-Wawi. No data is disclosed and no code is executed.

items.title: CVE-2026-85413: The Foxtool All-in-One: Contact chat button, Custom login, Media optimize images plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'foxtool_image_id' parame
items.summary: The Foxtool All-in-One: Contact chat button, Custom login, Media optimize images plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'foxtool_image_id' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.5.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. A subscriber-level attacker can store a payload in their own profile's foxtoolpic user-meta that executes in an administrator's browser session when the administrator views the user via the Users → Edit screen.

items.title: CVE-2026-123972: The WP-Slimbox2 Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.3.1 due to insufficie
items.summary: The WP-Slimbox2 Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.3.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires a logged-in user, typically an administrator, to click the attacker's image link in the comment; however, because unmoderated comments appear in the WordPress moderation queue where administrators routinely interact with them, the moderation gate does not meaningfully prevent exploitation. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete Administrator role.

items.title: CVE-2026-125060: The checkout of JTL-Shop stores the delivery address ID submitted by the customer in the session and adopts it into the order without verifying that the address belongs to the orde
items.summary: The checkout of JTL-Shop stores the delivery address ID submitted by the customer in the session and adopts it into the order without verifying that the address belongs to the ordering customer. A remote attacker with access to the checkout, including a guest, can thereby attach the delivery address of another customer to their own order. Name and address of the other customer, and depending on the shop configuration further contact data, then appear in the order confirmation and customer account. As the IDs are sequential, addresses can be enumerated. Goods may also be shipped to the wrong address.

items.title: CVE-2026-125061: The administration page "Offene Bestellungen" (open orders) of the JTL PayPal Checkout plugin for JTL-Shop outputs the customer name of pending orders without output encoding. A re
items.summary: The administration page "Offene Bestellungen" (open orders) of the JTL PayPal Checkout plugin for JTL-Shop outputs the customer name of pending orders without output encoding. A registered customer (free self-registration) can submit an HTML-entity-encoded name, which is decoded to markup when the billing address of an order is written. If the PayPal payment is left unfinished, the order is listed on the page and the name is rendered as markup in the browser of an administrator who opens the page. The script code runs with the privileges of that administrator and can, for example, create a new administrator account. Guest orders are not affected, because the name is encoded again.

items.title: CVE-2026-132128: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions up to and including 9.3.6, middie does not honor the router'
items.summary: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions up to and including 9.3.6, middie does not honor the router's caseSensitive setting and matches path-scoped middleware mount paths with a case-insensitive regular expression that does not fold non-ASCII characters, while Fastify's router, when caseSensitive is set to false, lowercases the request path with a Unicode-aware conversion that maps the KELVIN SIGN character (U+212A) to the ASCII letter k. A request that spells a k in a protected mount path as the percent-encoded KELVIN SIGN is therefore routed to the protected handler while the middleware mounted on that path, such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting, never matches and is skipped, letting an unauthenticated client reach the handler. Only applications that set caseSensitive to false and protect a mount path containing the letter k are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.7, and users should upgrade to 9.3.7 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, or keep routing case-sensitive, which is the default.

items.summary: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. items.summary: The web installer of JTL-Shop executes its state-changing installation tasks without checking whether the shop is already installed, and was not removed or locked after the installation. items.title: CVE-2026-123968: The Slimbox plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment (anchor title within comment HTML)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1
items.summary: The Slimbox plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment (anchor title within comment HTML)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.0.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. WordPress core comment KSES permits unauthenticated commenters to post anchor elements with href and title attributes, so an entity-encoded payload stored in the title attribute survives sanitization verbatim; the browser then decodes the entities when populating the DOM .title property, and the Slimbox library's jQuery .html() caption sink renders it as executable HTML.

items.title: CVE-2026-123969: The Fancy Lightbox plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.0.0 due to insufficient inp
items.summary: The Fancy Lightbox plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.0.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation without administrator interaction requires that the attacker first have one comment approved so that a subsequent payload comment is auto-published; the injected script only executes when a user clicks the malicious image link inside the comment. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

items.title: CVE-2026-123971: The Slimbox Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'el.title (HTML-decoded title attribute of a stored element
items.summary: The Slimbox Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'el.title (HTML-decoded title attribute of a stored element)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires a companion plugin such as bbPress that permits low-privileged users to store anchor elements with arbitrary title and rel attributes, as WordPress core comment handling does not preserve rel on anchor tags by default.

items.title: CVE-2026-133001: FlowIntel contains an authorization flaw in its duplicate alert ingestion logic. When a duplicate alert is received and its content is updated, the ownership and visibility scope f
items.summary: FlowIntel contains an authorization flaw in its duplicate alert ingestion logic. When a duplicate alert is received and its content is updated, the ownership and visibility scope fields (owner user and owner organization) were not refreshed to reflect the connector's current scope. As a result, an alert that was originally created under a broader visibility scope retained that broader scope even after the connector's scope was narrowed or changed. This means that users or organizations that should no longer have visibility into a given alert could continue to access it, because the stale ownership fields were never updated during the duplicate-update path. The issue affected all duplicate updates, including those involving alerts in terminal review states and those recovered from uniqueness conflicts. Security impact: - Unauthorized disclosure of security alert content to users or organizations outside the intended visibility scope. - Stale access persists indefinitely until the alert is independently re-scoped or deleted. Affected version: <4.1.0.

items.title: CVE-2026-120404: The built-in regular expression name finder for latitude and longitude coordinates uses a pattern that is vulnerable to excessive backtracking. An attacker who can supply text that
items.summary: The built-in regular expression name finder for latitude and longitude coordinates uses a pattern that is vulnerable to excessive backtracking. An attacker who can supply text that an application analyzes with this name finder can cause high CPU consumption, leading to denial of service. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.5.13 or 3.0.0, which fix the issue.

items.title: CVE-2026-112216: Vulnerability involving the exposure of sensitive information in the URLs of the UOC Virtual Campus’s document upload feature. After completing a document upload, the application i
items.summary: Vulnerability involving the exposure of sensitive information in the URLs of the UOC Virtual Campus’s document upload feature. After completing a document upload, the application includes identifiers related to the active session—such as `apjsessionid`—and other internal parameters associated with requests and users in the HTTP GET request parameters. This data may be stored in the browser history and in server or proxy logs, or transmitted via the HTTP Referer header, depending on the configuration and browsing flow. Its inclusion in the URL could allow for the unauthorized disclosure of information to third parties with access to those logs or recipients.

items.title: CVE-2026-85776: The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Missing Authorization in versions up to, and including, 1.1.11. This is due to a missing capabil
items.summary: The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Missing Authorization in versions up to, and including, 1.1.11. This is due to a missing capability check and missing nonce check on the start_zip_creation, start_zip_download, local_sync_get_init_root_files, and local_sync_get_files_by_key AJAX actions in the start_zip_creation_dev() and sibling functions. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to overwrite the plugin's prod_site_url setting so it points at an attacker-controlled host and enumerate arbitrary server directories, which when combined with a subsequent administrator-triggered sync results in an unsigned attacker-supplied ZIP archive being fetched, extracted via a WordPress-independent bridge deployed under the web root, resulting in remote code execution on the affected site.

items.title: CVE-2026-92613: In Eclipse iceoryx-rs, versions 0.0.11 to 0.0.13 and 0.1.0 as well as on the latest main branch. `SampleReceiver:: ::take()` and `Sample:: ::deref()` are safe functions that
items.summary: In Eclipse iceoryx-rs, versions 0.0.11 to 0.0.13 and 0.1.0 as well as on the latest main branch. `SampleReceiver:: ::take()` and `Sample:: ::deref()` are safe functions that hand the caller a `&T` pointing at a chunk written by another iceoryx process, but the subscriber path neither requires `T: ShmSend` nor verifies that the received chunk is at least `size_of:: ()` bytes / `align_of:: ()`-aligned. A peer process that publishes an undersized chunk, or any chunk at all when the subscriber chose a pointer-bearing `T`, drives a `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` subscriber into out-of-bounds reads of adjacent shared-memory chunks or dereference of a publisher-controlled pointer. Resolution: It will not be fixed since this is a known limitation in iceoryx as it is the users responsibility to specify the same data type on sender and receiver side. [iceoryx2](https://github.com/eclipse-iceoryx/iceoryx2) is the successor of iceoryx-rs where the API is designed to prevent this by default. It is strongly recommended to migrate to iceoryx2 which is actively maintained and receives security support. The iceoryx-rs package has officially reached End-of-life and will not receive any features, bugfixes

items.title: CVE-2026-126631: A flaw was found in OpenSCAP. This vulnerability allows for information disclosure when performing offline scans of untrusted filesystem images, such as container images or virtual
items.summary: A flaw was found in OpenSCAP. This vulnerability allows for information disclosure when performing offline scans of untrusted filesystem images, such as container images or virtual machine (VM) disks. Because the scanner does not properly restrict symbolic link (symlink) resolution to the target image's root directory, an attacker can supply a crafted image containing links pointing to files on the host system. When the scan runs, typically with elevated privileges, OpenSCAP follows these links to read sensitive host files and expose their contents in the scan report or manipulate compliance results.

items.title: CVE-2026-14491: The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.11 via the 'file_name' parameter.
items.summary: The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.11 via the 'file_name' parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information. The authentication bypass requires submitting the JSON boolean `true` as the `prod_key_random_id` value, which coerces against any non-empty stored secret so that the loose `!=` comparison evaluates to false, skipping the rejection branch entirely without knowledge of the secret.

items.title: CVE-2026-14492: The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.11 via the save_single_batch_fil
items.summary: The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.11 via the save_single_batch_file function. This is due to a PHP type-juggling authentication bypass via loose != comparison with no is_string() guard, combined with unsanitized base64-decoded path construction in save_single_batch_file() lacking any directory traversal containment. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with custom-level access and above, to execute code on the server. Exploitation requires that the site owner has completed the plugin's initial setup so that the site_type and prod_key_random_id options are non-empty, though any non-empty secret value is bypassable via the type-juggling flaw.

items.title: CVE-2026-99320: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ipv6: raw: fix use-after-free in rawv6_send_hdrinc() rawv6_send_hdrinc() caches the route before handing the s
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ipv6: raw: fix use-after-free in rawv6_send_hdrinc() rawv6_send_hdrinc() caches the route before handing the skb to l3mdev_ip6_out(). The VRF output path may replace skb->dst and release the original route, leaving the cached pointer stale. The function later dereferences that pointer for statistics accounting and as the output device passed to NF_HOOK(). Its RCU read-side critical section starts after l3mdev_ip6_out(), so it cannot prevent the old route from being reclaimed in between. Reload the route from the current skb destination after l3mdev_ip6_out() returns. KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free in rawv6_sendmsg(), with the route allocated by ip6_dst_alloc(), freed by dst_destroy() from rcu_core(), and the related RCU callback queued from vrf_l3_out().

items.title: CVE-2026-132043: In Eclipse Yasson versions 3.0 to 3.0.5, a race condition (CWE-362) exists in the handling of @JsonbNumberFormat. Yasson creates one java.text.NumberFormat instance per annotated p
items.summary: In Eclipse Yasson versions 3.0 to 3.0.5, a race condition (CWE-362) exists in the handling of @JsonbNumberFormat. Yasson creates one java.text.NumberFormat instance per annotated property and shares it across all threads that use the same Jsonb instance. NumberFormat is not thread-safe, and the deserializer called parse() on it without synchronization. When multiple threads deserialize concurrently, a thread can receive a numeric value that belongs to another thread's input, receive an incorrect value, or fail with an exception. A remote attacker who can send concurrent requests to an application that deserializes untrusted JSON this way may cause incorrect data to be processed or cause another user's value to be returned. Exploitation requires that the application use @JsonbNumberFormat with a shared Jsonb instance and that the attacker win a timing race. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.6 by synchronizing access to the shared NumberFormat instances.

items.title: CVE-2026-117678: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity vulnerability in benoitc idna allows an attacker who controls a hostname passed to the library to exhaust CPU via an over-long xn-- label. idna:u
items.summary: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity vulnerability in benoitc idna allows an attacker who controls a hostname passed to the library to exhaust CPU via an over-long xn-- label. idna:ulabel/1 in src/idna.erl hands every ASCII label that starts with xn-- to punycode:decode/1 without applying check_label_length/1, the 63-octet DNS label limit. punycode:decode/1 in src/punycode.erl builds its output with list appends in insert/4, so its cost grows super-linearly with the label length. A label of a few kilobytes keeps a scheduler busy for seconds to minutes before the label is rejected as invalid punycode. Every decode entry point reaches this path: decode/1, decode/2, to_unicode/1 and from_ascii/1. The encode path reaches it as well, because alabel/1 calls ulabel/1 on an ASCII xn-- label before its own length check, so encode/1, encode/2 and to_ascii/1 are affected for such input. This issue affects idna: from 0.5.0 before 8.0.0.

items.title: CVE-2026-109555: The WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 and 6.17.0, respectively, via deserializ
items.summary: The WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 and 6.17.0, respectively, via deserialization of untrusted input during database restore and staging reset. This is due to the database importer treating attacker-controlled text beginning with {WPSTG_BINARY} as trusted internal binary data and decoding its hexadecimal suffix into serialized bytes. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to plant a malicious serialized object in their own profile. When an Administrator later performs an ordinary database-including restore or staging reset containing that value, and the restored profile metadata is loaded, either during the restore or in a later request, a built-in POP chain can be used to execute arbitrary code on the server. Additional built-in gadget chains allow arbitrary local file read in both WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro and arbitrary file deletion in WP STAGING Pro. The attacker does not require Administrator credentials or a copy of a backup, but exploitation does require the later privileged restore or reset.

items.title: CVE-2026-104357: A flaw was found in libtirpc. The SunRPC UDP/datagram server transport reuses a single receive buffer across requests and resets the XDR decode position without rebinding the decod
items.summary: A flaw was found in libtirpc. The SunRPC UDP/datagram server transport reuses a single receive buffer across requests and resets the XDR decode position without rebinding the decode length to the size of the datagram actually received. As a result, when a short UDP RPC request is received after a longer one, the XDR decoder can read stale bytes left in the reused buffer and interpret them as part of the current request, including credential, verifier, or procedure-argument fields. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to data confidentiality and integrity for services that use a UDP-based SunRPC server.
